#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                       \
  do {                                                                         \
    cudaError_t e = (call);                                                    \
    if (e != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \
      fprintf(stderr, "CUDA error %s at %s:%d\n", cudaGetErrorString(e),       \
              __FILE__, __LINE__);                                             \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

#define CHECK_CUBLAS(call)                                                     \
  do {                                                                         \
    cublasStatus_t e = (call);                                                 \
    if (e != CUBLAS_STATUS_SUCCESS) {                                          \
      fprintf(stderr, "cuBLAS error %d at %s:%d\n", (int)e, __FILE__,          \
              __LINE__);                                                       \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

// ─── data init
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static void fill_rand_bf16(std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &v, unsigned seed) {
  srand(seed);
  for (auto &x : v)
    x = __float2bfloat16((float(rand()) / RAND_MAX) * 2.f - 1.f);
}

// ─── accuracy check
// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static double max_rel_err(const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &ref,
                          const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &out) {
  double max_e = 0.0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < ref.size(); ++i) {
    double r = __bfloat162float(ref[i]);
    double o = __bfloat162float(out[i]);
    double e = std::abs(r - o) / std::max(1e-5, std::abs(r));
    max_e = std::max(max_e, e);
  }
  return max_e;
}

// ─── benchmark harness
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Result {
  double blublas_tflops;
  double cublas_tflops;
  double rel_err;
  bool pass;
};

// Generic runner for any Config and Layout
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false>
static Result run_test_case(int M, int N, int K, int batchCount, float alpha,
                            float beta, cublasHandle_t cublas,
                            cudaStream_t stream) {
  // Determine dimensions based on layout
  long long elA = 0;
  long long elB = 0;
  const long long elC = (long long)batchCount * M * N;

  if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * N * K;
  } else { // TN
    elA = (long long)batchCount * K * M;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  }

  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hA(elA), hB(elB), hC_init(elC);
  fill_rand_bf16(hA, 42);
  fill_rand_bf16(hB, 99);

  // For beta != 0, initialize C with random values
  if (beta != 0.0f) {
    fill_rand_bf16(hC_init, 77);
  } else {
    std::fill(hC_init.begin(), hC_init.end(), __float2bfloat16(0.f));
  }

  __nv_bfloat16 *dA, *dB, *dC_ref, *dC_blu;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA, elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dA, hA.data(), elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, hB.data(), elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_ref, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_blu, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));

  // ── cuBLAS reference ────────
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
        cublas, transB, transA, // Swap due to column-major vs row-major
        N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb, strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF,
        (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF, N, (long long)M * N,
        batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  }

  // Run exactly one iteration of BluBridge for accuracy checking
  launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave>(
      dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Accuracy Check
  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hC_ref_h(elC), hC_blu_h(elC);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_ref_h.data(), dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_blu_h.data(), dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));

  double rel_err = max_rel_err(hC_ref_h, hC_blu_h);
  if (rel_err >= 0.05) {
    printf("  [DEBUG FAIL] First 10 elements:\n");
    printf("    Ref (cuBLAS): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_ref_h[i]));
    printf("\n    Blu (Template): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_blu_h[i]));
    printf("\n");
  }

  // Warmup BluBridge Cluster Template (5 iters)
  for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave>(
        dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Timed BluBridge Cluster Template (20 iters)
  cudaEvent_t t0, t1;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave>(
        dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());
  float blu_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&blu_ms, t0, t1));

  // Warmup + timed cuBLAS (20 iters)
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  }
  float cub_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&cub_ms, t0, t1));

  double flops = 2.0 * (double)M * N * K * batchCount;
  double iters = 20.0;
  double blu_tfl = flops * iters / (blu_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;
  double cub_tfl = flops * iters / (cub_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_ref));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_blu));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t1));

  return {blu_tfl, cub_tfl, rel_err, rel_err < 0.05};
}

// Struct to define dynamic test shape
struct Shape {
  int M, N, K, batch;
  float alpha, beta;
  const char *label;
};

// Layout name helper
static const char *layout_name(Sm103Layout layout) {
  switch (layout) {
  case Sm103Layout::NN:
    return "NN";
  case Sm103Layout::NT:
    return "NT";
  case Sm103Layout::TN:
    return "TN";
  }
  return "Unknown";
}

template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false>
static bool run_test_suite_for_layout_config(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                                             cublasHandle_t cublas,
                                             cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Testing Layout: %s | Config: %dx%dx%d (cta_group::2, %s wave) "
         "===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN, Config::BK,
         VerticalWave ? "vertical" : "horizontal");
  printf("%-18s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s  %-9s  %-9s  %-10s  %s\n", "Shape", "M",
         "N", "K", "Batch", "alpha", "beta", "Template", "cuBLAS", "MaxRelErr",
         "Status");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(98, '-').c_str());

  int passed = 0;
  int total = 0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    // 256x256x64 config requires M & N to be multiples of 256
    if (Config::BM == 256 && (s.M % 512 != 0 || s.N % 256 != 0)) {
      // Skip shapes that are not compatible with 256x256 config
      // Note: cluster height is 2*BM = 512, cluster width is BN = 256
      continue;
    }

    total++;
    Result r = run_test_case<Config, Layout, VerticalWave>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch, s.alpha, s.beta, cublas, stream);

    printf("%-18s %5d %5d %5d %5d %5.1f %5.1f  %8.2f T  %8.2f T  %9.2e  %s\n",
           s.label, s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch, s.alpha, s.beta, r.blublas_tflops,
           r.cublas_tflops, r.rel_err, r.pass ? "PASS" : "FAIL");

    if (r.pass)
      ++passed;
  }
  printf("Result: %d / %d PASSED\n", passed, total);
  return passed == total;
}

// ─── Qwen 42-shape sweep — P1 impact + dispatcher routing data
// ──────────────── For each real Qwen matmul shape (M=4096), run the 128×256
// tile in BOTH horizontal and vertical wave and compare to cuBLAS. Tells us,
// per shape, whether vertical helps (→ dispatcher routes it to vertical) and
// how close we are to cuBLAS. Correctness is validated by the suites above;
// here we focus on throughput, but still flag any accuracy miss.
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout>
static void run_qwen_sweep(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                           cublasHandle_t cublas, cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Qwen 42-shape sweep (%s, 128x256 tile): horizontal vs vertical "
         "vs cuBLAS ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout));
  printf("%-20s %7s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s  %-5s  %s\n", "Shape", "N",
         "K", "horiz", "h%", "vert", "v%", "cuBLAS", "best", "ok");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  int vwins = 0, total = 0;
  double h_sum = 0, v_sum = 0, c_sum = 0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    Result h = run_test_case<Config, Layout, false>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f,
                                                    0.0f, cublas, stream);
    Result v = run_test_case<Config, Layout, true>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f,
                                                   cublas, stream);
    bool vbest = v.blublas_tflops >= h.blublas_tflops;
    if (vbest)
      ++vwins;
    ++total;
    h_sum += h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops;
    v_sum += v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops;
    c_sum += std::max(h.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops) / v.cublas_tflops;
    printf(
        "%-20s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-5s  %s\n",
        s.label, s.N, s.K, h.blublas_tflops,
        h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops * 100, v.blublas_tflops,
        v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops * 100, v.cublas_tflops,
        vbest ? "vert" : "horiz", (h.pass && v.pass) ? "ok" : "FAIL");
  }
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  printf("vertical wins: %d / %d   avg%% of cuBLAS: horiz %.1f%%, vert %.1f%%, "
         "best-of-2 %.1f%%\n",
         vwins, total, h_sum / total * 100, v_sum / total * 100,
         c_sum / total * 100);
}

int main() {
  int dev = 0;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDevice(&dev));
  cudaDeviceProp prop;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, dev));

  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");
  printf("SM103 Cluster GEMM Unified Template Test Suite\n");
  printf("Device : %s  (SM %d.%d)\n", prop.name, prop.major, prop.minor);
  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");

  if (prop.major != 10 || prop.minor != 3) {
    printf("[SKIP] SM103 Cluster GEMM template requires SM 10.3 (Blackwell "
           "Ultra/sm_103a).\n"
           "       This device is SM %d.%d (%s).\n"
           "       Tests skipped.\n",
           prop.major, prop.minor, prop.name);
    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
  }

  cudaStream_t stream;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamCreate(&stream));

  cublasHandle_t cublas;
  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasCreate(&cublas));
  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasSetStream(cublas, stream));

  // Test cases for 128x128x64 configuration (requires M % 256 == 0, N % 128 ==
  // 0, K % 64 == 0) Note: for BM=128, cluster height is 2*BM = 256. So M must
  // be a multiple of 256.
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_128 = {
      // M, N, K, batch, alpha, beta, label
      {256, 128, 64, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "tiny"},
      {256, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "small"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "medium"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "large"},
      // Multi-batch test
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-4"},
      {256, 256, 128, 8, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-8"},
      // Alpha/Beta scaling and accumulation tests
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.0f, "alpha-scaling"},
      {256, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.5f, "beta-accumulate"},
      {512, 512, 128, 2, 1.2f, 0.8f, "alpha-beta-batch"},
      // ── Comparison shapes vs legacy _cluster.cu B0 results (M=4096) ──
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-wideN-gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-skinny-K"}};

  // Test cases for 256x256x64 configuration (requires M % 512 == 0, N % 256 ==
  // 0, K % 64 == 0)
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_256 = {
      {512, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "tiny-256"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "small-256"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "medium-256"},
      // Multi-batch test
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-4-256"},
      // Alpha/Beta scaling and accumulation tests
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.5f, "alpha-beta-256"},
      // ── Comparison shapes vs legacy _cluster.cu B0 results (M=4096) ──
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-wideN-gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-skinny-K"}};

  bool all_passed = true;

  // 1. NN Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::NN>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NN>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 2. NT Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::NT>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NT>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 3. TN Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::TN>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::TN>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 4. P1 variant: 128×256 tile + VERTICAL wave (cuBLAS `128x256_2x1_v`).
  // Same tile/cluster as the 256 suites above, VerticalWave=true. Compare the
  // TFLOPS here vs the horizontal 256 suites on the same shapes to isolate the
  // wave-order effect (expected to help the M=4096 wide-N shapes via L2 reuse).
  printf("\n########## P1: 128x256 tile, VERTICAL wave (2x1) ##########\n");
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NN,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NT,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::TN,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // ── Full Qwen matmul-shape sweep (42 shapes, M=4096) ──
  // (N, K) from analyzations.md §16.3. Runs 128×256 horizontal vs vertical vs
  // cuBLAS to measure P1 impact per shape + collect dispatcher routing data.
  const std::vector<Shape> qwen_shapes = {
      {4096, 896, 896, 1, 1, 0, "q25-0.5b-Q"},
      {4096, 128, 896, 1, 1, 0, "q25-0.5b-K"},

      {4096, 151936, 1536, 1, 1, 0, "q25-1.5b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 2048, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-Q"},
      {4096, 256, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-K"},
      {4096, 11008, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-Gate"},
      {4096, 2048, 11008, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 3584, 3584, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-Q"},
      {4096, 512, 3584, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-K"},
      {4096, 18944, 3584, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-Gate"},
      {4096, 3584, 18944, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-Down"},
      {4096, 152064, 3584, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 2048, 1024, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-Q"},
      {4096, 1024, 1024, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-K"},
      {4096, 1024, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-O"},
      {4096, 3072, 1024, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-Gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 3072, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 1024, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 2048, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-1.7b-Q"},
      {4096, 1024, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-1.7b-K"},
      {4096, 6144, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-1.7b-Gate"},

      {4096, 1024, 2560, 1, 1, 0, "q3-4b-K"},
      {4096, 2560, 4096, 1, 1, 0, "q3-4b-O"},
      {4096, 9728, 2560, 1, 1, 0, "q3-4b-Gate"},
      {4096, 2560, 9728, 1, 1, 0, "q3-4b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 2560, 1, 1, 0, "q3-4b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1, 0, "q3-8b-Q"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1, 0, "q3-8b-K"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1, 0, "q3-8b-Gate"},
      {4096, 4096, 12288, 1, 1, 0, "q3-8b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 4096, 1, 1, 0, "q3-8b-LMhead"}};

  printf("\n########## Qwen 42-shape sweep (P1 impact) ##########\n");
  run_qwen_sweep<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::TN>(qwen_shapes, cublas,
                                                          stream);

  printf("\n==================================================================="
         "======\n");
  if (all_passed) {
    printf("ALL TESTS PASSED SUCCESSFULLY!\n");
  } else {
    printf("SOME TESTS FAILED!\n");
  }
  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");

  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasDestroy(cublas));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamDestroy(stream));

  return all_passed ? EXIT_SUCCESS : EXIT_FAILURE;
}

### BLOCK 1 — paste immediately **before** `int main() {`

```cpp
// Qwen 42-shape sweep — horizontal vs vertical vs cuBLAS (P1 impact + routing).
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout>
static void run_qwen_sweep(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                           cublasHandle_t cublas, cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Qwen 42-shape sweep (%s, 128x256 tile): horizontal vs vertical "
         "vs cuBLAS ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout));
  printf("%-20s %7s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s  %-5s  %s\n", "Shape", "N",
         "K", "horiz", "h%", "vert", "v%", "cuBLAS", "best", "ok");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  int vwins = 0, total = 0;
  double h_sum = 0, v_sum = 0, c_sum = 0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    Result h = run_test_case<Config, Layout, false>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f,
                                                    0.0f, cublas, stream);
    Result v = run_test_case<Config, Layout, true>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f,
                                                   cublas, stream);
    bool vbest = v.blublas_tflops >= h.blublas_tflops;
    if (vbest) ++vwins;
    ++total;
    h_sum += h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops;
    v_sum += v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops;
    c_sum += std::max(h.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops) / v.cublas_tflops;
    printf("%-20s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-5s  %s\n",
           s.label, s.N, s.K, h.blublas_tflops,
           h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops * 100, v.blublas_tflops,
           v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops * 100, v.cublas_tflops,
           vbest ? "vert" : "horiz", (h.pass && v.pass) ? "ok" : "FAIL");
  }
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  printf("vertical wins: %d / %d   avg%% of cuBLAS: horiz %.1f%%, vert %.1f%%, "
         "best-of-2 %.1f%%\n",
         vwins, total, h_sum / total * 100, v_sum / total * 100,
         c_sum / total * 100);
}
```

Vertical wins **28/42**, and the 14 where horizontal wins are near-ties (within ~1%). `best-of-2` (88.6%) barely beats vert-only (88.5%) → **defaulting the 128×256 tile to vertical loses almost nothing and wins big on wide-N.** Simple, robust rule.

// test_bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cu
// Comprehensive accuracy and benchmark test suite for the unified SM103a
// Cluster GEMM template. Target: NVIDIA B300 (SM 10.3a) —
// tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16
//
// Usage:
//   make run TEST=examples/test_bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cu
//

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cublas_v2.h>
#include <cuda_bf16.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <numeric>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

// Include the unified SM103 cluster template
#include "../src/level3/batched_gemm/BF16/SM103/Bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cuh"

// ─── error helpers
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                       \
  do {                                                                         \
    cudaError_t e = (call);                                                    \
    if (e != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \
      fprintf(stderr, "CUDA error %s at %s:%d\n", cudaGetErrorString(e),       \
              __FILE__, __LINE__);                                             \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

#define CHECK_CUBLAS(call)                                                     \
  do {                                                                         \
    cublasStatus_t e = (call);                                                 \
    if (e != CUBLAS_STATUS_SUCCESS) {                                          \
      fprintf(stderr, "cuBLAS error %d at %s:%d\n", (int)e, __FILE__,          \
              __LINE__);                                                       \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

// ─── data init
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static void fill_rand_bf16(std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &v, unsigned seed) {
  srand(seed);
  for (auto &x : v)
    x = __float2bfloat16((float(rand()) / RAND_MAX) * 2.f - 1.f);
}

// ─── accuracy check
// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static double max_rel_err(const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &ref,
                          const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &out) {
  double max_e = 0.0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < ref.size(); ++i) {
    double r = __bfloat162float(ref[i]);
    double o = __bfloat162float(out[i]);
    double e = std::abs(r - o) / std::max(1e-5, std::abs(r));
    max_e = std::max(max_e, e);
  }
  return max_e;
}

// ─── benchmark harness
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Result {
  double blublas_tflops;
  double cublas_tflops;
  double rel_err;
  bool pass;
};

// Generic runner for any Config and Layout
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false>
static Result run_test_case(int M, int N, int K, int batchCount, float alpha,
                            float beta, cublasHandle_t cublas,
                            cudaStream_t stream) {
  // Determine dimensions based on layout
  long long elA = 0;
  long long elB = 0;
  const long long elC = (long long)batchCount * M * N;

  if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * N * K;
  } else { // TN
    elA = (long long)batchCount * K * M;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  }

  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hA(elA), hB(elB), hC_init(elC);
  fill_rand_bf16(hA, 42);
  fill_rand_bf16(hB, 99);

  // For beta != 0, initialize C with random values
  if (beta != 0.0f) {
    fill_rand_bf16(hC_init, 77);
  } else {
    std::fill(hC_init.begin(), hC_init.end(), __float2bfloat16(0.f));
  }

  __nv_bfloat16 *dA, *dB, *dC_ref, *dC_blu;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA, elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dA, hA.data(), elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, hB.data(), elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_ref, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_blu, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));

  // ── cuBLAS reference ────────
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
        cublas, transB, transA, // Swap due to column-major vs row-major
        N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb, strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF,
        (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF, N, (long long)M * N,
        batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  }

  // Run exactly one iteration of BluBridge for accuracy checking
  launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave>(
      dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Accuracy Check
  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hC_ref_h(elC), hC_blu_h(elC);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_ref_h.data(), dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_blu_h.data(), dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));

  double rel_err = max_rel_err(hC_ref_h, hC_blu_h);
  if (rel_err >= 0.05) {
    printf("  [DEBUG FAIL] First 10 elements:\n");
    printf("    Ref (cuBLAS): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_ref_h[i]));
    printf("\n    Blu (Template): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_blu_h[i]));
    printf("\n");
  }

  // Warmup BluBridge Cluster Template (5 iters)
  for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave>(
        dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Timed BluBridge Cluster Template (20 iters)
  cudaEvent_t t0, t1;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave>(
        dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());
  float blu_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&blu_ms, t0, t1));

  // Warmup + timed cuBLAS (20 iters)
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  }
  float cub_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&cub_ms, t0, t1));

  double flops = 2.0 * (double)M * N * K * batchCount;
  double iters = 20.0;
  double blu_tfl = flops * iters / (blu_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;
  double cub_tfl = flops * iters / (cub_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_ref));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_blu));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t1));

  return {blu_tfl, cub_tfl, rel_err, rel_err < 0.05};
}

// Struct to define dynamic test shape
struct Shape {
  int M, N, K, batch;
  float alpha, beta;
  const char *label;
};

// Layout name helper
static const char *layout_name(Sm103Layout layout) {
  switch (layout) {
  case Sm103Layout::NN:
    return "NN";
  case Sm103Layout::NT:
    return "NT";
  case Sm103Layout::TN:
    return "TN";
  }
  return "Unknown";
}

template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false>
static bool run_test_suite_for_layout_config(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                                             cublasHandle_t cublas,
                                             cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Testing Layout: %s | Config: %dx%dx%d (cta_group::2, %s wave) "
         "===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN, Config::BK,
         VerticalWave ? "vertical" : "horizontal");
  printf("%-18s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s  %-9s  %-9s  %-10s  %s\n", "Shape", "M",
         "N", "K", "Batch", "alpha", "beta", "Template", "cuBLAS", "MaxRelErr",
         "Status");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(98, '-').c_str());

  int passed = 0;
  int total = 0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    // 256x256x64 config requires M & N to be multiples of 256
    if (Config::BM == 256 && (s.M % 512 != 0 || s.N % 256 != 0)) {
      // Skip shapes that are not compatible with 256x256 config
      // Note: cluster height is 2*BM = 512, cluster width is BN = 256
      continue;
    }

    total++;
    Result r = run_test_case<Config, Layout, VerticalWave>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch, s.alpha, s.beta, cublas, stream);

    printf("%-18s %5d %5d %5d %5d %5.1f %5.1f  %8.2f T  %8.2f T  %9.2e  %s\n",
           s.label, s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch, s.alpha, s.beta, r.blublas_tflops,
           r.cublas_tflops, r.rel_err, r.pass ? "PASS" : "FAIL");

    if (r.pass)
      ++passed;
  }
  printf("Result: %d / %d PASSED\n", passed, total);
  return passed == total;
}

// ─── Qwen 42-shape sweep — P1 impact + dispatcher routing data
// ──────────────── For each real Qwen matmul shape (M=4096), run the 128×256
// tile in BOTH horizontal and vertical wave and compare to cuBLAS. Tells us,
// per shape, whether vertical helps (→ dispatcher routes it to vertical) and
// how close we are to cuBLAS. Correctness is validated by the suites above;
// here we focus on throughput, but still flag any accuracy miss.
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout>
static void run_qwen_sweep(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                           cublasHandle_t cublas, cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Qwen 42-shape sweep (%s, %dx%d tile): horizontal vs vertical "
         "vs cuBLAS ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN);
  printf("%-20s %7s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s  %-5s  %s\n", "Shape", "N",
         "K", "horiz", "h%", "vert", "v%", "cuBLAS", "best", "ok");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  int vwins = 0, total = 0;
  double h_sum = 0, v_sum = 0, c_sum = 0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    Result h = run_test_case<Config, Layout, false>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f,
                                                    0.0f, cublas, stream);
    Result v = run_test_case<Config, Layout, true>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f,
                                                   cublas, stream);
    bool vbest = v.blublas_tflops >= h.blublas_tflops;
    if (vbest)
      ++vwins;
    ++total;
    h_sum += h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops;
    v_sum += v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops;
    c_sum += std::max(h.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops) / v.cublas_tflops;
    printf(
        "%-20s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-5s  %s\n",
        s.label, s.N, s.K, h.blublas_tflops,
        h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops * 100, v.blublas_tflops,
        v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops * 100, v.cublas_tflops,
        vbest ? "vert" : "horiz", (h.pass && v.pass) ? "ok" : "FAIL");
  }
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  printf("vertical wins: %d / %d   avg%% of cuBLAS: horiz %.1f%%, vert %.1f%%, "
         "best-of-2 %.1f%%\n",
         vwins, total, h_sum / total * 100, v_sum / total * 100,
         c_sum / total * 100);
}

  // 0, K % 64 == 0) Note: for BM=128, cluster height is 2*BM = 256. So M must

**This matches the symptom precisely:** the first M-block (CTA0's rows, `first 10 elements`) is correct; the **second M-block (CTA1's rows) is wrong** → all-FAIL. It's not a random bug — it's that one `* BM` should be `* 128` (the TMEM lane count / peer-CTA offset).

It was *spurious* — it only ever "worked" at BM=128 by accident (the value 128 falls outside the 7-bit TMEM lane range and the hardware silently ignores it). We removed that term → DP offset 0, which is the *correct* form per CUTLASS/DeepGEMM. **This code is used by the working 128×128 and 128×256 variants**, so this is a genuine correctness improvement to them — now correct *by design*, not by luck. (They still pass — proven above.)

**2. We REMOVED the broken 64×128 (BM=64) variant (deleted, not fixed).**
BM=64 with `cta_group::2` is *fundamentally* unsupported by this kernel — it forces an interleaved 2×2 TMEM accumulator our epilogue doesn't de-interleave. It can't be fixed with a small tweak; it needs a *different* kernel (`cta_group::1`, M=64). So we deleted the `64×128`/`64×256` aliases + their sweep call, and added `static_assert(BM==128)` so nobody can instantiate a broken BM again.

## So, to your questions directly:

- **Did we fix or remove?** Both: **fixed** the underlying epilogue bug (in the code the good variants use), and **removed** the one broken variant (BM=64) that couldn't be fixed here.
- **Do we still have the variants that caused the bug?** The 64×128 **variant is gone** (it was never correct). But we **kept every working variant** — 128×128 and 128×256, both waves — all validated. We lost *nothing that worked*.
- **Net:** the template is now **more correct than before** (the latent BM=128-only assumption is fixed + guarded), and we're back to the solid **~92% best-of-tiles** state with a clean, trustworthy codebase.

**Skinny-N isn't abandoned** — it just needs the *right* tool (a `cta_group::1` M=64 variant, or DeepGEMM's swap-AB), which is separate future work. # Summary of the key finding

**On Blackwell there is no 4-CTA MMA.** The only multi-CTA `tcgen05.mma` atom is the 2-CTA (`cta_group::2`) `2x1SM` family. A "2×2" cluster is **not** a 4-CTA MMA — it is **the same `cta_group::2` MMA pair (along cluster-x/M) replicated along cluster-y/N as a second pair, with TMA multicast used to share the operand that is invariant along the added axis.** DeepGEMM implements only the 1-D (2×1) case; the 2-D (2×2) machinery lives entirely in CUTLASS. Details and citations below.

---

## Q1 — Is the MMA still `cta_group::2` in a 2×2? What does `_2x2_2cta` mean?

**Yes, still `cta_group::2`.** There is exactly one multi-CTA BF16 MMA atom and it is 2-CTA:

- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cute/arch/mma_sm100_umma.hpp:552`
  ```cpp
  struct SM100_MMA_F16BF16_2x1SM_SS
  ...:554  static_assert(M == 128 || M == 256, "... M-mode size should be 128 or 256 for 2 CTA cluster MMA.");
  ...:576  "tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16 [%0], %1, %2, %3, {%5,...,%12}, p; \n\t"
  ```
  A grep of the whole `cute/` tree for `2x2SM` returns **nothing** — no 4-CTA MMA atom exists. The atom's thread-id (number of cooperating CTAs) is 2:
- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cute/atom/mma_traits_sm100.hpp:2044`
  ```cpp
  using ThrID   = Layout&lt;_2&gt;;   // 2 CTAs cooperate per MMA
  ```
  and the A/B/C layouts (lines 2045-2050) show mode-0 (size 2 = the pair) splits **both** operands: A by `M/2` rows per CTA, B by `N/2` cols per CTA — matching your "each CTA loads its M-half / BN-half" observation.

DeepGEMM's hand-written equivalent is the same instruction:
- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/DeepGEMM/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/ptx/tcgen05.cuh:34` — `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16`.

**Structure = MMA-atom (fixed at 2 CTAs) × ClusterShape (a separate, larger tiling).** CUTLASS keeps these orthogonal: the atom (`AtomThrID = _2`) always consumes cluster **mode-0 (M/x)**, and the cluster can add more CTAs on top:
- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:374`
  ```cpp
  auto cluster_layout_vmnk = tiled_divide(make_layout(cluster_shape), make_tile(typename TiledMma::AtomThrID{}));
  ```
  `tiled_divide((M,N,K), tile&lt;2&gt;)` splits the M mode into `V=2` (the MMA pair) and a leftover M, giving a `(V, M, N, K)` layout. So for `ClusterShape&lt;2,2,1&gt;`: `V=2` (the pair), `M=1`, `N=2`, `K=1`.
- The per-CTA slice within the pair is `blockIdx.x % 2`:
  `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:516`
  ```cpp
  ThrMMA cta_mma = TiledMma{}.get_slice(blockIdx.x % size(typename TiledMma::AtomThrID{}));
  ```

**`..._2x2_2cta` interpretation:** `2cta` = the `cta_group::2` MMA (unchanged). `2x2` = `ClusterShape&lt;2,2,1&gt;` on top. (Note: cuBLAS source is *not* in these repos, so this mapping is inferred from the CUTLASS conventions above, not quoted from cuBLAS.) Instruction-level it is: **one `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` per N-column pair + 2-D TMA multicast**, not a new instruction.

## Q2 — Exact 2-D multicast-mask computation

Two independent, authoritative implementations exist in CUTLASS. Both give the same masks.

### (a) The CuTe layout-algebra version (used by the collective)

- Definition: `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cute/atom/copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1468-1511` (`create_tma_multicast_mask`). The projected-mode overload at 1504-1511 replaces one mode with `_` (wildcard) and OR-s a bit per CTA in the resulting slice, then shifts by the elected CTA:
  ```cpp
  for (int i = 0; i &lt; size(cta_layout); ++i) mcast_mask |= uint16_t(1) &lt;&lt; cta_layout(i);
  ...
  mcast_mask &lt;&lt;= elected_cta;      // line 1499
  ```
- Call site (rank→coord decomposition + which mode each operand projects):
  `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:524-541`
  ```cpp
  Layout cta_layout_mnk  = make_layout(cluster_shape_);
  Layout cta_layout_vmnk = tiled_divide(cta_layout_mnk, make_tile(typename TiledMma::AtomThrID{}));
  auto   cta_coord_vmnk  = cta_layout_vmnk.get_flat_coord(block_rank_in_cluster_);   // rank -&gt; (v,m,n,k)
  ...
  uint16_t mcast_mask_a = create_tma_multicast_mask&lt;2&gt;(cta_layout_vmnk, cta_coord_vmnk); // project N-mode
  uint16_t mcast_mask_b = create_tma_multicast_mask&lt;1&gt;(cta_layout_vmnk, cta_coord_vmnk); // project M-mode
  ```
  - **A projects mode 2 (N)** → A (invariant in N) is multicast to the CTAs that share (V,M,K) and differ in N.
  - **B projects mode 1 (M)** → B (invariant in M) is multicast to the CTAs that differ in M *beyond the atom pair*.
  - The A-partition is along N-modes, B along M-modes (lines 529-537 comments: *"Project the cta_layout for tma_a along the n-modes" / "...tma_b along the m-modes"*).

### (b) The explicit integer version (used by the pipeline; easiest to port by hand)

- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp:55-92` (`calculate_multicast_mask`) — this is the release/multicast mask, and its comment is the definitive picture for `2x1SM`:
  ```cpp
  // With MMA_2x1SM, ... send the notification ... to all 2x1 threadblocks of the cluster.
  // Below is a 4x4 example where R are the threadblocks that receive the release for
  // A/B buffers that threadblock (0,0) uses.
  // Row&amp;Col   Row     Col
  // RRRR      RRRR    Cxxx
  // RRRR      RRRR    Cxxx
  // Rxxx      xxxx    Cxxx
  // Rxxx      xxxx    Cxxx
  ```
  The participant test (lines 58-68) divides the coordinate by the atom shape (`size&lt;0&gt;(atom_thr_shape)=2` on x), i.e. "same MMA-cluster row/col":
  ```cpp
  kRow: x/2 == myx/2 ;  kCol: y == myy ;  kRowCol: row OR col
  ```
- The **UMMA peer mask** (the intrinsic 2SM pair, always present) is separate:
  `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp:96-110` (`calculate_umma_peer_mask`) — it snaps x,y down to the atom origin and sets a bit for each of the `2×1` CTAs in the pair.

### Concrete masks for `ClusterShape&lt;2,2,1&gt;`

Cluster rank (CUDA col-major) = `cta_m + 2*cta_n`, with **`cta_m = rank &amp; 1`** (position in the MMA pair, along x/M) and **`cta_n = rank &gt;&gt; 1`** (N-block, along y). Ranks: 0=(m0,n0), 1=(m1,n0), 2=(m0,n1), 3=(m1,n1).

- **A-multicast group** (share M-half, differ in N) = `{cta_m, cta_m+2}`:
  - CTA0 &amp; CTA2 → `0b0101`; CTA1 &amp; CTA3 → `0b1010`.
- **B-multicast group** (share N-block, differ in M beyond the pair): in a 2×2 there is **no** extra M axis (M-mode size = cluster.x/2 = 1), so `create_tma_multicast_mask&lt;1&gt;` returns **self-only (1 bit)**. B sharing across the pair is handled intrinsically by the `cta_group::2` TMA, not by a mask.

So your `0b11` in the 2×1 case is the *pair* mask (the `cta_group::2` scope). In the 2×2 it becomes: **A = 2-bit N-partner mask (`0b0101`/`0b1010`), B = the pair handled by the 2SM load as before.** Symmetric two-way multicast (both A *and* B) only appears when *both* cluster.x/2 &gt; 1 and cluster.y &gt; 1 — e.g. the 4×4 example above — which is 16 CTAs, not 4.

## Q3 — Cluster launch, `CTA_MASK`, barriers, `mapa`, limits

**Launch dims.** DeepGEMM launches strictly 1-D and would need changing:
- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/DeepGEMM/csrc/jit/handle.hpp:94-97`
  ```cpp
  attr.id = cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension;
  attr.val.clusterDim = {static_cast&lt;unsigned&gt;(cluster_dim), 1, 1};   // &lt;-- {2,1,1}; make {2,2,1}
  ```
  (second launch path at lines 197-202 sets `.clusterDim.x/.y/.z` likewise). Kernel attribute: `__cluster_dims__(2,1,1)` → `__cluster_dims__(2,2,1)`.

**Hard limits** (`/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cute/arch/cluster_sm100.hpp`):
- `:58-64` total cluster CTAs must be in `(0,32]` ("hardware requirement"). 2×2=4 is fine.
- `:82-88` grid must be divisible by the cluster dims; `:90-97` fallback must divide preferred; `:100-104` preferred/fallback must share z-depth.
- The multicast mask is **`uint16_t`** (see all `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST_*` sigs, e.g. `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cute/arch/copy_sm100_tma.hpp:258`), so at most 16 CTAs are individually addressable by a multicast — well above 4. (Note: clusters &gt; 8 are non-portable and require `cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed`; 4 is within the portable limit, so no opt-in needed.)

**`CTA_MASK` (the `cta_group::2` commit mask).** This is the arg to `tcgen05.commit ... multicast::cluster`:
- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/arch/barrier.h:848-863`
  ```cpp
  void umma_arrive_multicast_2x1SM(uint64_t const* smem_ptr, uint16_t cta_mask) {
    ... "tcgen05.commit.cta_group::2.mbarrier::arrive::one.shared::cluster.multicast::cluster.b64 [%0], %1;"
        :: "r"(bar_intptr), "h"(cta_mask)
  ```
  DeepGEMM builds it as `(1&lt;&lt;kNumMulticast)-1 = 0b11` for the pair (`/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/DeepGEMM/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:287-288`). **This mask is the set of CTAs whose empty/tmem barrier the MMA commit must signal — i.e. the `umma_peer_mask`, NOT the launch cluster mask.** In a 2×2 it stays the *pair* mask (2 bits) because the MMA only cooperates within its own pair; it is `calculate_umma_peer_mask` (sm100_pipeline.hpp:96-110), which for `&lt;2,2,1&gt;` yields `{cta_m_origin, cta_m_origin+1}` for that pair — e.g. `0b0011` for pair n0, `0b1100` for pair n1. Do **not** blindly widen `0b11 → 0b1111`; `0b1111` is wrong for the MMA commit (it would signal the other pair's TMEM). `0b1111` is only correct where you genuinely mean "all 4 CTAs" (e.g. a full-cluster sync).

**mbarrier arrive counts.** From `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/DeepGEMM/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:144-158`:
```cpp
full_barriers[i]-&gt;init(kNumMulticast);            // TMA-full: one arrive per pair CTA (2)
empty_barriers[i]-&gt;init(1);
tmem_full_barriers[i]-&gt;init(1);
tmem_empty_barriers[i]-&gt;init(kNumMulticast * kNumUMMAStoreThreads);  // scaled by pair size
```
These counts are keyed to the **pair (`kNumMulticast`=2)**, not to the full cluster. Going 2×1→2×2 does **not** change them, because each pair has its own barriers and its own leader — you now simply have two independent pairs' worth. The only new arrival to handle is **A's TMA multicast**: with the A load multicast across the N-partner, the completion signals *both* N-partners' `full_barrier`, so exactly one CTA per A-multicast group must issue the A load (see checklist), and the leader's `expect_tx` must still equal the bytes it actually receives (A-half once + its own B-half).

**`mapa.shared::cluster` peer addressing** works unchanged for 4 CTAs — it maps an smem address to a peer by cluster-CTA-rank:
- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/arch/barrier.h:493` and `:615` (`mapa.shared::cluster.u32 remAddr32, %0, %1;`). You just pass the 0-3 rank of the target CTA (compute peers via `cta_m/cta_n` as above).

Cluster-wide sync helper used around TMEM alloc/dealloc: `comm::cluster_sync_with_relaxed_arrive()` (sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:98,168,423) — keep these; they already gate on `kNumMulticast&gt;1` and are cluster-scoped.

## Q4 — Per-CTA output tile in a 2×2

The tile the pair's MMA instruction produces is `M = 128 * kNumMulticast = 256`, split 128 rows per CTA in TMEM:
- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/DeepGEMM/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:57-59`
  ```cpp
  constexpr uint32_t LAYOUT_AD_M = 128;                 // per-CTA TMEM M (data-partition rows)
  constexpr uint32_t UMMA_M = LAYOUT_AD_M * kNumMulticast; // = 256 instruction M for the pair
  constexpr uint32_t UMMA_N = ... BLOCK_N;
  ```
So **`128x256` is per-CTA** (128 M rows in this CTA's TMEM × 256 N), and the `2cta` pair's instruction spans `256 × 256`. For `ClusterShape&lt;2,2,1&gt;` the 4 CTAs cover the cluster output as:

| CTA rank | (cta_m,cta_n) | Rows (M) | N-block | TMEM DP base |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | (0,0) | [0,128)   | n0 | 0 |
| 1 | (1,0) | [128,256) | n0 | 0 |
| 2 | (0,1) | [0,128)   | n1 | 0 |
| 3 | (1,1) | [128,256) | n1 | 0 |

Cluster output = `256 (M) × 2·BN (N)`. **Each CTA reads its own 128 rows at TMEM data-partition base 0** — exactly your known "DP=0, no peer offset" fact. The CTA→subtile mapping is the `blockIdx.x % 2` pair-slice (sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:516) crossed with the scheduler's `(m_block, n_block)` assignment (DeepGEMM `get_swizzled_block_idx`, `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/DeepGEMM/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/scheduler/gemm.cuh:95-129`); in a 2×2 the two N-pairs of a cluster must be handed consecutive `n_block` values.

---

## Q5 — The single highest-fidelity reference

**`/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp`** is the one to copy. It is the persistent, warp-specialized `tcgen05` SS mainloop that supports an arbitrary `ClusterShape` (including 2-D) with `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD[_MULTICAST]`. Structure:
- Constructed with `(cluster_shape, block_rank_in_cluster)` (`:336`); validates the TMA copy op is either SM90 1SM or `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD[_MULTICAST]` (`:197-205`).
- `load_init` (`:497-547`) builds `cta_layout_vmnk`, decodes this CTA's `(v,m,n,k)`, partitions A along N-modes / B along M-modes, and computes `mcast_mask_a = &lt;2&gt;`, `mcast_mask_b = &lt;1&gt;`.
- Producer loop (`:598-621`) issues `copy(tma_load_a-&gt;with(*tma_barrier, mcast_mask_a), ...)` / `mcast_mask_b`.
- Consumer/MMA and TMEM-release masks come from `PipelineUmmaAsync` (`/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/cutlass/include/cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp:118-264`, masks at `:55-110`).

**DeepGEMM's `kNumMulticast` is 1-D only (2×1), not 2×2:**
- `/home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/DeepGEMM/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:64` — `DG_STATIC_ASSERT(kNumMulticast == 1 or kNumMulticast == 2, "Only support 1/2 multicast");`
- Its offsetting is a single-axis rank shift: `sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:220-223` (`m_idx += rank*load_block_m` **or** `n_idx += rank*LOAD_BLOCK_N`, never both).
- Its launch is `{cluster_dim,1,1}` (handle.hpp:94-97).
So **the 2-D pattern is provided only by CUTLASS** (the `create_tma_multicast_mask&lt;Mode&gt;` projection + `tiled_divide` by `AtomThrID` in `sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp`, and the `McastDirection` masks in `sm100_pipeline.hpp`). Use DeepGEMM as the skeleton for the hand-written pipeline/TMEM plumbing, and CUTLASS for the exact 2-D coord/mask math.

# Conversion checklist: 2×1 (`cta_group::2`) → 2×2 (4-CTA)

Model to adopt (the only valid one for 4 CTAs + `cta_group::2`): **keep the MMA pair exactly as-is along cluster-x/M; add a size-2 cluster-y/N axis giving a second pair; multicast A across the two N-blocks.** This is *not* "two independent M-pairs sharing nothing" and it is *not* a 4-CTA MMA.

1. **Cluster dims.** `__cluster_dims__(2,1,1)` → `(2,2,1)`; host `clusterDim = {2,2,1}` (handle.hpp:94-97 / 197-202). Ensure grid.x%2==0 and grid.y%2==0 (cluster_sm100.hpp:82-88). 4 CTAs ≤ 32 and ≤ 8, so no non-portable opt-in.

2. **Rank decomposition.** `cta_m = block_rank_in_cluster &amp; 1` (pair role, x/M); `cta_n = block_rank_in_cluster &gt;&gt; 1` (N-block, y). (Matches `get_flat_coord` in sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:527 and `blockIdx.x % 2` slice at :516.)

3. **MMA issue — unchanged.** Still `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16` (tcgen05.cuh:34). The **leader is per-pair**: `is_leader = (cta_m == 0)`, i.e. ranks 0 and 2 each issue their pair's MMA into their own TMEM. (Do *not* make only global rank 0 issue.)

4. **A producer (now multicast across N).** Each CTA still loads its M-half (`m_idx += cta_m * 128`) **but** switch A to `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST_2D` with `mask_a = (0b01 &lt;&lt; cta_m) | (0b01 &lt;&lt; (cta_m+2))` = `0b0101` (cta_m=0) / `0b1010` (cta_m=1) (derivation: `create_tma_multicast_mask&lt;2&gt;`, copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1468-1511 + sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:540). **Only one CTA per A-group issues the A load** (e.g. the `cta_n==0` CTA), because the multicast completion signals *both* N-partners' `full_barrier`; the other N-partner must not also issue A.

5. **B producer (unchanged sharing).** B stays per-pair: each pair loads its own N-block. Add the N-block offset to the column index: `n_idx = n_block_idx*BLOCK_N + cta_m * (BLOCK_N/2)` — i.e. keep the intra-pair N/2 split (via `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_2D`, cta_group::2) and select the pair's N-block from the scheduler's `n_block`. `mask_b` from `create_tma_multicast_mask&lt;1&gt;` is self/pair-only (no cross-N B multicast in a 2×2).

6. **Scheduler.** Assign the cluster's two pairs consecutive `n_block` values so pair-n0 and pair-n1 cover adjacent N tiles (extend DeepGEMM `get_swizzled_block_idx`, scheduler/gemm.cuh:95-129, to a 2-D cluster rasterization).

7. **`CTA_MASK` for MMA commit / empty / tmem barriers.** Keep it the **pair mask**, computed via `calculate_umma_peer_mask` (sm100_pipeline.hpp:96-110): `0b0011` for pair n0, `0b1100` for pair n1 — **not** `0b1111`. Pass it to `umma_arrive_multicast_2x1SM` (barrier.h:848). `0b1111` is only for a genuine all-4-CTA cluster sync.

8. **mbarrier arrive counts — unchanged.** `full_barriers[i]-&gt;init(kNumMulticast=2)`, `tmem_empty_barriers[i]-&gt;init(2*kNumUMMAStoreThreads)`, etc. (sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:144-158) stay keyed to the pair; you now just have two independent pairs. Adjust the A `arrive_and_expect_tx` byte count so it matches what each barrier actually receives (A-half delivered once via multicast + own B-half), and make sure the non-issuing A-partner still `arrive`s/waits correctly (mirror the leader/non-leader `arrive_and_expect_tx` vs `arrive(0u)` split at sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:243-247).

9. **Epilogue / TMEM read — unchanged.** Each CTA reads its own 128 rows at **TMEM DP base 0** (your known invariant; sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:374-376 confirms warp/DP bits are ignored and no peer offset). Output store target = `(m_block rows [cta_m*128, +128), n_block for cta_n)`.

10. **Cluster sync points.** Keep `comm::cluster_sync_with_relaxed_arrive()` around TMEM alloc/free (sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:98,168,423) — already cluster-scoped, correct for 4 CTAs.

### Pitfalls
- **No 4-CTA MMA** — never try `cta_group::4`; it doesn't exist for BF16 (mma_sm100_umma.hpp:552 is the only 2-CTA atom).
- **Per-CTA M ≤ 128** (TMEM DP limit): the pair gives 256 via 2×128; do not raise BM above 128.
- **B is not multicast in a 2×2** — only A is (asymmetric). If you actually want two-way A+B multicast, you need cluster.x ≥ 4 (multiple M-pairs), i.e. a larger cluster than 4 CTAs (see the 4×4 comment at sm100_pipeline.hpp:73-81).
- **Exactly one issuer per multicast group for A**, or you double-load and over-count `expect_tx`.
- **Don't confuse the three masks:** launch cluster dims (4 CTAs), the TMA multicast mask (A: 2 bits across N), and the MMA-commit `CTA_MASK`/peer mask (2 bits within the pair). Widening everything to `0b1111` is a correctness bug.
- **cuBLAS `128x256` is per-CTA** (128 = per-CTA M; the pair makes the MMA M=256); the cluster covers `256 × 2·N`. (This cuBLAS-naming reading is inferred from CUTLASS conventions — cuBLAS source is not in these repos.)</result>

## What the research found (authoritative, reference-cited)

**1. There is no 4-CTA MMA.** A "2×2" cluster is *not* a bigger MMA — it's the **same `cta_group::2` pair (along M) replicated as a second pair along N**, with TMA multicast. `_2x2_2cta` = the 2-CTA MMA + a `ClusterShape<2,2,1>` on top.

**2. Big correction — 2×2 does NOT "halve both operands" (my earlier §23.2 was wrong).** In a 4-CTA 2×2, **only A (the activation) is multicast** across the 2 N-blocks; **B is not** — each pair loads its own N-block. Halving *both* would need ≥16 CTAs. So 2×2's real payoff is **halving activation traffic across 2 adjacent N-tiles** — real, but **more modest** than we'd hoped.

**3. It's implementable** — I have a concrete, reference-backed 10-step checklist (cluster dims `{2,2,1}`, rank decomp `cta_m=rank&1`/`cta_n=rank>>1`, A→2D-multicast with mask `0b0101`/`0b1010`, one issuer per A-group, B per-pair N-offset, pair-scoped commit mask `0b0011`/`0b1100` — *not* `0b1111`, epilogue unchanged at DP=0).

**4. One real risk:** our kernel uses **CLC persistent scheduling**, but the references use explicit tile schedulers. Making CLC hand the cluster's two pairs *adjacent N-blocks* is the part the references don't cover — it's the main integration risk.

## Honest re-weighting → my recommendation

So 2×2 is now: **the biggest, riskiest build yet** (producer multicast rework + 2-D scheduling over our CLC loop + careful barrier/expect_tx accounting), for a **more modest benefit** than the §23.2 hope. # 2×2 cluster (4-CTA) adaptation plan for `Bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cuh`

Everything below is grounded in your file, the PTX ISA 9.3 spec, and CUTLASS/DeepGEMM. I do **not** re-derive the model; I give the mechanics and the concrete edits. Two important framing facts up front, because they change the whole shape of the plan:

**Fact A — the 2SM TMA already distributes across the MMA pair; multicast is only needed to reach the *second* pair.** DeepGEMM's SM100 path issues `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_*` (the *non*-multicast `cta_group::2` form) for *both* A and B — see `DeepGEMM/.../common/tma_copy.cuh:36-45` (the `__CUDA_ARCH__ &gt;= 1000` branch uses `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_2D`, **not** the multicast op). That is exactly what your kernel already does at `tma_4d_gmem2smem&lt;CLUSTER_SIZE&gt;` (`Bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cuh:222-232`, called at :700-704/:726-730/:754-758). So within a pair you keep doing what you do now. Multicast `.multicast::cluster` + `ctaMask` is **only** the mechanism to also deposit A into the *other* N-pair.

**Fact B — CLC hands out work per *cluster*, not per CTA.** PTX ISA 9.3 §9.7.14.18 (`ptx_isa_9.3.txt:23554-23556`): "the opaque response contains the ctaid of the **first CTA of the canceled cluster**." With `.multicast::cluster::all` (`:23576-23579`) that response is broadcast to every CTA of the requesting cluster. So one `try_cancel` = one work item for the whole 4-CTA cluster, which you split into 2 N-blocks. This is the single most important consequence for your scheduler.

Because of Fact B, I strongly recommend **`__cluster_dims__(4,1,1)` with a 1-D grid**, not `(2,2,1)`. Both are legal and produce *identical* masks, but `(4,1,1)` keeps your CLC decode 1-D (`first_ctaid.x / 4`), exactly analogous to today's `/CLUSTER_SIZE`. See "Hurdle 1" for the full argument. I give the `(4,1,1)` path as primary and note the `(2,2,1)` deltas.

## 0. Rank → (cta_m, cta_n) — the foundation (Question 5)

Your `get_cluster_cta_rank()` reads `%cluster_ctaid.x` (`:206-210`). For a 1-D `(4,1,1)` cluster that is still the flat 0..3 rank, so it keeps working. But make it shape-independent by switching to the flat rank register, which PTX guarantees is unique across all dims:

- PTX ISA 9.3 `:1146-1150`: "Each CTA in the cluster also has a unique CTA identifier (`cluster_ctarank`) across all dimensions … `%cluster_ctarank`." (TOC `:433`).

```
// replace body of get_cluster_cta_rank()
asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctarank;" : "=r"(r));   // flat 0..3, any shape
```

Then, with the **model's** bit assignment (which is what `(4,1,1)` linear rank and `(2,2,1)` rank=`x+2y` both give):

```
const uint32_t cta_m = cta_rank &amp; 1u;   // 0 / 1  → M-partner (pair-internal, drives DP rows)
const uint32_t cta_n = cta_rank &gt;&gt; 1;   // 0 / 1  → N-partner (which BN block)
const uint32_t pair_leader = cta_rank &amp; ~1u;   // even rank of my pair (0 or 2)
const uint32_t n_peer      = cta_rank ^ 2u;     // same cta_m, other N-block (0↔2, 1↔3)
```

This reproduces the model exactly:
- A multicast mask (same cta_m, both cta_n): rank0→`{0,2}`=`0b0101`, rank1→`{1,3}`=`0b1010`.
- Pair (commit/peer) mask (same cta_n, both cta_m): pair0=`{0,1}`=`0b0011`, pair1=`{2,3}`=`0b1100`.

For **`mapa.shared::cluster`** peer addressing (`map_smem_addr_to_cta_rank`, `:212-219`): the rank you pass is the *flat* cluster rank of the target CTA. For reaching your pair leader pass `pair_leader`; for the N-partner pass `n_peer`. (Today you hard-code rank `0`/`1` at `:655/:659/:914/:945` — those all become the computed peers below.)

**`(2,2,1)` delta:** identical, because `%cluster_ctarank` = `ctaid.x + 2*ctaid.y`, so bit0=cta_m(x), bit1=cta_n(y). The masks come out the same. Do **not** use `%cluster_ctaid.x` for `(2,2,1)` — it would only give 0/1.

## 1. TMA multicast — exact instruction + descriptor (Question 1)

**Instruction form.** Your current op (`:226-231`) has no mask. The multicast form adds the `.multicast::cluster` qualifier **and** a `u16` `ctaMask` operand, *keeping* `.cta_group::2`. Both qualifiers are present simultaneously. Exact PTX from CUTLASS `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST_4D` (`cutlass/include/cute/arch/copy_sm100_tma.hpp:320-326`):

```
cp.async.bulk.tensor.4d.cta_group::2.shared::cluster.global.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.multicast::cluster.L2::cache_hint
    [%0], [%1, {%4,%5,%6,%7}], [%2], %3, %8;
//  dst   tmap  coords          mbar   ctaMask(%3, "h")   cache_hint(%8)
```

The PTX ISA generic tensor syntax confirming operand order (`ptx_isa_9.3.txt:17004-17028`, example `:17276-17279`): `… .multicast::cluster … [sMem],[tmap,{coords}],[mbar], ctaMask;`. The mask semantics (`:17170-17172`): "Operand `ctaMask` … each bit position in the 16-bit `ctaMask` corresponds to the `%cluster_ctarank` of the destination CTA. The source data is multicast to the same offset as `dstMem` in the shared memory of each destination CTA."

A cache-hint-free multicast form is also legal (drop `.L2::cache_hint` and the last operand); you can keep your no-cache-hint style. So your device helper becomes a second overload:

```
template &lt;int CTA_GROUP=2&gt;
__device__ __forceinline__ void
tma_4d_gmem2smem_mc(int dst, const void* tmap, int x,int y,int z,int w,
                    int mbar, uint16_t ctaMask) {
  asm volatile(
    "cp.async.bulk.tensor.4d.shared::cluster.global"
    ".mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.cta_group::%8.multicast::cluster"
    " [%0], [%1, {%2,%3,%4,%5}], [%6], %7;"
    :: "r"(dst),"l"(tmap),"r"(x),"r"(y),"r"(z),"r"(w),"r"(mbar),
       "h"(ctaMask),"n"(CTA_GROUP) : "memory");
}
```

**cta_group::2 × multicast::cluster interaction** (the part you asked to nail down). PTX ISA 9.3 `:17173-17180`: the *data* goes to every CTA whose bit is set in `ctaMask`. The *mbarrier completion signal*, under `.cta_group::2`, "is sent either to the destination CTA or its peer-CTA based on the `%cluster_ctarank` **parity of the shared memory where the mbarrier object `mbar` resides**." So if your `mbar` operand lives on an even (leader) CTA, all the completion bytes are routed to the *even* CTA of each destination pair. That is exactly why CUTLASS masks the mbar pointer with `Sm100MmaPeerBitMask = 0xFEFFFFFF` (clears smem addr bit 24) before every 2SM load — `copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45` and applied at `:318` (multicast 4D) / `:141` (plain 4D): "Set peer bit to 0 so that the transaction bytes will update CTA0's barrier." You already exploit the same bit-24 trick in the epilogue at `:1006-1008`.

**Descriptor / `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`: no change.** Multicast is purely an instruction-time mask; the `CUtensorMap` is unchanged. Nothing in `init_4d_tma_A_MK/A_KM/B_KN/B_NK` (`:379-461`) needs to change for multicast. (This matches CUTLASS: the same TMA descriptor is used by both `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_4D` and `..._MULTICAST_4D`.) The *only* descriptor consideration for you is the A box: A must still describe **BM rows** (one M-half) — which it already does (`boxDim {64, BM, BK/64, 1}` at `:389`), so a single A multicast delivers exactly one M-half to both N-partners. Good.

## 2. expect_tx / barrier byte accounting with multicast (Question 2)

First, the reference pattern. DeepGEMM's asymmetric split:
- `full_barriers[i]-&gt;init(kNumMulticast)` (`sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh:148`) — full-barrier arrival count = #CTAs feeding it.
- leader: `arrive_and_expect_tx(kNumArrivalBytes * kNumMulticast)` (`:243-244`); non-leader: `arrive(0u)` (`:245-246`).

Your kernel instead uses the **symmetric** pattern: `full_mbar` init = `1*CLUSTER_SIZE` (`:626`) and *each* CTA calls `mbarrier_arrive_expect(mbar, copy_size)` on the leader's barrier (`:697/:723/:751`). Both are valid; expect_tx is purely a byte *counter* (PTX `:22630-22633`: "the count argument of the arrive-on operation is assumed to be 1" when `.arrive.expect_tx` are combined). The symmetric form is what makes your adaptation trivial.

**Key result (worked out from PTX `:17173-17180`): the per-CTA `copy_size` declaration is unchanged, per pair.** Reasoning for pair-0 leader (`rank0.full_mbar`), with A multicast:
- rank0 issues A-multicast mask `0b0101`: its rank0 copy signals `rank0.full_mbar` (+A_half); the rank2 copy signals `rank2.full_mbar` (+A_half) — routed to the even CTA of each dest pair because mbar sits on an even CTA.
- rank1 issues A-multicast mask `0b1010`: rank1 copy → routed to its even peer rank0 → `rank0.full_mbar` (+A_half); rank3 copy → `rank2.full_mbar`.
- rank0 and rank1 each issue their own B (plain 2SM, no multicast) → each signals `rank0.full_mbar` (+B_half each).

Total into `rank0.full_mbar` = A_half + A_half + B_half + B_half = **2·copy_size**. Same as today. Identically, `rank2.full_mbar` receives A_half (from rank0's mc) + A_half (from rank1's mc) + B_half (rank2) + B_half (rank3) = 2·copy_size.

Because expect_tx only sums bytes, you make each of the pair's two CTAs declare `copy_size` on **its pair leader**:

```
const int mbar = tma_mbar_base + stage*8;      // tma_mbar_base now = leader's full_mbar (see §6)
mbarrier_arrive_expect(mbar, copy_size);        // UNCHANGED per-CTA; leader now = rank &amp; ~1
```

So the accounting edits are only:
- `full_mbar` init count stays `1*CLUSTER_SIZE` = 2 (`:626`) — it is **per pair**, feeding count = 2 CTAs per pair. Do **not** bump to 4.
- `tma_mbar_base` (`:653-655`) changes from "rank0 vs mapa(…,0)" to "own if even, else `mapa(full_mbar, pair_leader)`" (§6).
- The A multicast mbar operand must have bit-24 cleared (peer bit) so all A bytes land on the leader, exactly like CUTLASS `copy_sm100_tma.hpp:318`. Concretely: `int a_mbar = mbar &amp; 0xFEFFFFFF;` for the A multicast call, while B uses the plain `mbar`. (In your single-leader-per-pair scheme `mbar` already points at the even leader, so bit 24 is likely already 0; masking is a safe no-op that matches the reference.)

Which CTA calls what, precisely:
- **rank0, rank1 (cta_n=0):** issue B (plain 2SM), issue A (multicast), and `mbarrier_arrive_expect(leader_mbar, copy_size)`.
- **rank2, rank3 (cta_n=1):** issue B (plain 2SM) only, do **not** issue A, and still `mbarrier_arrive_expect(leader_mbar, copy_size)` (declaring the copy_size = A_half they will *receive* + B_half they load).

**Simpler correct fallback (recommended first milestone):** skip A multicast entirely — let all 4 CTAs load their own A+B (rank2 redundantly re-loads rank0's A rows). Then each pair is byte-for-byte your current 2-CTA kernel; expect_tx, init counts, and TMA calls are 100% unchanged, and the only new logic is the scheduler split (§3) + per-pair leader (§6). Cost: 2× A DRAM traffic. Validate this first, then turn on A multicast for the bandwidth win.

## 3. CLC + 2-D cluster — the hard part (Question 3)

**(a) Granularity.** Per-cluster (Fact B, PTX `:23554-23556`, `:23576-23579`). CLC does **not** know your cluster is 2×2; it just returns the ctaid of the first CTA of the next cluster and broadcasts it to all CTAs of the requesting cluster. It does not split into N-blocks — you do.

**(b) Decode.** Redefine the tile space so one cluster = one row-tile × **two adjacent** N-blocks. In the launcher (§4) set `grid_n_blocks = N/BN` (unchanged concept) but iterate clusters over `grid_n_clusters = ceil(grid_n_blocks / 2)`. Two clean options:

- **Option A (recommended, minimal code):** keep `grid_n` meaning "N-blocks" and `total_mn_tiles = grid_m * grid_n` as today, but note the *cluster* stride is 4 CTAs and each cluster owns 2 N-blocks. The scheduler enumerates over **pairs of tiles**. Easiest is to change the linear→tile identity: with `(4,1,1)`, `cluster_index = first_ctaid.x / 4`, and you map cluster_index to `(row_tile, n_cluster)` where `n_cluster = cluster_index % grid_n_clusters`, `row_tile = cluster_index / grid_n_clusters`, `grid_n_clusters = ceil_div(grid_n, 2)`. Then:

```
block_row = row_tile*CLUSTER_M + cta_m;      // CLUSTER_M = 2 (M-partners)
block_col = n_cluster*2 + cta_n;             // the two adjacent N-blocks
```

So pair-0 (cta_n=0) does N-block `2*n_cluster`, pair-1 (cta_n=1) does N-block `2*n_cluster+1`. This replaces the current `decode_mn_tile` + `block_row = row_tile*CLUSTER_SIZE + cta_rank` (`:673-675`, `:962-963`, `:1080-1082`). Note the two distinct "cluster" factors now: **M-cluster = 2** (partners in a pair, was `CLUSTER_SIZE`) and **N-cluster = 2** (pairs). Introduce `constexpr int CLUSTER_M=2, CLUSTER_N=2;` and stop overloading `CLUSTER_SIZE` (which conflated "pair size" and "cluster size"). Anywhere `CLUSTER_SIZE` meant "MMA pair" (TMA `cta_group`, `i_desc` M height `:498`, TMEM per-CTA, B split `:88`) it stays **2**. Anywhere it meant "CTAs per cluster / grid stride / CLC arrive count" it becomes **4**.

- **Option B (`(2,2,1)`):** `first_ctaid.x/2` and `first_ctaid.y/2` give `(cx, cy)` cluster coords directly; `n_cluster=cx`, `row_tile=cy` (or your wave policy). Requires reading `get_first_ctaid::y` too (see hurdle).

**(c) Ordering / deadlock hazards with 4 CTAs sharing CLC.** Three concrete ones:

1. **`clc_empty` arrive count.** Today `CLC_EMPTY_ARRIVE = NUM_WARPS * CLUSTER_SIZE` (`:108-110`) = warps × 2. All CTAs' warps arrive on the leader's `clc_empty` (`cta0_clc_empty_addr`, `:657-659`, arrivals at `:769/:898/:927/:1069`). With 4 CTAs it **must become `NUM_WARPS * 4`**. If you leave it at ×2 the leader's `clc_empty` never reaches count → scheduler blocks at `:938` → deadlock. This is the single most likely 4-CTA hang.
2. **`try_cancel` response + expect_tx must be armed on all 4 CTAs.** The scheduler (rank0 only, `:909/:937`) pre-arms `clc_full` expect_tx=16 on rank0 and rank1 (`:912-916`, `:942-948`). With `.multicast::cluster::all` the response is written to *every* CTA and each CTA's `clc_full` is completed (PTX `:23576-23579`). So you must arm expect_tx=16 on **all four** CTAs' `clc_full` before each `try_cancel`: loop the `mbarrier_arrive_expect_cluster(mapa(clc_full, r),16)` for `r=0..3`. Miss one and that CTA's `clc_full` wait (`:765/:894/:923/:1064`) hangs.
3. **`clc_full` init count / who consumes.** `clc_full_mbar` init=1 (`:634`) and is completed by the async `try_cancel` transaction bytes, not by arrive-count, so it stays 1 — but every one of the 4 CTAs' non-scheduler warps waits on its *own local* `clc_full` (they read `clc_full_mbar_addr + …`, local). Since the response is multicast to all CTAs, each CTA's local `clc_full` is signaled. Good — no change to init, but confirm every CTA (not just rank0/1) has its `clc_full` armed (point 2).

There is no new cross-CTA ordering hazard beyond these counts: the CLC pipeline is driven solely by rank0's scheduler; the other 3 CTAs are pure consumers of the broadcast response, exactly as ranks 0/1 are today.

## 4. Cluster launch mechanics (Question 4)

- **Compile-time is fine.** Switch the attribute at `:539` from `__cluster_dims__(2,1,1)` to `__cluster_dims__(4,1,1)` (primary) or `__cluster_dims__(2,2,1)`. No need for `cudaLaunchKernelEx` runtime clusters — 4 ≤ 8 is portable and well under the hardware cap of 32 total CTAs/cluster (CUTLASS `cluster_sm100.hpp:57-64`: "Total number of cluster cannot be greater than 32"). Keep your plain `kernel&lt;&lt;&lt;grid, threads, smem, stream&gt;&gt;&gt;` (`:1184`).
- **Grid divisibility.** CUTLASS `cluster_sm100.hpp` (the `grid_dims % cluster_dims` check ~`:83-90`): grid must be divisible by cluster dims **per axis**. For `(4,1,1)`: `grid.x % 4 == 0`. For `(2,2,1)`: `grid.x % 2 == 0 &amp;&amp; grid.y % 2 == 0` → grid must become 2-D.
- **Grid shape.** Primary `(4,1,1)` keeps the grid **1-D**: change `:1182` from
  `dim3 grid(total_mn_tiles * batchCount * CLUSTER_SIZE)` (stride 2) to
  `dim3 grid(total_cluster_tiles * batchCount * 4)`, where `total_cluster_tiles = grid_m * ceil_div(grid_n, 2)` (§3b). `grid.x` is automatically a multiple of 4. For `(2,2,1)` you'd instead build `dim3 grid(2*grid_n_clusters, 2*grid_m, batch)` and read both ctaid dims — more launcher churn for zero benefit, hence the `(4,1,1)` recommendation.
- `init_tile_idx = blockIdx.x / CLUSTER_SIZE` (`:661`) → `/ 4`; and CLC `new_tile_idx = new_ctaid / CLUSTER_SIZE` (`:777/:1077`) → `/ 4`. DeepGEMM/CUTLASS set grid+cluster the same way (DeepGEMM launches a persistent grid of `kNumSMs` and lets CLC page work; you're keeping your `total_*·batch·clusterCTAs` grid, which is also fine).

## 6. The A-load one-issuer problem — producer restructure (Question 6)

Which CTA issues what (matches §1/§2):
- **A:** issued only by **cta_n==0** CTAs (ranks 0,1), multicast, mask = `(cta_m==0)?0b0101:0b1010` i.e. `mask = 0b0101 &lt;&lt; cta_m`. mbar = leader's full_mbar with bit-24 cleared.
- **B:** issued by **all four** CTAs (plain 2SM `cta_group::2`), each its own N-half (unchanged code path).
- **expect_tx:** all four CTAs `mbarrier_arrive_expect(leader_mbar, copy_size)` (§2).

Concrete producer edit (NN shown; TN/NT identical pattern at `:682-763`). Precompute once per tile:

```
const int leader_mbar_base = (cta_m==0) ? full_mbar_addr        // I am the even leader
                                        : map_smem_addr_to_cta_rank(full_mbar_addr, pair_leader);
const uint16_t a_mask = (uint16_t)(0b0101u &lt;&lt; cta_m);   // 0b0101 (rank0) / 0b1010 (rank1)
```

Inside the k-loop, replace the two unconditional `tma_4d_gmem2smem&lt;2&gt;` calls (`:754-758`) with:

```
const int mbar   = leader_mbar_base + stage*8;
const int a_mbar = mbar &amp; 0xFEFFFFFF;          // peer bit → leader (CUTLASS copy_sm100_tma.hpp:318)
mbarrier_arrive_expect(mbar, copy_size);        // every CTA declares its copy_size

// B: every CTA loads its own N-half (unchanged)
tma_4d_gmem2smem&lt;2&gt;(B_smem, &amp;B_tmap, 0, k*BK, B_col, cur_batch, mbar);

// A: only cta_n==0 issues, multicast to its N-partner
if (cta_n == 0)
  tma_4d_gmem2smem_mc&lt;2&gt;(A_smem, &amp;A_tmap, 0, A_row, k, cur_batch, a_mbar, a_mask);
```

`A_row`/`B_col` use `block_row = row_tile*CLUSTER_M + cta_m` and `block_col = n_cluster*2 + cta_n` from §3b. Note `A_row` depends only on `cta_m` (same for the two N-partners — that's *why* A is shareable); `B_col` depends on both `cta_n` (which block) and `cta_rank`'s half within the pair (the existing `(int)cta_rank*(BN/CLUSTER_SIZE)` term at `:741` becomes `cta_m*(BN/2)` since the pair-internal half is indexed by cta_m).

The non-issuing CTAs (ranks 2,3) still get correct arrivals because (a) they declare `copy_size` expect_tx on their leader, and (b) the A bytes are delivered by ranks 0/1's multicast and routed to their leader `rank2.full_mbar` (§2). The consumer/MMA leader for pair1 (rank2) waits on its local `full_mbar` and it completes at 2·copy_size — no code difference from pair0.
