// test_bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cu
// Comprehensive accuracy and benchmark test suite for the unified SM103a
// Cluster GEMM template. Target: NVIDIA B300 (SM 10.3a) —
// tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16
//
// Usage:
//   make run TEST=examples/test_bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cu
//

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cublas_v2.h>
#include <cuda_bf16.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <numeric>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

// Include the unified SM103 cluster template
#include "../src/level3/batched_gemm/BF16/SM103/Bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cuh"

// ─── error helpers
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                       \
  do {                                                                         \
    cudaError_t e = (call);                                                    \
    if (e != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \
      fprintf(stderr, "CUDA error %s at %s:%d\n", cudaGetErrorString(e),       \
              __FILE__, __LINE__);                                             \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

#define CHECK_CUBLAS(call)                                                     \
  do {                                                                         \
    cublasStatus_t e = (call);                                                 \
    if (e != CUBLAS_STATUS_SUCCESS) {                                          \
      fprintf(stderr, "cuBLAS error %d at %s:%d\n", (int)e, __FILE__,          \
              __LINE__);                                                       \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

// ─── data init
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static void fill_rand_bf16(std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &v, unsigned seed) {
  srand(seed);
  for (auto &x : v)
    x = __float2bfloat16((float(rand()) / RAND_MAX) * 2.f - 1.f);
}

// ─── accuracy check
// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Worst-element info from the last max_rel_err call (printed on FAIL so we
// can SEE whether a failure is real corruption or a near-zero cancellation
// artifact).
static size_t g_err_idx = 0;
static float g_err_ref = 0.f, g_err_out = 0.f;

static double max_rel_err(const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &ref,
                          const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &out) {
  double max_e = 0.0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < ref.size(); ++i) {
    double r = __bfloat162float(ref[i]);
    double o = __bfloat162float(out[i]);
    // Denominator floor 1.0 (was 1e-5): outputs are O(sqrt(K)) ~ 10..100, but
    // a few elements are near-zero by CANCELLATION, and there cuBLAS vs our
    // kernel legitimately differ by accumulation ORDER (different tiles split
    // K differently) — tiny absolute diffs that explode as RELATIVE error
    // (seen on the 622M-element LM-heads: identical dumps yet rel>5%). Real
    // corruption (wrong tile/swizzle/barrier) shifts elements by O(10-100) and
    // still trips 5% against floor 1.0. DeepGEMM avoids the same artifact by
    // using a norm-based diff instead of per-element rel-err.
    double e = std::abs(r - o) / std::max(1.0, std::abs(r));
    if (e > max_e) {
      max_e = e;
      g_err_idx = i;
      g_err_ref = (float)r;
      g_err_out = (float)o;
    }
  }
  return max_e;
}

// ─── benchmark harness
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Result {
  double blublas_tflops;
  double cublas_tflops;
  double rel_err;
  bool pass;
};

// Global progress counter — how many test CASES (run_test_case calls) have
// finished. Printed as a leading [n] on every result row so a long run shows
// live progress (and you can tell it's not hung). Set g_cases_total in main to
// enable an [n/total] readout.
static int g_cases_done = 0;
static int g_cases_total = 0;

// Generic runner for any Config and Layout
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false,
          bool MulticastA = false>
static Result run_test_case(int M, int N, int K, int batchCount, float alpha,
                            float beta, cublasHandle_t cublas,
                            cudaStream_t stream) {
  // Determine dimensions based on layout
  long long elA = 0;
  long long elB = 0;
  const long long elC = (long long)batchCount * M * N;

  if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * N * K;
  } else { // TN
    elA = (long long)batchCount * K * M;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  }

  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hA(elA), hB(elB), hC_init(elC);
  fill_rand_bf16(hA, 42);
  fill_rand_bf16(hB, 99);

  // For beta != 0, initialize C with random values
  if (beta != 0.0f) {
    fill_rand_bf16(hC_init, 77);
  } else {
    std::fill(hC_init.begin(), hC_init.end(), __float2bfloat16(0.f));
  }

  __nv_bfloat16 *dA, *dB, *dC_ref, *dC_blu;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA, elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dA, hA.data(), elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, hB.data(), elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_ref, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_blu, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));

  // ── cuBLAS reference ────────
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
        cublas, transB, transA, // Swap due to column-major vs row-major
        N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb, strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF,
        (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF, N, (long long)M * N,
        batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  }

  // Run exactly one iteration of BluBridge for accuracy checking
  launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA>(
      dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Accuracy Check
  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hC_ref_h(elC), hC_blu_h(elC);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_ref_h.data(), dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_blu_h.data(), dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));

  double rel_err = max_rel_err(hC_ref_h, hC_blu_h);
  if (rel_err >= 0.05) {
    printf("  [DEBUG FAIL] worst element: idx=%zu (row %lld, col %lld)  "
           "ref=%.6f  out=%.6f  absdiff=%.6f\n",
           g_err_idx, (long long)(g_err_idx / N), (long long)(g_err_idx % N),
           g_err_ref, g_err_out, std::abs(g_err_ref - g_err_out));
    printf("  [DEBUG FAIL] First 10 elements:\n");
    printf("    Ref (cuBLAS): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_ref_h[i]));
    printf("\n    Blu (Template): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_blu_h[i]));
    printf("\n");
  }

  // Warmup BluBridge Cluster Template (5 iters)
  for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA>(
        dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Timed BluBridge Cluster Template (20 iters)
  cudaEvent_t t0, t1;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA>(
        dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());
  float blu_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&blu_ms, t0, t1));

  // Warmup + timed cuBLAS (20 iters)
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  }
  float cub_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&cub_ms, t0, t1));

  double flops = 2.0 * (double)M * N * K * batchCount;
  double iters = 20.0;
  double blu_tfl = flops * iters / (blu_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;
  double cub_tfl = flops * iters / (cub_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_ref));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_blu));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t1));

  ++g_cases_done; // one more test case finished (progress readout)
  return {blu_tfl, cub_tfl, rel_err, rel_err < 0.05};
}

// Struct to define dynamic test shape
struct Shape {
  int M, N, K, batch;
  float alpha, beta;
  const char *label;
};

// Layout name helper
static const char *layout_name(Sm103Layout layout) {
  switch (layout) {
  case Sm103Layout::NN:
    return "NN";
  case Sm103Layout::NT:
    return "NT";
  case Sm103Layout::TN:
    return "TN";
  }
  return "Unknown";
}

template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false,
          bool MulticastA = false>
static bool run_test_suite_for_layout_config(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                                             cublasHandle_t cublas,
                                             cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Testing Layout: %s | Config: %dx%dx%d (cta_group::2, %s wave, "
         "clusterN=%d, mcastA=%d) ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN, Config::BK,
         VerticalWave ? "vertical" : "horizontal", Config::CLUSTER_N,
         (int)MulticastA);
  printf("%-18s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s  %-9s  %-9s  %-7s  %-10s  %-6s  %s\n",
         "Shape", "M", "N", "K", "Batch", "alpha", "beta", "Template", "cuBLAS",
         "%cuBLAS", "MaxRelErr", "Status", "wall(ms)");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(116, '-').c_str());
  fflush(stdout); // flush the suite header NOW so a hang on the first kernel
                  // still shows which suite/layout we're in (frontier visible)

  int passed = 0;
  int total = 0;
  double suite_wall_ms = 0.0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    // 256x256x64 config requires M & N to be multiples of 256
    if (Config::BM == 256 && (s.M % 512 != 0 || s.N % 256 != 0)) {
      // Skip shapes that are not compatible with 256x256 config
      // Note: cluster height is 2*BM = 512, cluster width is BN = 256
      continue;
    }

    total++;
    // Per-test wall-clock (whole run_test_case: alloc + cuBLAS ref + accuracy
    // check + warmups + 20 timed iters of both). Includes host-side work, so
    // it's much larger than the pure-kernel Template/cuBLAS TFLOPS above.
    auto t_start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result r = run_test_case<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch, s.alpha, s.beta, cublas, stream);
    auto t_end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double wall_ms =
        std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t_end - t_start).count();
    suite_wall_ms += wall_ms;

    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-18s %5d %5d %5d %5d %5.1f %5.1f  %8.2f T  %8.2f T  "
           "%5.1f%%  "
           "%9.2e  %-6s  %8.1f\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch,
           s.alpha, s.beta, r.blublas_tflops, r.cublas_tflops,
           r.cublas_tflops > 0 ? r.blublas_tflops / r.cublas_tflops * 100 : 0.0,
           r.rel_err, r.pass ? "PASS" : "FAIL", wall_ms);
    fflush(stdout); // flush so progress is visible live during long runs

    if (r.pass)
      ++passed;
  }
  printf("Result: %d / %d PASSED   (suite wall time: %.1f ms)\n", passed, total,
         suite_wall_ms);
  fflush(stdout); // flush the suite Result so the log frontier is always exact
  return passed == total;
}

// ─── Qwen 42-shape sweep — P1 impact + dispatcher routing data
// ──────────────── For each real Qwen matmul shape (M=4096), run the 128×256
// tile in BOTH horizontal and vertical wave and compare to cuBLAS. Tells us,
// per shape, whether vertical helps (→ dispatcher routes it to vertical) and
// how close we are to cuBLAS. Correctness is validated by the suites above;
// here we focus on throughput, but still flag any accuracy miss.
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout>
static void run_qwen_sweep(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                           cublasHandle_t cublas, cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Qwen 42-shape sweep (%s, %dx%d tile): horizontal vs vertical "
         "vs cuBLAS ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN);
  printf("%-20s %-6s %7s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s  %-6s  %8s  %s\n", "Shape", "wave",
         "N", "K", "TFLOPS", "%cuB", "cuBLAS", "Status", "wall(ms)", "best");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  int vwins = 0, total = 0;
  double h_sum = 0, v_sum = 0, c_sum = 0;
  double sweep_wall_ms = 0.0; // total sweep wall-clock (whole run_test_case
                              // incl. host-side work, like the suites)
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    // One printed row PER test case (own [n/total], own TFLOPS/%/Status/wall)
    // — no combined row hiding the losing wave's numbers. Winner marked on the
    // vert row once both are known.
    auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result h = run_test_case<Config, Layout, false>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f,
                                                    0.0f, cublas, stream);
    auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double h_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t1 - t0).count();
    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-20s %-6s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-6s  "
           "%8.1f\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, "horiz", s.N, s.K,
           h.blublas_tflops, h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops * 100,
           h.cublas_tflops, h.pass ? "ok" : "FAIL", h_ms);
    fflush(stdout);
    auto t2 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result v = run_test_case<Config, Layout, true>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f,
                                                   cublas, stream);
    auto t3 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double v_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t3 - t2).count();
    bool vbest = v.blublas_tflops >= h.blublas_tflops;
    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-20s %-6s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-6s  "
           "%8.1f  best=%s\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, "vert", s.N, s.K,
           v.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops * 100,
           v.cublas_tflops, v.pass ? "ok" : "FAIL", v_ms,
           vbest ? "vert" : "horiz");
    fflush(stdout);
    sweep_wall_ms += h_ms + v_ms;
    if (vbest)
      ++vwins;
    ++total;
    h_sum += h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops;
    v_sum += v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops;
    c_sum += std::max(h.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops) / v.cublas_tflops;
  }
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  printf("vertical wins: %d / %d   avg%% of cuBLAS: horiz %.1f%%, vert %.1f%%, "
         "best-of-2 %.1f%%   (sweep wall time: %.1f s)\n",
         vwins, total, h_sum / total * 100, v_sum / total * 100,
         c_sum / total * 100, sweep_wall_ms / 1000.0);
}

int main() {
  int dev = 0;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDevice(&dev));
  cudaDeviceProp prop;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, dev));

  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");
  printf("SM103 Cluster GEMM Unified Template Test Suite\n");
  printf("Device : %s  (SM %d.%d)\n", prop.name, prop.major, prop.minor);
  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");

  if (prop.major != 10 || prop.minor != 3) {
    printf("[SKIP] SM103 Cluster GEMM template requires SM 10.3 (Blackwell "
           "Ultra/sm_103a).\n"
           "       This device is SM %d.%d (%s).\n"
           "       Tests skipped.\n",
           prop.major, prop.minor, prop.name);
    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
  }

  cudaStream_t stream;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamCreate(&stream));

  cublasHandle_t cublas;
  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasCreate(&cublas));
  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasSetStream(cublas, stream));

  // Test cases for 128x128x64 configuration (requires M % 256 == 0, N % 128 ==
  // 0, K % 64 == 0) Note: for BM=128, cluster height is 2*BM = 256. So M must
  // be a multiple of 256.
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_128 = {
      // M, N, K, batch, alpha, beta, label
      {256, 128, 64, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "tiny"},
      {256, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "small"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "medium"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "large"},
      // Multi-batch test
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-4"},
      {256, 256, 128, 8, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-8"},
      // Alpha/Beta scaling and accumulation tests
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.0f, "alpha-scaling"},
      {256, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.5f, "beta-accumulate"},
      {512, 512, 128, 2, 1.2f, 0.8f, "alpha-beta-batch"},
      // ── Comparison shapes vs legacy _cluster.cu B0 results (M=4096) ──
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-wideN-gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-skinny-K"}};

  // Test cases for 256x256x64 configuration (requires M % 512 == 0, N % 256 ==
  // 0, K % 64 == 0)
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_256 = {
      {512, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "tiny-256"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "small-256"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "medium-256"},
      // Multi-batch test
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-4-256"},
      // Alpha/Beta scaling and accumulation tests
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.5f, "alpha-beta-256"},
      // ── Comparison shapes vs legacy _cluster.cu B0 results (M=4096) ──
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-wideN-gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-skinny-K"}};

  bool all_passed = true;

  // Total test cases for the [done/total] progress readout. Keep in sync if the
  // suites below change: 128x128 (×3 layouts) + 128x256 (×3) + P1-vertical (×3)

// test_bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cu
// Comprehensive accuracy and benchmark test suite for the unified SM103a
// Cluster GEMM template. Target: NVIDIA B300 (SM 10.3a) —
// tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16
//
// Usage:
//   make run TEST=examples/test_bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cu
//

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cublas_v2.h>
#include <cuda_bf16.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <numeric>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

// Include the unified SM103 cluster template
#include "../src/level3/batched_gemm/BF16/SM103/Bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cuh"

// ─── error helpers
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                       \
  do {                                                                         \
    cudaError_t e = (call);                                                    \
    if (e != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \
      fprintf(stderr, "CUDA error %s at %s:%d\n", cudaGetErrorString(e),       \
              __FILE__, __LINE__);                                             \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

#define CHECK_CUBLAS(call)                                                     \
  do {                                                                         \
    cublasStatus_t e = (call);                                                 \
    if (e != CUBLAS_STATUS_SUCCESS) {                                          \
      fprintf(stderr, "cuBLAS error %d at %s:%d\n", (int)e, __FILE__,          \
              __LINE__);                                                       \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

// ─── data init
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static void fill_rand_bf16(std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &v, unsigned seed) {
  srand(seed);
  for (auto &x : v)
    x = __float2bfloat16((float(rand()) / RAND_MAX) * 2.f - 1.f);
}

// ─── accuracy check
// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Worst-element info from the last max_rel_err call (printed on FAIL so we
// can SEE whether a failure is real corruption or a near-zero cancellation
// artifact).
static size_t g_err_idx = 0;
static float g_err_ref = 0.f, g_err_out = 0.f;

static double max_rel_err(const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &ref,
                          const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &out) {
  double max_e = 0.0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < ref.size(); ++i) {
    double r = __bfloat162float(ref[i]);
    double o = __bfloat162float(out[i]);
    // Denominator floor 1.0 (was 1e-5): outputs are O(sqrt(K)) ~ 10..100, but
    // a few elements are near-zero by CANCELLATION, and there cuBLAS vs our
    // kernel legitimately differ by accumulation ORDER (different tiles split
    // K differently) — tiny absolute diffs that explode as RELATIVE error
    // (seen on the 622M-element LM-heads: identical dumps yet rel>5%). Real
    // corruption (wrong tile/swizzle/barrier) shifts elements by O(10-100) and
    // still trips 5% against floor 1.0. DeepGEMM avoids the same artifact by
    // using a norm-based diff instead of per-element rel-err.
    double e = std::abs(r - o) / std::max(1.0, std::abs(r));
    if (e > max_e) {
      max_e = e;
      g_err_idx = i;
      g_err_ref = (float)r;
      g_err_out = (float)o;
    }
  }
  return max_e;
}

// ─── benchmark harness
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Result {
  double blublas_tflops;
  double cublas_tflops;
  double rel_err;
  bool pass;
};

// Global progress counter — how many test CASES (run_test_case calls) have
// finished. Printed as a leading [n] on every result row so a long run shows
// live progress (and you can tell it's not hung). Set g_cases_total in main to
// enable an [n/total] readout.
static int g_cases_done = 0;
static int g_cases_total = 0;

// Generic runner for any Config and Layout
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false,
          bool MulticastA = false>
static Result run_test_case(int M, int N, int K, int batchCount, float alpha,
                            float beta, cublasHandle_t cublas,
                            cudaStream_t stream) {
  // Determine dimensions based on layout
  long long elA = 0;
  long long elB = 0;
  const long long elC = (long long)batchCount * M * N;

  if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * N * K;
  } else { // TN
    elA = (long long)batchCount * K * M;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  }

  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hA(elA), hB(elB), hC_init(elC);
  fill_rand_bf16(hA, 42);
  fill_rand_bf16(hB, 99);

  // For beta != 0, initialize C with random values
  if (beta != 0.0f) {
    fill_rand_bf16(hC_init, 77);
  } else {
    std::fill(hC_init.begin(), hC_init.end(), __float2bfloat16(0.f));
  }

  __nv_bfloat16 *dA, *dB, *dC_ref, *dC_blu;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA, elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dA, hA.data(), elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, hB.data(), elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_ref, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_blu, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));

  // ── cuBLAS reference ────────
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
        cublas, transB, transA, // Swap due to column-major vs row-major
        N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb, strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF,
        (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF, N, (long long)M * N,
        batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  }

  // Run exactly one iteration of BluBridge for accuracy checking
  launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA>(
      dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Accuracy Check
  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hC_ref_h(elC), hC_blu_h(elC);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_ref_h.data(), dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_blu_h.data(), dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));

  double rel_err = max_rel_err(hC_ref_h, hC_blu_h);
  if (rel_err >= 0.05) {
    printf("  [DEBUG FAIL] worst element: idx=%zu (row %lld, col %lld)  "
           "ref=%.6f  out=%.6f  absdiff=%.6f\n",
           g_err_idx, (long long)(g_err_idx / N), (long long)(g_err_idx % N),
           g_err_ref, g_err_out, std::abs(g_err_ref - g_err_out));
    printf("  [DEBUG FAIL] First 10 elements:\n");
    printf("    Ref (cuBLAS): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_ref_h[i]));
    printf("\n    Blu (Template): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_blu_h[i]));
    printf("\n");
  }

  // Warmup BluBridge Cluster Template (5 iters)
  for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA>(
        dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Timed BluBridge Cluster Template (20 iters)
  cudaEvent_t t0, t1;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA>(
        dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K, batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());
  float blu_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&blu_ms, t0, t1));

  // Warmup + timed cuBLAS (20 iters)
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  }
  float cub_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&cub_ms, t0, t1));

  double flops = 2.0 * (double)M * N * K * batchCount;
  double iters = 20.0;
  double blu_tfl = flops * iters / (blu_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;
  double cub_tfl = flops * iters / (cub_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_ref));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_blu));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t1));

  ++g_cases_done; // one more test case finished (progress readout)
  return {blu_tfl, cub_tfl, rel_err, rel_err < 0.05};
}

// Struct to define dynamic test shape
struct Shape {
  int M, N, K, batch;
  float alpha, beta;
  const char *label;
};

// Layout name helper
static const char *layout_name(Sm103Layout layout) {
  switch (layout) {
  case Sm103Layout::NN:
    return "NN";
  case Sm103Layout::NT:
    return "NT";
  case Sm103Layout::TN:
    return "TN";
  }
  return "Unknown";
}

template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false,
          bool MulticastA = false>
static bool run_test_suite_for_layout_config(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                                             cublasHandle_t cublas,
                                             cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Testing Layout: %s | Config: %dx%dx%d (cta_group::2, %s wave, "
         "clusterN=%d, mcastA=%d) ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN, Config::BK,
         VerticalWave ? "vertical" : "horizontal", Config::CLUSTER_N,
         (int)MulticastA);
  printf("%-18s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s  %-9s  %-9s  %-7s  %-10s  %-6s  %s\n",
         "Shape", "M", "N", "K", "Batch", "alpha", "beta", "Template", "cuBLAS",
         "%cuBLAS", "MaxRelErr", "Status", "wall(ms)");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(116, '-').c_str());
  fflush(stdout); // flush the suite header NOW so a hang on the first kernel
                  // still shows which suite/layout we're in (frontier visible)

  int passed = 0;
  int total = 0;
  double suite_wall_ms = 0.0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    // 256x256x64 config requires M & N to be multiples of 256
    if (Config::BM == 256 && (s.M % 512 != 0 || s.N % 256 != 0)) {
      // Skip shapes that are not compatible with 256x256 config
      // Note: cluster height is 2*BM = 512, cluster width is BN = 256
      continue;
    }

    total++;
    // Per-test wall-clock (whole run_test_case: alloc + cuBLAS ref + accuracy
    // check + warmups + 20 timed iters of both). Includes host-side work, so
    // it's much larger than the pure-kernel Template/cuBLAS TFLOPS above.
    auto t_start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result r = run_test_case<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch, s.alpha, s.beta, cublas, stream);
    auto t_end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double wall_ms =
        std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t_end - t_start).count();
    suite_wall_ms += wall_ms;

    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-18s %5d %5d %5d %5d %5.1f %5.1f  %8.2f T  %8.2f T  "
           "%5.1f%%  "
           "%9.2e  %-6s  %8.1f\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch,
           s.alpha, s.beta, r.blublas_tflops, r.cublas_tflops,
           r.cublas_tflops > 0 ? r.blublas_tflops / r.cublas_tflops * 100 : 0.0,
           r.rel_err, r.pass ? "PASS" : "FAIL", wall_ms);
    fflush(stdout); // flush so progress is visible live during long runs

    if (r.pass)
      ++passed;
  }
  printf("Result: %d / %d PASSED   (suite wall time: %.1f ms)\n", passed, total,
         suite_wall_ms);
  fflush(stdout); // flush the suite Result so the log frontier is always exact
  return passed == total;
}

// ─── Qwen 42-shape sweep — P1 impact + dispatcher routing data
// ──────────────── For each real Qwen matmul shape (M=4096), run the 128×256
// tile in BOTH horizontal and vertical wave and compare to cuBLAS. Tells us,
// per shape, whether vertical helps (→ dispatcher routes it to vertical) and
// how close we are to cuBLAS. Correctness is validated by the suites above;
// here we focus on throughput, but still flag any accuracy miss.
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout>
static void run_qwen_sweep(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                           cublasHandle_t cublas, cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Qwen 42-shape sweep (%s, %dx%d tile): horizontal vs vertical "
         "vs cuBLAS ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN);
  printf("%-20s %-6s %7s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s  %-6s  %8s  %s\n", "Shape", "wave",
         "N", "K", "TFLOPS", "%cuB", "cuBLAS", "Status", "wall(ms)", "best");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  int vwins = 0, total = 0;
  double h_sum = 0, v_sum = 0, c_sum = 0;
  double sweep_wall_ms = 0.0; // total sweep wall-clock (whole run_test_case
                              // incl. host-side work, like the suites)
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    // One printed row PER test case (own [n/total], own TFLOPS/%/Status/wall)
    // — no combined row hiding the losing wave's numbers. Winner marked on the
    // vert row once both are known.
    auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result h = run_test_case<Config, Layout, false>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f,
                                                    0.0f, cublas, stream);
    auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double h_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t1 - t0).count();
    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-20s %-6s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-6s  "
           "%8.1f\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, "horiz", s.N, s.K,
           h.blublas_tflops, h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops * 100,
           h.cublas_tflops, h.pass ? "ok" : "FAIL", h_ms);
    fflush(stdout);
    auto t2 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result v = run_test_case<Config, Layout, true>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f,
                                                   cublas, stream);
    auto t3 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double v_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t3 - t2).count();
    bool vbest = v.blublas_tflops >= h.blublas_tflops;
    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-20s %-6s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-6s  "
           "%8.1f  best=%s\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, "vert", s.N, s.K,
           v.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops * 100,
           v.cublas_tflops, v.pass ? "ok" : "FAIL", v_ms,
           vbest ? "vert" : "horiz");
    fflush(stdout);
    sweep_wall_ms += h_ms + v_ms;
    if (vbest)
      ++vwins;
    ++total;
    h_sum += h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops;
    v_sum += v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops;
    c_sum += std::max(h.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops) / v.cublas_tflops;
  }
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  printf("vertical wins: %d / %d   avg%% of cuBLAS: horiz %.1f%%, vert %.1f%%, "
         "best-of-2 %.1f%%   (sweep wall time: %.1f s)\n",
         vwins, total, h_sum / total * 100, v_sum / total * 100,
         c_sum / total * 100, sweep_wall_ms / 1000.0);
}

int main() {
  int dev = 0;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDevice(&dev));
  cudaDeviceProp prop;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, dev));

  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");
  printf("SM103 Cluster GEMM Unified Template Test Suite\n");
  printf("Device : %s  (SM %d.%d)\n", prop.name, prop.major, prop.minor);
  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");

  if (prop.major != 10 || prop.minor != 3) {
    printf("[SKIP] SM103 Cluster GEMM template requires SM 10.3 (Blackwell "
           "Ultra/sm_103a).\n"
           "       This device is SM %d.%d (%s).\n"
           "       Tests skipped.\n",
           prop.major, prop.minor, prop.name);
    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
  }

  cudaStream_t stream;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamCreate(&stream));

  cublasHandle_t cublas;
  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasCreate(&cublas));
  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasSetStream(cublas, stream));

  // Test cases for 128x128x64 configuration (requires M % 256 == 0, N % 128 ==
  // 0, K % 64 == 0) Note: for BM=128, cluster height is 2*BM = 256. So M must
  // be a multiple of 256.
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_128 = {
      // M, N, K, batch, alpha, beta, label
      {256, 128, 64, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "tiny"},
      {256, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "small"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "medium"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "large"},
      // Multi-batch test
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-4"},
      {256, 256, 128, 8, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-8"},
      // Alpha/Beta scaling and accumulation tests
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.0f, "alpha-scaling"},
      {256, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.5f, "beta-accumulate"},
      {512, 512, 128, 2, 1.2f, 0.8f, "alpha-beta-batch"},
      // ── Comparison shapes vs legacy _cluster.cu B0 results (M=4096) ──
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-wideN-gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-skinny-K"}};

  // Test cases for 256x256x64 configuration (requires M % 512 == 0, N % 256 ==
  // 0, K % 64 == 0)
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_256 = {
      {512, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "tiny-256"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "small-256"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "medium-256"},
      // Multi-batch test
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-4-256"},
      // Alpha/Beta scaling and accumulation tests
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.5f, "alpha-beta-256"},
      // ── Comparison shapes vs legacy _cluster.cu B0 results (M=4096) ──
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-wideN-gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-skinny-K"}};

  bool all_passed = true;

  // Total test cases for the [done/total] progress readout. Keep in sync if the
  // suites below change: 128x128 (×3 layouts) + 128x256 (×3) + P1-vertical (×3)
  // + P2 2x2 (×3) + P2-M2 (×3) + Qwen sweep (42 shapes × 2 waves × 2 tiles).
  // shapes_2x2 has 7 shapes, qwen_shapes has 42 (defined below).
  // 2×2 (4-CTA) cluster suites are OPT-IN via RUN_2X2=1 (and RUN_2X2_MCAST=1
  // for the A-multicast suite). Both are VALIDATED bit-exact on B300
  // (2026-07-04, §30.11-30.12) — kept opt-in only to keep the default run
  // short.
  const bool run_2x2 = (getenv("RUN_2X2") != nullptr);
  const bool run_2x2_mcast = (getenv("RUN_2X2_MCAST") != nullptr);
  g_cases_total = (int)shapes_128.size() * 3 + (int)shapes_256.size() * 3 * 2 +
                  (run_2x2 ? 7 * 3 : 0) +
                  (run_2x2 && run_2x2_mcast ? 7 * 3 : 0) + 42 * 2 * 2;

  // 1. NN Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::NN>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NN>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 2. NT Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::NT>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NT>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 3. TN Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::TN>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::TN>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 4. P1 variant: 128×256 tile + VERTICAL wave (cuBLAS `128x256_2x1_v`).
  // Same tile/cluster as the 256 suites above, VerticalWave=true. Compare the
  // TFLOPS here vs the horizontal 256 suites on the same shapes to isolate the
  // wave-order effect (expected to help the M=4096 wide-N shapes via L2 reuse).
  printf("\n########## P1: 128x256 tile, VERTICAL wave (2x1) ##########\n");
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NN,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NT,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::TN,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // ── P2: 128×256 tile, 2×2 cluster (4-CTA) — Milestone 1 (redundant-A) ──
  // Correctness-first. Shapes have M%256==0 and N%512==0 so both N-blocks of
  // each cluster are valid (no partial-tile OOB). If these pass bit-exact, the
  // 4-CTA cluster + per-pair MMA + scheduler N-split are correct (§30).
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_2x2 = {
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-small"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-medium"},
      {2048, 2048, 512, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-large"},
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-batched"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.5f, "2x2-alpha-beta"},
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-wideN"}};
  if (run_2x2) {
    printf("\n########## P2: 128x256 tile, 2x2 cluster (4-CTA) ##########\n");
    all_passed &= run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                                   Sm103Layout::NN>(
        shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    all_passed &= run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                                   Sm103Layout::NT>(
        shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    all_passed &= run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                                   Sm103Layout::TN>(
        shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);

    // P2 Milestone 2: A-MULTICAST ON (load A once, multicast across N —
    // halves A DRAM traffic). VALIDATED bit-exact on B300 after the mbar
    // parity fix (leader mbar for even-parity routing, §30.11). Opt-in via
    // RUN_2X2_MCAST=1 only to keep the default run short.
    if (getenv("RUN_2X2_MCAST") != nullptr) {
      printf("\n########## P2-M2: 128x256 2x2 cluster, A-MULTICAST ON "
             "##########\n");
      all_passed &=
          run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                           Sm103Layout::NN, false, true>(
              shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
      all_passed &=
          run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                           Sm103Layout::NT, false, true>(
              shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
      all_passed &=
          run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                           Sm103Layout::TN, false, true>(
              shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    } else {
      printf("\n########## P2-M2 (A-MULTICAST) SKIPPED — redundant-A 2x2 above "
             "is correct; multicast is a deferred DRAM-opt (RUN_2X2_MCAST=1 to "
             "test) ##########\n");
    }
  } else {
    printf("\n########## P2 2x2 (4-CTA) SUITES SKIPPED (set RUN_2X2=1 to "
           "include; currently deadlocks on small grids — §30.x) ##########\n");
  }

  // ── Full Qwen matmul-shape sweep (42 shapes, M=4096) ──
  // (N, K) from analyzations.md §16.3. Runs 128×256 horizontal vs vertical vs
  // cuBLAS to measure P1 impact per shape + collect dispatcher routing data.
  const std::vector<Shape> qwen_shapes = {
      {4096, 896, 896, 1, 1, 0, "q25-0.5b-Q"},
      {4096, 128, 896, 1, 1, 0, "q25-0.5b-K"},
      {4096, 4864, 896, 1, 1, 0, "q25-0.5b-Gate"},
      {4096, 896, 4864, 1, 1, 0, "q25-0.5b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 896, 1, 1, 0, "q25-0.5b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 1536, 1536, 1, 1, 0, "q25-1.5b-Q"},
      {4096, 256, 1536, 1, 1, 0, "q25-1.5b-K"},
      {4096, 8960, 1536, 1, 1, 0, "q25-1.5b-Gate"},
      {4096, 1536, 8960, 1, 1, 0, "q25-1.5b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 1536, 1, 1, 0, "q25-1.5b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 2048, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-Q"},
      {4096, 256, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-K"},
      {4096, 11008, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-Gate"},
      {4096, 2048, 11008, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q25-3b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 3584, 3584, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-Q"},
      {4096, 512, 3584, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-K"},
      {4096, 18944, 3584, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-Gate"},
      {4096, 3584, 18944, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-Down"},
      {4096, 152064, 3584, 1, 1, 0, "q25-7b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 2048, 1024, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-Q"},
      {4096, 1024, 1024, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-K"},
      {4096, 1024, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-O"},
      {4096, 3072, 1024, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-Gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 3072, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 1024, 1, 1, 0, "q3-0.6b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 2048, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-1.7b-Q"},
      {4096, 1024, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-1.7b-K"},
      {4096, 6144, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-1.7b-Gate"},
      {4096, 2048, 6144, 1, 1, 0, "q3-1.7b-Down"},
      {4096, 151936, 2048, 1, 1, 0, "q3-1.7b-LMhead"},
      {4096, 4096, 2560, 1, 1, 0, "q3-4b-Q"},
      {4096, 1024, 2560, 1, 1, 0, "q3-4b-K"},
      {4096, 2560, 4096, 1, 1, 0, "q3-4b-O"},

All **336/336 PASSED, zero failures** — the 2×2f variant is **correctness-validated** on the first run (both A-modes, all layouts, mixed granted cluster sizes handled right). Full honesty on the performance picture though:

## Correctness: complete ✅
Every suite green, `0.00e+00` everywhere, and the launch-mechanism change is proven safe (all rigid variants unchanged: square4096 still 96–98%).

## Performance: M1 is slower — expected, and diagnostic

| shape | P2 rigid 2×2 | P3 dynamic (M1) |
|---|---|---|
| 2x2-square4096 | 96.4–98.2% | **81.7%** |
| 2x2-wideN | ~91% | **70.5%** |

This gap is **not** the dynamic-cluster feature — it's the **M1 restriction**: with CLC stealing disabled, each cluster computes exactly one tile-unit and exits. That means the kernel pays the full prologue (tmem alloc, barrier init, cluster sync, pipeline warm-up) **per tile** instead of once per SM residency, and loses tail load-balancing. That cost (~16–20 points) swamps the occupancy win.

**Conclusion (measured, not guessed): CLC persistence is worth ~15–20% on big shapes — so M2 (CLC under dynamic clusters) is required for 2×2f to be competitive, exactly as cuBLAS runs it.**

## M2 design insight (from this data)

The clean way to make CLC safe under mixed granted sizes, without depending on the unverified cancellation-alignment contract: **make the work unit the preferred unit, and let a fallback-granted (2-CTA) cluster process the stolen unit's two N-blocks *sequentially*** (granted-4 does them in parallel across its 2 pairs). Any stealer then covers the whole stolen unit — no tile can be orphaned regardless of how the hardware aligns cancellations. That's the M2 implementation plan.

So: 2×2f M1 = done and validated; M2 (CLC + sequential-fallback work model) is the next block. Want me to proceed with M2 now, or park 2×2f here and knock out the simpler remaining variants first (1×2, extra tiles) and return to M2 after?

### CLAUDE [2026-07-04 18:02 IST]

Good question — let me be straight about it, because right now the numbers **don't** show a win yet.

## What 2×2f is *supposed* to beat, and why

The comparison is **2×2f vs the rigid 2×2** (not vs 2×1):

- **Rigid 2×2** demands 4 CTAs placed *together* as one cluster. B300 has 148 SMs → 148/4 = only **33 clusters fit → 132 SMs busy, 16 SMs sit idle** (89% of the GPU). That waste is structural — every wave, forever.
- **2×2f** says: *prefer* 4-CTA clusters, but where a 4-slot doesn't fit, *fall back* to 2-CTA clusters and use those leftover SMs → **74 clusters → all 148 SMs busy (100%)**.

So the theoretical prize is that ~**11% more hardware doing work** on big shapes, at the cost that fallback clusters lose the cross-pair A-sharing. That's why it's cuBLAS's pick for exactly the largest Qwen shapes — we measured this from cuBLAS's own launches (33 vs 74 active clusters).

## Why OUR numbers show 81% instead of a win

What we validated today is **M1 = correctness only, with one hand tied behind its back**: I deliberately disabled CLC (the persistent "grab the next tile" scheduler) for the dynamic variant, because one hardware behavior under mixed cluster sizes is still unverified. Without CLC, every cluster does ONE tile then dies — so the kernel pays its whole startup cost (tmem alloc, barriers, pipeline warm-up) **per tile** instead of once. ### CLAUDE [2026-07-04 18:03 IST]

Yes — exactly. M2 is the step that makes it actually fast. Simple picture:

## What the f-variant needs to win

Two ingredients, **both together**:

1. **100% SM fill** (all 148 SMs busy) ← we got this today with the fallback-cluster launch ✅
2. **Persistence** (each cluster stays alive and keeps grabbing new tiles via CLC, paying startup cost only once) ← **this is what M1 turned OFF** ❌

Today's run proved each ingredient's worth separately: rigid 2×2 has persistence but only 89% fill → ~97%. Dynamic M1 has 100% fill but no persistence → 82%. **cuBLAS's crown jewel has both** — that's the target.

## What M2 concretely is

Re-enable CLC (tile stealing) on the dynamic kernel — but that has the one danger I flagged: when a cluster steals a pending tile-unit, the stolen unit is sized for a **4-CTA** cluster (2 N-blocks of work). If the *stealer* happens to be a **2-CTA fallback** cluster, it only has one MMA pair — it can naturally cover only 1 of the 2 N-blocks → the other would be silently lost (exactly the missing-tile class of bug we just spent a day killing).

**M2's fix — make any stealer cover the whole unit:**

- a **4-CTA** cluster does the stolen unit's 2 N-blocks **in parallel** (one per pair — same as today), 
- a **2-CTA** fallback cluster does them **sequentially** (its single pair loops: N-block 0, then N-block 1).

Either way the stolen unit is *fully* computed, no matter what the hardware's cancellation alignment turns out to be — we don't have to trust the unverified contract at all.

## The work involved

Mostly in the producer/consumer/epilogue loops: for a fallback-granted cluster, an inner "2 iterations per tile-unit" loop (second iteration shifts `block_col` by one BN). Barriers/pipeline stay as-is — it's the same pattern as processing two consecutive CLC tiles, which the code already does. Then validate: full suites + LM-heads repeatedly (our missing-tile detector), and compare P3 vs P2 TFLOPS — expecting P3 ≥ P2 on square4096/wideN if the theory holds.

// test_clc_dynamic_probe.cu
// Device probe: CLC try_cancel semantics under a PREFERRED(4)/FALLBACK(2)
// cluster launch on B300 (sm_103a). Answers the M2 design question (§31.2):
//
//   When a cluster steals a pending cluster via clusterlaunchcontrol.
//   try_cancel, what is the CANCELLED UNIT's size/alignment?
//     (B) always a full PREFERRED unit  → first_ctaid % 4 == 0 always
//     (D) sized like the REQUESTER      → fallback stealers see % 4 == 2 too
//
//   Also measures: how many clusters get granted PREFERRED (4) vs FALLBACK
//   (2) on this GPU — the occupancy story (cuBLAS f-kernel: 74×2 vs 33×4).
//
// Usage:  ./build/test_clc_dynamic_probe
// Safe to run on a busy GPU (tiny kernel, ~2s).

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                       \
  do {                                                                         \
    cudaError_t e = (call);                                                    \
    if (e != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \
      fprintf(stderr, "CUDA error %s at %s:%d\n", cudaGetErrorString(e),       \
              __FILE__, __LINE__);                                             \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

// Record: x = type (0=cluster-launch record, 1=steal record)
//         y = granted cluster size (%cluster_nctaid.x of the recorder)
//         z = type0: first blockIdx of this cluster | type1: cancelled ctaid
//         w = type0: 0                              | type1: cancelled ctaid %
//         PREFERRED
struct Rec {
  int type, granted, ctaid, misalign;
};

__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned p_cluster_nctas() {
  unsigned n;
  asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_nctaid.x;" : "=r"(n));
  return n;
}
__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned p_cluster_rank() {
  unsigned r;
  asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctarank;" : "=r"(r));
  return r;
}
__device__ __forceinline__ void p_mbar_init(unsigned addr, int count) {
  asm volatile("mbarrier.init.shared::cta.b64 [%0], %1;" ::"r"(addr),
               "r"(count));
}
__device__ __forceinline__ void p_mbar_arrive_expect(unsigned addr, int tx) {
  asm volatile("mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx.release.cta.shared::cta.b64 _, "
               "[%0], %1;" ::"r"(addr),
               "r"(tx)
               : "memory");
}
__device__ __forceinline__ void p_mbar_wait(unsigned addr, int phase) {
  unsigned ticks = 0x989680;
  asm volatile("{\n\t"
               ".reg .pred P;\n\t"
               "LAB_WAIT:\n\t"
               "mbarrier.try_wait.parity.acquire.cta.shared::cta.b64 P, [%0], "
               "%1, %2;\n\t"
               "@P bra.uni DONE;\n\t"
               "bra.uni LAB_WAIT;\n\t"
               "DONE:\n\t"
               "}" ::"r"(addr),
               "r"(phase), "r"(ticks));
}
// NON-multicast try_cancel: response + completion land on THIS CTA only, so
// peer CTAs need no barrier participation (multicast::all would require every
// cluster CTA to arm/consume).
__device__ __forceinline__ void p_clc_try_cancel(unsigned resp, unsigned mbar) {
  asm volatile("clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel.async.shared::cta"
               ".mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.b128 [%0], [%1];" ::"r"(resp),
               "r"(mbar)
               : "memory");
}
__device__ __forceinline__ void p_clc_query(unsigned resp, unsigned &valid,
                                            unsigned &ctaid) {
  asm volatile("{\n\t"
               ".reg .b128 handle;\n\t"
               ".reg .pred p;\n\t"
               "mov.s32 %0, 0;\n\t"
               "ld.shared.b128 handle, [%2];\n\t"
               "clusterlaunchcontrol.query_cancel.is_canceled.pred.b128 p, "
               "handle;\n\t"
               "@p mov.s32 %0, 1;\n\t"
               "clusterlaunchcontrol.query_cancel.get_first_ctaid::x.b32.b128 "
               "%1, handle;\n\t"
               "}"
               : "=r"(valid), "=r"(ctaid)
               : "r"(resp)
               : "memory");
}
__device__ __forceinline__ void p_cluster_sync() {
  asm volatile("barrier.cluster.arrive.release.aligned;\n"
               "barrier.cluster.wait.acquire.aligned;\n" ::
                   : "memory");
}

__global__ void __launch_bounds__(32)
    clc_probe_kernel(Rec *out, int *out_n, int max_out, long long spin_cycles,
                     int preferred) {
  __shared__ __align__(16) unsigned char resp[16];
  __shared__ __align__(8) unsigned long long mbar[1];
  const unsigned granted = p_cluster_nctas();
  const unsigned rank = p_cluster_rank();
  const unsigned resp_a = (unsigned)__cvta_generic_to_shared(resp);
  const unsigned mbar_a = (unsigned)__cvta_generic_to_shared(mbar);

  if (rank == 0 && threadIdx.x == 0) {
    p_mbar_init(mbar_a, 1);
    // one record per CLUSTER: granted size + where it sits in the grid
    int i = atomicAdd(out_n, 1);
    if (i < max_out)
      out[i] = {0, (int)granted, (int)blockIdx.x,
                (int)(blockIdx.x % preferred)};
  }
  p_cluster_sync();

  // burn time so later clusters stay PENDING and steals actually happen
  long long t0 = clock64();
  while (clock64() - t0 < spin_cycles)
    ;

  if (rank == 0 && threadIdx.x == 0) {
    int phase = 0;
    while (true) {
      p_mbar_arrive_expect(mbar_a, 16);
      p_clc_try_cancel(resp_a, mbar_a);
      p_mbar_wait(mbar_a, phase);
      phase ^= 1;
      unsigned valid, ctaid;
      p_clc_query(resp_a, valid, ctaid);
      if (!valid)
        break;
      int i = atomicAdd(out_n, 1);
      if (i < max_out)
        out[i] = {1, (int)granted, (int)ctaid, (int)(ctaid % preferred)};
    }
  }
  p_cluster_sync();
}

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, 0));
  printf("Device: %s (SM %d.%d, %d SMs)\n", prop.name, prop.major, prop.minor,

  if (prop.major != 10 || prop.minor != 3) {

  const int PREFERRED = 4, FALLBACK = 2;
  const int UNITS = 2048; // pending pool ≫ resident capacity
  const int GRID = UNITS * PREFERRED;

  Rec *d_out;
  int *d_n;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&d_out, MAX_OUT * sizeof(Rec)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&d_n, sizeof(int)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemset(d_n, 0, sizeof(int)));

  cudaLaunchConfig_t cfg = {};
  cfg.gridDim = dim3(GRID);
  cfg.blockDim = dim3(32);
  cudaLaunchAttribute attrs[2] = {};
  attrs[0].id = cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension;
  attrs[0].val.clusterDim.x = FALLBACK;
  attrs[0].val.clusterDim.y = 1;

  if (n > MAX_OUT)

  long launch_mis[2] = {0, 0}; // fallback clusters at offset 0 vs 2
  long steals[2][2] = {{0, 0},

  long steal_mis_vals[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {

    } else {

  }
  printf("\n=== LAUNCH GRANTS ===\n");
  printf("clusters granted FALLBACK(2): %ld  (at preferred-offset 0: %ld, "

The probe delivered a **decisive, beautiful result** — and it's the answer I *couldn't* get from CUTLASS's source:

## Measured contract (hypothesis D confirmed)
- **Preferred-4 stealers: 1686 steals, 100% aligned** (`%4==0`) — they always cancel full 4-CTA units
- **Fallback-2 stealers: 66 aligned + 66 at `%4==2`** — they cancel **requester-sized 2-CTA pieces**, either half of a preferred unit
- **Accounting closes EXACTLY**: 296 launched units + 1686 stolen units + 66 stolen half-unit-pairs (132 halves ÷ 2) = **2048/2048** — no unit lost, none double-issued

**The hardware hands each stealer exactly as much work as it can chew.** That makes M2 *simpler* than my sequential-loop plan: no loop needed — a fallback stealer's piece is one N-block, and the piece's position is encoded in the response ctaid. The unified decode (works for static AND dynamic):

```
n_sub = ((new_ctaid % CLUSTER_CTAS) >> 1) + cta_n_grant
```

M2 is in and compiles clean. Now your question — it's a good design check, here's the honest reasoning:

## Did removing the M1 blocks lose anything we might want later?

**No — M1's "CLC off" was scaffolding, not a feature.** Its only purpose was to validate the dynamic-cluster machinery in isolation *while* the steal contract was unverified. Both reasons are now gone: the machinery is validated (42/42) and the contract is measured (probe §31.3). And crucially, we **measured** what CLC-off costs: 81.7% vs 97% — it loses by 15–20 points on big shapes and wins nowhere (on small grids there are no steals anyway, so CLC costs ~one `try_cancel` round-trip per cluster — negligible; all our tiny-shape suites prove it). A variant that's strictly worse on every shape would never be picked by the dispatcher.

## Should it be a knob anyway?

Deliberately **no**, and this is our knob philosophy applied consistently: we make something a parameter when the benchmark might pick *either side* per shape (wave order, tile, cluster N, multicast, dynamic — all genuinely shape-dependent). A `UseCLC` knob fails that test — one side always loses — so it would be dead weight: it **doubles the test matrix** (every suite × CLC on/off) for zero routing value. That's the real overhead to avoid, not the runtime one.

If a future variant genuinely needs non-persistence (say, a tiny-shape latency special), recovery is trivial: the M1 form is documented in §31.2 and in git history, and re-adding the knob is a 10-minute mechanical change (it was 3 `if constexpr` lines + a gate). We're not burning a bridge; we're just not carrying an unused one.

## Is CLC itself overhead? Are we correct?

- **Cost**: one scheduler warp + 2 small mbarriers + 1 outstanding steal request per cluster. **Measured benefit**: +15–20% on large shapes (persistence amortizes the per-tile prologue). This is why cuBLAS and CUTLASS ship CLC-persistent kernels universally on Blackwell — it's the standard, not an exotic add-on.
- **Correctness**: our CLC now matches CUTLASS's one-outstanding protocol (§30.12, fixed the orphan bug), and the M2 mixed-size handling follows the **hardware-measured** contract (requester-sized pieces, position from response ctaid, unit accounting closing 2048/2048 exactly). The LM-head sweep remains our missing-tile detector on every run.
