// test_bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cu
// Comprehensive accuracy and benchmark test suite for the unified SM103a
// Cluster GEMM template. Target: NVIDIA B300 (SM 10.3a) —
// tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16
//
// Usage:
//   make run TEST=examples/test_bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cu
//

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cublas_v2.h>
#include <cuda_bf16.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <numeric>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

// Include the unified SM103 cluster template
#include "../src/level3/batched_gemm/BF16/SM103/Bgemm_sm103_cluster_template.cuh"

// ─── error helpers
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#define CHECK_CUDA(call)                                                       \
  do {                                                                         \
    cudaError_t e = (call);                                                    \
    if (e != cudaSuccess) {                                                    \
      fprintf(stderr, "CUDA error %s at %s:%d\n", cudaGetErrorString(e),       \
              __FILE__, __LINE__);                                             \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

#define CHECK_CUBLAS(call)                                                     \
  do {                                                                         \
    cublasStatus_t e = (call);                                                 \
    if (e != CUBLAS_STATUS_SUCCESS) {                                          \
      fprintf(stderr, "cuBLAS error %d at %s:%d\n", (int)e, __FILE__,          \
              __LINE__);                                                       \
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                      \
    }                                                                          \
  } while (0)

// ─── data init
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static void fill_rand_bf16(std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &v, unsigned seed) {
  srand(seed);
  for (auto &x : v)
    x = __float2bfloat16((float(rand()) / RAND_MAX) * 2.f - 1.f);
}

// ─── accuracy check
// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Worst-element info from the last max_rel_err call (printed on FAIL so we
// can SEE whether a failure is real corruption or a near-zero cancellation
// artifact).
static size_t g_err_idx = 0;
static float g_err_ref = 0.f, g_err_out = 0.f;

static double max_rel_err(const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &ref,
                          const std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> &out) {
  double max_e = 0.0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < ref.size(); ++i) {
    double r = __bfloat162float(ref[i]);
    double o = __bfloat162float(out[i]);
    // Denominator floor 1.0 (was 1e-5): outputs are O(sqrt(K)) ~ 10..100, but
    // a few elements are near-zero by CANCELLATION, and there cuBLAS vs our
    // kernel legitimately differ by accumulation ORDER (different tiles split
    // K differently) — tiny absolute diffs that explode as RELATIVE error
    // (seen on the 622M-element LM-heads: identical dumps yet rel>5%). Real
    // corruption (wrong tile/swizzle/barrier) shifts elements by O(10-100) and
    // still trips 5% against floor 1.0. DeepGEMM avoids the same artifact by
    // using a norm-based diff instead of per-element rel-err.
    double e = std::abs(r - o) / std::max(1.0, std::abs(r));
    if (e > max_e) {
      max_e = e;
      g_err_idx = i;
      g_err_ref = (float)r;
      g_err_out = (float)o;
    }
  }
  return max_e;
}

// ─── benchmark harness
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Result {
  double blublas_tflops;
  double cublas_tflops;
  double rel_err;
  bool pass;
};

// Global progress counter — how many test CASES (run_test_case calls) have
// finished. Printed as a leading [n] on every result row so a long run shows
// live progress (and you can tell it's not hung). Set g_cases_total in main to
// enable an [n/total] readout.
static int g_cases_done = 0;
static int g_cases_total = 0;

// Generic runner for any Config and Layout
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false,
          bool MulticastA = false, bool DynamicCluster = false>
static Result run_test_case(int M, int N, int K, int batchCount, float alpha,
                            float beta, cublasHandle_t cublas,
                            cudaStream_t stream) {
  // Determine dimensions based on layout
  long long elA = 0;
  long long elB = 0;
  const long long elC = (long long)batchCount * M * N;

  if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
    elA = (long long)batchCount * M * K;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * N * K;
  } else { // TN
    elA = (long long)batchCount * K * M;
    elB = (long long)batchCount * K * N;
  }

  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hA(elA), hB(elB), hC_init(elC);
  fill_rand_bf16(hA, 42);
  fill_rand_bf16(hB, 99);

  // For beta != 0, initialize C with random values
  if (beta != 0.0f) {
    fill_rand_bf16(hC_init, 77);
  } else {
    std::fill(hC_init.begin(), hC_init.end(), __float2bfloat16(0.f));
  }

  __nv_bfloat16 *dA, *dB, *dC_ref, *dC_blu;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA, elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dA, hA.data(), elA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, hB.data(), elB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_ref, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dC_blu, hC_init.data(), elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));

  // ── cuBLAS reference ────────
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
        cublas, transB, transA, // Swap due to column-major vs row-major
        N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb, strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF,
        (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF, N, (long long)M * N,
        batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  }

  // Run exactly one iteration of BluBridge for accuracy checking
  launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA,
                             DynamicCluster>(dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K,
                                             batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Accuracy Check
  std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> hC_ref_h(elC), hC_blu_h(elC);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_ref_h.data(), dC_ref, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(hC_blu_h.data(), dC_blu, elC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                        cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));

  double rel_err = max_rel_err(hC_ref_h, hC_blu_h);
  if (rel_err >= 0.05) {
    printf("  [DEBUG FAIL] worst element: idx=%zu (row %lld, col %lld)  "
           "ref=%.6f  out=%.6f  absdiff=%.6f\n",
           g_err_idx, (long long)(g_err_idx / N), (long long)(g_err_idx % N),
           g_err_ref, g_err_out, std::abs(g_err_ref - g_err_out));
    printf("  [DEBUG FAIL] First 10 elements:\n");
    printf("    Ref (cuBLAS): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_ref_h[i]));
    printf("\n    Blu (Template): ");
    for (int i = 0; i < std::min(10, (int)elC); ++i)
      printf("%.4f ", __bfloat162float(hC_blu_h[i]));
    printf("\n");
  }

  // Warmup BluBridge Cluster Template (5 iters)
  for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA,
                               DynamicCluster>(dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K,
                                               batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());

  // Timed BluBridge Cluster Template (20 iters)
  cudaEvent_t t0, t1;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
  for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA,
                               DynamicCluster>(dA, dB, dC_blu, M, N, K,
                                               batchCount, alpha, beta, stream);
  }
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());
  float blu_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&blu_ms, t0, t1));

  // Warmup + timed cuBLAS (20 iters)
  {
    float fa = alpha, fb = beta;
    cublasOperation_t transA, transB;
    long long lda, ldb, strideA, strideB;

    if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NN) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = K;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    } else if (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      lda = K;
      ldb = K;
      strideA = (long long)M * K;
      strideB = (long long)N * K;
    } else { // TN
      transA = CUBLAS_OP_T;
      transB = CUBLAS_OP_N;
      lda = M;
      ldb = N;
      strideA = (long long)K * M;
      strideB = (long long)K * N;
    }

    for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) {
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, transB, transA, N, M, K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)ldb,
          strideB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, (int)lda, strideA, &fb, dC_ref, CUDA_R_16BF,
          N, (long long)M * N, batchCount, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
          CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    }
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  }
  float cub_ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&cub_ms, t0, t1));

  double flops = 2.0 * (double)M * N * K * batchCount;
  double iters = 20.0;
  double blu_tfl = flops * iters / (blu_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;
  double cub_tfl = flops * iters / (cub_ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_ref));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC_blu));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t1));

  ++g_cases_done; // one more test case finished (progress readout)
  return {blu_tfl, cub_tfl, rel_err, rel_err < 0.05};
}

// Struct to define dynamic test shape
struct Shape {
  int M, N, K, batch;
  float alpha, beta;
  const char *label;
};

// Layout name helper
static const char *layout_name(Sm103Layout layout) {
  switch (layout) {
  case Sm103Layout::NN:
    return "NN";
  case Sm103Layout::NT:
    return "NT";
  case Sm103Layout::TN:
    return "TN";
  }
  return "Unknown";
}

template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false,
          bool MulticastA = false, bool DynamicCluster = false>
static bool run_test_suite_for_layout_config(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                                             cublasHandle_t cublas,
                                             cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Testing Layout: %s | Config: %dx%dx%d (cta_group::2, %s wave, "
         "clusterN=%d, mcastA=%d, dyn=%d) ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN, Config::BK,
         VerticalWave ? "vertical" : "horizontal", Config::CLUSTER_N,
         (int)MulticastA, (int)DynamicCluster);
  printf("%-18s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s %5s  %-9s  %-9s  %-7s  %-10s  %-6s  %s\n",
         "Shape", "M", "N", "K", "Batch", "alpha", "beta", "Template", "cuBLAS",
         "%cuBLAS", "MaxRelErr", "Status", "wall(ms)");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(116, '-').c_str());
  fflush(stdout); // flush the suite header NOW so a hang on the first kernel
                  // still shows which suite/layout we're in (frontier visible)

  int passed = 0;
  int total = 0;
  double suite_wall_ms = 0.0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    // Batched partial-M cluster tiles are unsupported by design: the C TMA
    // store clips only at the TENSOR edge (batchCount*M rows), so a batch's
    // OOB tail rows would land in the NEXT batch's region. Single-batch
    // partial-M is fine (TMA OOB zero-fill + edge clip) and MUST be tested.
    // (Replaces a legacy BM==256 modulo skip that silently dropped the
    // cm256-partialM case — dead code before B1 since no config had BM=256.)
    if (s.batch > 1 && s.M % (Config::CLUSTER_SIZE * Config::OUT_ROWS) != 0)
      continue;

    total++;
    // Per-test wall-clock (whole run_test_case: alloc + cuBLAS ref + accuracy
    // check + warmups + 20 timed iters of both). Includes host-side work, so
    // it's much larger than the pure-kernel Template/cuBLAS TFLOPS above.
    auto t_start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result r =
        run_test_case<Config, Layout, VerticalWave, MulticastA, DynamicCluster>(
            s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch, s.alpha, s.beta, cublas, stream);
    auto t_end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double wall_ms =
        std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t_end - t_start).count();
    suite_wall_ms += wall_ms;

    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-18s %5d %5d %5d %5d %5.1f %5.1f  %8.2f T  %8.2f T  "
           "%5.1f%%  "
           "%9.2e  %-6s  %8.1f\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, s.M, s.N, s.K, s.batch,
           s.alpha, s.beta, r.blublas_tflops, r.cublas_tflops,
           r.cublas_tflops > 0 ? r.blublas_tflops / r.cublas_tflops * 100 : 0.0,
           r.rel_err, r.pass ? "PASS" : "FAIL", wall_ms);
    fflush(stdout); // flush so progress is visible live during long runs

    if (r.pass)
      ++passed;
  }
  printf("Result: %d / %d PASSED   (suite wall time: %.1f ms)\n", passed, total,
         suite_wall_ms);
  fflush(stdout); // flush the suite Result so the log frontier is always exact
  return passed == total;
}

// ─── Qwen 42-shape sweep — P1 impact + dispatcher routing data
// ──────────────── For each real Qwen matmul shape (M=4096), run the 128×256
// tile in BOTH horizontal and vertical wave and compare to cuBLAS. Tells us,
// per shape, whether vertical helps (→ dispatcher routes it to vertical) and
// how close we are to cuBLAS. Correctness is validated by the suites above;
// here we focus on throughput, but still flag any accuracy miss.
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout>
static void run_qwen_sweep(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                           cublasHandle_t cublas, cudaStream_t stream) {
  printf("\n=== Qwen 42-shape sweep (%s, %dx%d tile): horizontal vs vertical "
         "vs cuBLAS ===\n",
         layout_name(Layout), Config::BM, Config::BN);
  printf("%-20s %-6s %7s %6s   %8s %6s   %8s  %-6s  %8s  %s\n", "Shape", "wave",
         "N", "K", "TFLOPS", "%cuB", "cuBLAS", "Status", "wall(ms)", "best");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  int vwins = 0, total = 0;
  double h_sum = 0, v_sum = 0, c_sum = 0;
  double sweep_wall_ms = 0.0; // total sweep wall-clock (whole run_test_case
                              // incl. host-side work, like the suites)
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    // One printed row PER test case (own [n/total], own TFLOPS/%/Status/wall)
    // — no combined row hiding the losing wave's numbers. Winner marked on the
    // vert row once both are known.
    auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result h = run_test_case<Config, Layout, false>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f,
                                                    0.0f, cublas, stream);
    auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double h_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t1 - t0).count();
    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-20s %-6s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-6s  "
           "%8.1f\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, "horiz", s.N, s.K,
           h.blublas_tflops, h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops * 100,
           h.cublas_tflops, h.pass ? "ok" : "FAIL", h_ms);
    fflush(stdout);
    auto t2 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    Result v = run_test_case<Config, Layout, true>(s.M, s.N, s.K, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f,
                                                   cublas, stream);
    auto t3 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    double v_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t3 - t2).count();
    bool vbest = v.blublas_tflops >= h.blublas_tflops;
    printf("[%3d/%3d] %-20s %-6s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%   %7.1fT  %-6s  "
           "%8.1f  best=%s\n",
           g_cases_done, g_cases_total, s.label, "vert", s.N, s.K,
           v.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops * 100,
           v.cublas_tflops, v.pass ? "ok" : "FAIL", v_ms,
           vbest ? "vert" : "horiz");
    fflush(stdout);
    sweep_wall_ms += h_ms + v_ms;
    if (vbest)
      ++vwins;
    ++total;
    h_sum += h.blublas_tflops / h.cublas_tflops;
    v_sum += v.blublas_tflops / v.cublas_tflops;
    c_sum += std::max(h.blublas_tflops, v.blublas_tflops) / v.cublas_tflops;
  }
  printf("%s\n", std::string(96, '-').c_str());
  printf("vertical wins: %d / %d   avg%% of cuBLAS: horiz %.1f%%, vert %.1f%%, "
         "best-of-2 %.1f%%   (sweep wall time: %.1f s)\n",
         vwins, total, h_sum / total * 100, v_sum / total * 100,
         c_sum / total * 100, sweep_wall_ms / 1000.0);
}

// ── B5: best-variant benchmark (RUN_BENCH=1) ─────────────────────────────
// For each Qwen shape (TN, batch 1), time cuBLAS once and EVERY validated
// variant (tile x wave x cluster x dynamic x swap), then print the winner.
// Perf-only: correctness is covered by the suites above (all bit-exact).
template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool V = false, bool MC = false,
          bool DY = false>
static double bench_one(int M, int N, int K, const __nv_bfloat16 *dA,
                        const __nv_bfloat16 *dB, __nv_bfloat16 *dC,
                        cudaStream_t stream) {
  for (int w = 0; w < 3; ++w)
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, V, MC, DY>(
        dA, dB, dC, M, N, K, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, stream);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError());
  cudaEvent_t t0, t1;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
  for (int i = 0; i < 10; ++i)
    launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster<Config, Layout, V, MC, DY>(
        dA, dB, dC, M, N, K, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, stream);
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
  float ms = 0.f;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&ms, t0, t1));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t0));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t1));
  return 2.0 * (double)M * N * K * 10.0 / (ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;
}

static void run_best_variant_bench(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                                   cublasHandle_t cublas, cudaStream_t stream) {
  const int NS = (int)shapes.size();
  printf("\n=== B5 bench, VARIANT-MAJOR: each variant swept over all %d "
         "shapes (TN, batch 1) ===\n",
         NS);
  // One max-size buffer set reused by EVERY (variant, shape) timing: no
  // alloc churn between measurements, identical memory conditions for all.
  long long maxA = 0, maxB = 0, maxC = 0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    maxA = std::max(maxA, (long long)s.K * s.M);
    maxB = std::max(maxB, (long long)s.K * s.N);
    maxC = std::max(maxC, (long long)s.M * s.N);
  }
  __nv_bfloat16 *dA, *dB, *dC;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA, maxA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, maxB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC, maxC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  {
    std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> h(maxA);
    fill_rand_bf16(h, 42);
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dA, h.data(), maxA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                          cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  }
  {
    std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> h(maxB);
    fill_rand_bf16(h, 99);
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, h.data(), maxB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                          cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  }

  // cuBLAS timing helper (5 warmup + 20 timed)
  auto time_cublas = [&](const Shape &s) -> double {
    const long long elA = (long long)s.K * s.M, elB = (long long)s.K * s.N,
                    elC = (long long)s.M * s.N;
    float fa = 1.0f, fb = 0.0f;
    for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w)
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, CUBLAS_OP_N, CUBLAS_OP_T, s.N, s.M, s.K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF,
          s.N, elB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, s.M, elA, &fb, dC, CUDA_R_16BF, s.N, elC,
          1, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    cudaEvent_t t0, t1;
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t0));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t1));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i)
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, CUBLAS_OP_N, CUBLAS_OP_T, s.N, s.M, s.K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF,
          s.N, elB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, s.M, elA, &fb, dC, CUDA_R_16BF, s.N, elC,
          1, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
    float ms = 0.f;
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&ms, t0, t1));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t0));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t1));
    return 2.0 * (double)s.M * s.N * s.K * 20.0 / (ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;
  };

  // ── preheat to thermal steady state ──────────────────────────────────────
  // Even with -lgc, the MEMORY clock / HBM thermals decay ~10% over the first
  // ~2 minutes (seen as a monotone drift gradient: early-baseline shapes
  // -14%, late ~0 — §47.4). Burn heavy GEMMs until equilibrium so EVERY
  // measurement (baseline, variants, recheck) sees the same conditions.
  {
    int hot = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < NS; ++i)
      if ((double)shapes[i].M * shapes[i].N * shapes[i].K >
          (double)shapes[hot].M * shapes[hot].N * shapes[hot].K)
        hot = i;
    printf("\npreheating: 60s of %s ...\n", shapes[hot].label);
    fflush(stdout);
    const auto t_begin = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const Shape &h = shapes[hot];
    const long long helA = (long long)h.K * h.M, helB = (long long)h.K * h.N,
                    helC = (long long)h.M * h.N;
    float fa = 1.0f, fb = 0.0f;
    while (std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() -
                                         t_begin)
               .count() < 60.0) {
      for (int i = 0; i < 10; ++i)
        CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
            cublas, CUBLAS_OP_N, CUBLAS_OP_T, h.N, h.M, h.K, &fa, dB,
            CUDA_R_16BF, h.N, helB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, h.M, helA, &fb, dC,
            CUDA_R_16BF, h.N, helC, 1, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
            CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
      CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    }
    printf("preheat done.\n");
    fflush(stdout);
  }

  // ── pass 0: cuBLAS baseline, one clean sweep ──────────────────────────────
  std::vector<double> cub(NS);
  std::vector<double> best(NS, 0.0);
  std::vector<const char *> bestname(NS, "-");
  printf("\n--- cuBLAS baseline (42-shape sweep) ---\n");
  for (int i = 0; i < NS; ++i) {
    cub[i] = time_cublas(shapes[i]);
    printf("  %-20s %7d %6d   %8.1f T\n", shapes[i].label, shapes[i].N,
           shapes[i].K, cub[i]);
    fflush(stdout);
  }

  // ── per-variant 42-shape sweeps ───────────────────────────────────────────
#define BENCH_VARIANT(LBL, CFG, VW, MC, DY)                                    \
  {                                                                            \
    printf("\n=== variant %-16s: %d-shape sweep ===\n", LBL, NS);              \
    printf("%-20s %7s %6s   %8s %6s\n", "Shape", "N", "K", "TFLOPS", "%cuB");  \
    double rsum = 0.0;                                                         \
    int vwins = 0;                                                             \
    for (int i = 0; i < NS; ++i) {                                             \
      const Shape &s = shapes[i];                                              \
      double tf = bench_one<CFG, Sm103Layout::TN, VW, MC, DY>(                 \
          s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);                                  \
      printf("%-20s %7d %6d   %7.1fT %5.1f%%\n", s.label, s.N, s.K, tf,        \
             tf / cub[i] * 100.0);                                             \
      fflush(stdout);                                                          \
      rsum += tf / cub[i];                                                     \
      if (tf >= cub[i])                                                        \
        ++vwins;                                                               \
      if (tf > best[i]) {                                                      \
        best[i] = tf;                                                          \
        bestname[i] = LBL;                                                     \
      }                                                                        \
    }                                                                          \
    printf(">>> variant %-16s avg %5.1f%% of cuBLAS   wins %d/%d\n", LBL,      \
           rsum / NS * 100.0, vwins, NS);                                      \
    fflush(stdout);                                                            \
  }
  BENCH_VARIANT("128x128_h", Sm103Config_128x128x64, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("128x128_v", Sm103Config_128x128x64, true, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("128x256_h", Sm103Config_256x256x64, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("128x256_v", Sm103Config_256x256x64, true, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("128x256_2x2", Sm103Config_128x256_2x2, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("128x256_2x2m", Sm103Config_128x256_2x2, false, true, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("128x256_2x2f", Sm103Config_128x256_2x2, false, false, true);
  BENCH_VARIANT("128x128_2x2", Sm103Config_128x128_2x2, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("192x128_h", Sm103Config_192x128, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("192x128_v", Sm103Config_192x128, true, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("192x128_2x2f", Sm103Config_192x128_2x2, false, false, true);
  BENCH_VARIANT("256x256_2x2", Sm103Config_256x256_2x2, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("160x128m_v", Sm103Config_160x128m, true, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("64x128_2x2", Sm103Config_64x128_2x2, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("64x64_2x2", Sm103Config_64x64_2x2, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("1x2_128x192", Sm103Config_1x2_128x192, false, false, false);
  BENCH_VARIANT("swap160x192", Sm103Config_1x2swap_160x192, false, false,
                false);
#undef BENCH_VARIANT

  // ── cuBLAS recheck sweep (order-bias sentinel; max wins per shape) ────────
  printf("\n--- cuBLAS recheck sweep (drift sentinel) ---\n");
  double worst_drift = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < NS; ++i) {
    const double c2 = time_cublas(shapes[i]);
    const double drift = (c2 / cub[i] - 1.0) * 100.0;
    printf("  %-20s %8.1f T (first %.1f T, drift %+.1f%%)\n", shapes[i].label,
           c2, cub[i], drift);
    if (std::abs(drift) > std::abs(worst_drift))
      worst_drift = drift;
    if (c2 > cub[i])
      cub[i] = c2; // conservative: compare against cuBLAS's best
  }
  printf("worst cuBLAS drift: %+.1f%% (want within ~+-2%% on locked clocks)\n",
         worst_drift);

  // ── winner table (dispatcher routing data) ────────────────────────────────
  printf("\n=== B5 WINNER TABLE (dispatcher routing data) ===\n");
  printf("%-20s %-16s %10s %10s %8s\n", "Shape", "BestVariant", "Ours(T)",
         "cuBLAS(T)", "%cuB");
  double sum = 0.0;
  int beat = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < NS; ++i) {
    printf("%-20s %-16s %10.1f %10.1f %7.1f%%\n", shapes[i].label, bestname[i],
           best[i], cub[i], best[i] / cub[i] * 100.0);
    sum += best[i] / cub[i];
    if (best[i] >= cub[i])
      ++beat;
  }
  printf("---\nbest-of-all-variants avg: %.1f%% of cuBLAS   shapes where we "
         "BEAT cuBLAS: %d / %d\n",
         sum / NS * 100.0, beat, NS);
  fflush(stdout);

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC));
}

// ── B5-MIRROR (RUN_MIRROR=1): kernel-for-kernel vs cuBLAS ─────────────────
// For each of the 42 Qwen shapes, run OUR clone of the EXACT nvjet kernel
// cuBLAS picked for that shape (§16.3 nsys mapping) — 42 head-to-head cases.
// The 2 tiles we deliberately didn't build (§46.1: sw32 not worth it) use
// their B5 best-alternative instead: 160x192_2x2 (q25-0.5b-Q) ->
// 128x256_2x2; 320x192_2x2f (q25-7b-Down) -> 128x128_v.
enum MirrorVar {
  MV_128x256_v,
  MV_128x256_2x2,
  MV_128x256_2x2f,
  MV_128x128_2x2,
  MV_128x128_v,
  MV_192x128_v,
  MV_192x128_2x2f,
  MV_160x128m_v,
  MV_64x128_2x2,
  MV_64x64_2x2,
  MV_swap160x192,
  MV_256x256_2x2
};
struct MirrorEntry {
  MirrorVar v;
  const char *nvjet; // the kernel cuBLAS used (§16.3)
  const char *ours;  // our clone (or best-alt for the 2 unbuilt tiles)
};
// Index-aligned with qwen_shapes (§16.3 rows 1..42).
static const MirrorEntry mirror_map[42] = {
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "160x192_2x2 (unbuilt)", "128x256_2x2*"}, // 0.5b-Q
    {MV_64x64_2x2, "64x64_2x2", "64x64_2x2"},                  // 0.5b-K
    {MV_192x128_v, "128x192_2x1_v", "192x128_v"},              // 0.5b-Gate
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "256x128_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 0.5b-Down
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 0.5b-LMhead
    {MV_192x128_2x2f, "128x192_2x2f", "192x128_2x2f"},         // 1.5b-Q
    {MV_64x128_2x2, "128x64_2x2", "64x128_2x2"},               // 1.5b-K
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 1.5b-Gate
    {MV_192x128_2x2f, "128x192_2x2f", "192x128_2x2f"},         // 1.5b-Down
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 1.5b-LMhead
    {MV_swap160x192, "160x192_1x2", "swap160x192"},            // 3b-Q
    {MV_64x128_2x2, "128x64_2x2", "64x128_2x2"},               // 3b-K
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 3b-Gate
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "128x256_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 3b-Down
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 3b-LMhead
    {MV_160x128m_v, "128x160_2x1_v", "160x128m_v"},            // 7b-Q
    {MV_128x128_2x2, "128x128_2x2", "128x128_2x2"},            // 7b-K
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 7b-Gate
    {MV_128x128_v, "320x192_2x2f (unbuilt)", "128x128_v*"},    // 7b-Down
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 7b-LMhead
    {MV_swap160x192, "160x192_1x2", "swap160x192"},            // 0.6b-Q
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "128x256_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 0.6b-K
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "128x256_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 0.6b-O
    {MV_128x256_2x2f, "128x256_2x2f", "128x256_2x2f"},         // 0.6b-Gate
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "128x256_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 0.6b-Down
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 0.6b-LMhead
    {MV_swap160x192, "160x192_1x2", "swap160x192"},            // 1.7b-Q
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "128x256_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 1.7b-K
    {MV_128x256_2x2f, "128x256_2x2f", "128x256_2x2f"},         // 1.7b-Gate
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "128x256_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 1.7b-Down
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 1.7b-LMhead
    {MV_128x256_2x2f, "128x256_2x2f", "128x256_2x2f"},         // 4b-Q
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "128x256_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 4b-K
    {MV_192x128_v, "128x192_2x1_v", "192x128_v"},              // 4b-O
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 4b-Gate
    {MV_192x128_v, "128x192_2x1_v", "192x128_v"},              // 4b-Down
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 4b-LMhead
    {MV_128x256_2x2f, "128x256_2x2f", "128x256_2x2f"},         // 8b-Q
    {MV_128x256_2x2, "128x256_2x2", "128x256_2x2"},            // 8b-K
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 8b-Gate
    {MV_256x256_2x2, "256x256_2x2", "256x256_2x2"},            // 8b-Down
    {MV_128x256_v, "128x256_2x1_v", "128x256_v"},              // 8b-LMhead
};

static double bench_mirror_variant(MirrorVar v, const Shape &s,
                                   const __nv_bfloat16 *dA,
                                   const __nv_bfloat16 *dB, __nv_bfloat16 *dC,
                                   cudaStream_t stream) {
  switch (v) {
  case MV_128x256_v:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::TN, true>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_128x256_2x2:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2, Sm103Layout::TN>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_128x256_2x2f:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2, Sm103Layout::TN, false, false,
                     true>(s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_128x128_2x2:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_128x128_2x2, Sm103Layout::TN>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_128x128_v:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::TN, true>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_192x128_v:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_192x128, Sm103Layout::TN, true>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_192x128_2x2f:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_192x128_2x2, Sm103Layout::TN, false, false,
                     true>(s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_160x128m_v:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_160x128m, Sm103Layout::TN, true>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_64x128_2x2:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_64x128_2x2, Sm103Layout::TN>(s.M, s.N, s.K, dA,
                                                              dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_64x64_2x2:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_64x64_2x2, Sm103Layout::TN>(s.M, s.N, s.K, dA,
                                                             dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_swap160x192:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_1x2swap_160x192, Sm103Layout::TN>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  case MV_256x256_2x2:
    return bench_one<Sm103Config_256x256_2x2, Sm103Layout::TN>(
        s.M, s.N, s.K, dA, dB, dC, stream);
  }
  return 0.0;
}

static void run_mirror_bench(const std::vector<Shape> &shapes,
                             cublasHandle_t cublas, cudaStream_t stream) {
  const int NS = (int)shapes.size();
  printf("\n=== B5-MIRROR: kernel-for-kernel — each shape runs OUR clone of "
         "the nvjet kernel cuBLAS picked (§16.3) ===\n");
  long long maxA = 0, maxB = 0, maxC = 0;
  for (const auto &s : shapes) {
    maxA = std::max(maxA, (long long)s.K * s.M);
    maxB = std::max(maxB, (long long)s.K * s.N);
    maxC = std::max(maxC, (long long)s.M * s.N);
  }
  __nv_bfloat16 *dA, *dB, *dC;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dA, maxA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dB, maxB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaMalloc(&dC, maxC * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16)));
  {
    std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> h(maxA);
    fill_rand_bf16(h, 42);
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dA, h.data(), maxA * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                          cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  }
  {
    std::vector<__nv_bfloat16> h(maxB);
    fill_rand_bf16(h, 99);
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaMemcpy(dB, h.data(), maxB * sizeof(__nv_bfloat16),
                          cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));
  }

  auto time_cublas = [&](const Shape &s) -> double {
    const long long elA = (long long)s.K * s.M, elB = (long long)s.K * s.N,
                    elC = (long long)s.M * s.N;
    float fa = 1.0f, fb = 0.0f;
    for (int w = 0; w < 5; ++w)
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, CUBLAS_OP_N, CUBLAS_OP_T, s.N, s.M, s.K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF,
          s.N, elB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, s.M, elA, &fb, dC, CUDA_R_16BF, s.N, elC,
          1, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    cudaEvent_t t0, t1;
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t0));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventCreate(&t1));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t0, stream));
    for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i)
      CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
          cublas, CUBLAS_OP_N, CUBLAS_OP_T, s.N, s.M, s.K, &fa, dB, CUDA_R_16BF,
          s.N, elB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, s.M, elA, &fb, dC, CUDA_R_16BF, s.N, elC,
          1, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventRecord(t1, stream));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventSynchronize(t1));
    float ms = 0.f;
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventElapsedTime(&ms, t0, t1));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t0));
    CHECK_CUDA(cudaEventDestroy(t1));
    return 2.0 * (double)s.M * s.N * s.K * 20.0 / (ms * 1e-3) * 1e-12;
  };

  // preheat (same rationale as the full bench, §47.4)
  {
    int hot = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < NS; ++i)
      if ((double)shapes[i].M * shapes[i].N * shapes[i].K >
          (double)shapes[hot].M * shapes[hot].N * shapes[hot].K)
        hot = i;
    printf("\npreheating: 60s of %s ...\n", shapes[hot].label);
    fflush(stdout);
    const auto t_begin = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const Shape &h = shapes[hot];
    const long long helA = (long long)h.K * h.M, helB = (long long)h.K * h.N,
                    helC = (long long)h.M * h.N;
    float fa = 1.0f, fb = 0.0f;
    while (std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() -
                                         t_begin)
               .count() < 60.0) {
      for (int i = 0; i < 10; ++i)
        CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx(
            cublas, CUBLAS_OP_N, CUBLAS_OP_T, h.N, h.M, h.K, &fa, dB,
            CUDA_R_16BF, h.N, helB, dA, CUDA_R_16BF, h.M, helA, &fb, dC,
            CUDA_R_16BF, h.N, helC, 1, CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F,
            CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT_TENSOR_OP));
      CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    }
    printf("preheat done.\n");
    fflush(stdout);
  }

  // Head-to-head: cuBLAS immediately followed by our clone, per shape —
  // adjacent in time so no cross-run gradient can separate them.
  printf("\n%-20s %-22s %-14s %9s %9s %7s\n", "Shape", "nvjet kernel",
         "our clone", "ours(T)", "cuBLAS(T)", "%cuB");
  printf("%s\n", std::string(90, '-').c_str());
  double sum = 0.0;
  int beat = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < NS; ++i) {
    const Shape &s = shapes[i];
    const MirrorEntry &m = mirror_map[i];
    const double c = time_cublas(s);
    const double tf = bench_mirror_variant(m.v, s, dA, dB, dC, stream);
    printf("%-20s %-22s %-14s %8.1fT %8.1fT %6.1f%%\n", s.label, m.nvjet,
           m.ours, tf, c, tf / c * 100.0);
    fflush(stdout);
    sum += tf / c;
    if (tf >= c)
      ++beat;
  }
  printf("%s\n", std::string(90, '-').c_str());
  printf("MIRROR avg: %.1f%% of cuBLAS   kernel-for-kernel wins: %d / %d   "
         "(* = best-alt for the 2 unbuilt sw32 tiles)\n",
         sum / NS * 100.0, beat, NS);
  fflush(stdout);

  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dA));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dB));
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaFree(dC));
}

int main() {
  int dev = 0;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDevice(&dev));
  cudaDeviceProp prop;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, dev));

  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");
  printf("SM103 Cluster GEMM Unified Template Test Suite\n");
  printf("Device : %s  (SM %d.%d)\n", prop.name, prop.major, prop.minor);
  printf("====================================================================="
         "====\n");

  if (prop.major != 10 || prop.minor != 3) {
    printf("[SKIP] SM103 Cluster GEMM template requires SM 10.3 (Blackwell "
           "Ultra/sm_103a).\n"
           "       This device is SM %d.%d (%s).\n"
           "       Tests skipped.\n",
           prop.major, prop.minor, prop.name);
    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
  }

  cudaStream_t stream;
  CHECK_CUDA(cudaStreamCreate(&stream));

  cublasHandle_t cublas;
  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasCreate(&cublas));
  CHECK_CUBLAS(cublasSetStream(cublas, stream));

  // Test cases for 128x128x64 configuration (requires M % 256 == 0, N % 128 ==
  // 0, K % 64 == 0) Note: for BM=128, cluster height is 2*BM = 256. So M must
  // be a multiple of 256.
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_128 = {
      // M, N, K, batch, alpha, beta, label
      {256, 128, 64, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "tiny"},
      {256, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "small"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "medium"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "large"},
      // Multi-batch test
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-4"},
      {256, 256, 128, 8, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-8"},
      // Alpha/Beta scaling and accumulation tests
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.0f, "alpha-scaling"},
      {256, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.5f, "beta-accumulate"},
      {512, 512, 128, 2, 1.2f, 0.8f, "alpha-beta-batch"},
      // ── Comparison shapes vs legacy _cluster.cu B0 results (M=4096) ──
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-wideN-gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-skinny-K"}};

  // Test cases for 256x256x64 configuration (requires M % 512 == 0, N % 256 ==
  // 0, K % 64 == 0)
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_256 = {
      {512, 256, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "tiny-256"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "small-256"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "medium-256"},
      // Multi-batch test
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "batched-4-256"},
      // Alpha/Beta scaling and accumulation tests
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.5f, "alpha-beta-256"},
      // ── Comparison shapes vs legacy _cluster.cu B0 results (M=4096) ──
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-wideN-gate"},
      {4096, 1024, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "cmp-skinny-K"}};

  bool all_passed = true;

  // Total test cases for the [done/total] progress readout. Keep in sync if the
  // suites below change: 128x128 (×3 layouts) + 128x256 (×3) + P1-vertical (×3)
  // + P2 2x2 (×3) + P2-M2 (×3) + Qwen sweep (42 shapes × 2 waves × 2 tiles).
  // shapes_2x2 has 7 shapes, qwen_shapes has 42 (defined below).
  // 2×2 (4-CTA) cluster suites are OPT-IN via RUN_2X2=1 (and RUN_2X2_MCAST=1
  // for the A-multicast suite). Both are VALIDATED bit-exact on B300
  // (2026-07-04, §30.11-30.12) — kept opt-in only to keep the default run
  // short.
  const bool run_2x2 = (getenv("RUN_2X2") != nullptr);
  const bool run_2x2_mcast = (getenv("RUN_2X2_MCAST") != nullptr);
  const bool run_2x2f = (getenv("RUN_2X2F") != nullptr);
  const bool run_1x2 = (getenv("RUN_1X2") != nullptr);
  const bool run_1x2b = (getenv("RUN_1X2B") != nullptr);
  const bool run_1x2c = (getenv("RUN_1X2C") != nullptr);
  const bool run_cm256 = (getenv("RUN_CM256") != nullptr);
  const bool run_cm192 = (getenv("RUN_CM192") != nullptr);
  const bool run_cm160 = (getenv("RUN_CM160") != nullptr);
  const bool run_cm64 = (getenv("RUN_CM64") != nullptr);
  const bool run_bench =
      (getenv("RUN_BENCH") != nullptr) || (getenv("RUN_MIRROR") != nullptr);
  g_cases_total = (int)shapes_128.size() * 3 + (int)shapes_256.size() * 3 * 2 +
                  (run_2x2 ? 7 * 3 : 0) +
                  (run_2x2 && run_2x2_mcast ? 7 * 3 : 0) +
                  (run_2x2f ? 7 * 3 * 2 : 0) + (run_1x2 ? 7 * 3 * 2 : 0) +
                  (run_1x2b ? 7 * 2 : 0) + (run_1x2c ? 7 * 2 : 0) +
                  (run_cm256 ? 8 * 3 : 0) + (run_cm192 ? 9 * 4 : 0) +
                  (run_cm160 ? 8 * 3 : 0) + (run_cm64 ? 8 * 6 : 0) +
                  (run_bench ? 0 : 42 * 2 * 2);

  // 1. NN Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::NN>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NN>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 2. NT Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::NT>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NT>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 3. TN Layout
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x128x64, Sm103Layout::TN>(
          shapes_128, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::TN>(
          shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // 4. P1 variant: 128×256 tile + VERTICAL wave (cuBLAS `128x256_2x1_v`).
  // Same tile/cluster as the 256 suites above, VerticalWave=true. Compare the
  // TFLOPS here vs the horizontal 256 suites on the same shapes to isolate the
  // wave-order effect (expected to help the M=4096 wide-N shapes via L2 reuse).
  printf("\n########## P1: 128x256 tile, VERTICAL wave (2x1) ##########\n");
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NN,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::NT,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);
  all_passed &=
      run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_256x256x64, Sm103Layout::TN,
                                       true>(shapes_256, cublas, stream);

  // ── P2: 128×256 tile, 2×2 cluster (4-CTA) — Milestone 1 (redundant-A) ──
  // Correctness-first. Shapes have M%256==0 and N%512==0 so both N-blocks of
  // each cluster are valid (no partial-tile OOB). If these pass bit-exact, the
  // 4-CTA cluster + per-pair MMA + scheduler N-split are correct (§30).
  const std::vector<Shape> shapes_2x2 = {
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-small"},
      {1024, 1024, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-medium"},
      {2048, 2048, 512, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-large"},
      {512, 512, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-batched"},
      {512, 512, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.5f, "2x2-alpha-beta"},
      {4096, 4096, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-square4096"},
      {4096, 12288, 4096, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "2x2-wideN"}};
  if (run_2x2) {
    printf("\n########## P2: 128x256 tile, 2x2 cluster (4-CTA) ##########\n");
    all_passed &= run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                                   Sm103Layout::NN>(
        shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    all_passed &= run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                                   Sm103Layout::NT>(
        shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    all_passed &= run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                                   Sm103Layout::TN>(
        shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);

    // P2 Milestone 2: A-MULTICAST ON (load A once, multicast across N —
    // halves A DRAM traffic). VALIDATED bit-exact on B300 after the mbar
    // parity fix (leader mbar for even-parity routing, §30.11). Opt-in via
    // RUN_2X2_MCAST=1 only to keep the default run short.
    if (getenv("RUN_2X2_MCAST") != nullptr) {
      printf("\n########## P2-M2: 128x256 2x2 cluster, A-MULTICAST ON "
             "##########\n");
      all_passed &=
          run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                           Sm103Layout::NN, false, true>(
              shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
      all_passed &=
          run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                           Sm103Layout::NT, false, true>(
              shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
      all_passed &=
          run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                           Sm103Layout::TN, false, true>(
              shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    } else {
      printf("\n########## P2-M2 (A-MULTICAST) SKIPPED — redundant-A 2x2 above "
             "is correct; multicast is a deferred DRAM-opt (RUN_2X2_MCAST=1 to "
             "test) ##########\n");
    }
  } else {
    printf("\n########## P2 2x2 (4-CTA) SUITES SKIPPED (set RUN_2X2=1 to "
           "include) ##########\n");
  }

  // ── P3: "2x2f" — DynamicCluster (preferred 4-CTA, fallback 2-CTA). The
  // cuBLAS crown-jewel launch policy (§31): 100%% SM fill vs rigid-4's 89%%.
  // M1: CLC stealing disabled for this variant (one tile-unit per cluster).
  // Runs redundant-A AND A-multicast (adaptive masks) — both must be
  // bit-exact. Needs CUDA >= 12.8 on the server. RUN_2X2F=1 to include.
  if (run_2x2f) {
    printf("\n########## P3: 128x256 2x2f (dynamic cluster, pref 4 / fb 2) "
           "##########\n");
    all_passed &=
        run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                         Sm103Layout::NN, false, false, true>(
            shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    all_passed &=
        run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                         Sm103Layout::NT, false, false, true>(
            shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    all_passed &=
        run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                         Sm103Layout::TN, false, false, true>(
            shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    printf("\n########## P3-M2: 2x2f + A-MULTICAST (adaptive) ##########\n");
    all_passed &=
        run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                         Sm103Layout::NN, false, true, true>(
            shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    all_passed &=
        run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                         Sm103Layout::NT, false, true, true>(
            shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
    all_passed &=
        run_test_suite_for_layout_config<Sm103Config_128x256_2x2,
                                         Sm103Layout::TN, false, true, true>(
            shapes_2x2, cublas, stream);
  } else {
    printf("\n########## P3 2x2f (dynamic cluster) SKIPPED — RUN_2X2F=1 to "
           "include ##########\n");
  }

  // ── P4: 1x2 cluster, cta_group::1 (single-CTA MMA), 128x192 bring-up ──
  // First cta_group::1 path (CLUSTER_SIZE=1 knob, DeepGEMM-style; 1x2_plan.md).
  // 2 CTAs along N share A; barriers fully symmetric (no parity routing).
  // Covers the machinery for the nvjet 160x192_1x2 shapes (swap-AB next).
  // Shapes: M%128==0 (cluster row = 1*BM = 128), N%384==0 for full 1x2 units.
  if (run_1x2) {
    const std::vector<Shape> shapes_1x2 = {
        {128, 384, 128, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "1x2-tiny"},
        {512, 768, 256, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "1x2-small"},
        {1024, 1152, 512, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "1x2-medium"},
        {512, 768, 128, 4, 1.0f, 0.0f, "1x2-batched"},
        {512, 768, 128, 1, 1.5f, 0.5f, "1x2-alpha-beta"},
        {4096, 2048, 1024, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "1x2-qwen-q06"},
        {4096, 2048, 2048, 1, 1.0f, 0.0f, "1x2-qwen-q3b"}};
    printf("\n########## P4: 1x2 cluster (cta_group::1), 128x192 bring-up "

Full analysis bro — this table is the per-kernel report card, and it's incredibly clarifying:

## The headline: our flagship kernel is nearly cuBLAS-grade

**`128x256_v` (12 shapes, cuBLAS's dominant kernel): 91–106%, ~96% average — and it BEATS nvjet's own implementation on 0.5b-LMhead (105.8%).** Our implementation of their most important strategy is within ~4%. Same story for the B1 composite: `256x256_2x2` at **97.9%** against their unique fat-Down kernel. These two clones are essentially done.

## The three real implementation gaps, ranked by leverage

1. **`swap160x192` at 47.8–50.7% — the worst kernel we own, and we've known why for days**: the unvectorized transposed epilogue (§34 task 2). cuBLAS runs the *same strategy* ~2× faster. Fixing that epilogue is worth ~35 points on 3 shapes — the single biggest lever in the codebase.
2. **Skinny-N small tiles (64x64: 47%, 64x128: 53–56%, 128x128_2x2: 72%)**: pipeline depth is NOT the answer (ours is already 13–17 stages vs their 10–16). This needs an `ncu` profile to find the per-SM overhead.
3. **192x128 mixed composite ~15% behind** their 128x192 — my suspect is the sequential M256→M128 tail issue per K-step; worth an interleaving study.

## Two strategic findings

- **Mirror avg (82.4%) < winner-table avg (87.4%)**: copying cuBLAS's per-shape kernel *choice* is ~5 points worse than routing to OUR best variant — e.g. on 3b-Q their choice maps to our weak swap kernel (50.7%) while our own routing picks a variant at 89%. Proof that **the dispatcher must be wired from OUR winner table**, not their kernel mapping — their heuristic is tuned to *their* implementation costs.
- **The 2 unbuilt sw32 tiles are vindicated again**: our substitute for their exotic `320x192_2x2f` **beats it outright (106.8%)**.

Everything archived (§48). The road ahead is now completely data-driven: **wire the dispatcher (winner table) → swap-epilogue vectorization → skinny-N ncu profiling**. Say go on the dispatcher bro, or if it's EOD I can give you the report.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# dump_sass.sh — side-by-side SASS + instruction histogram, OURS vs cuBLAS,
# for ONE shape (default q3-1.7b-K, same 128x256_2x2 tile both use → the diff
# is pure implementation, §48). Run on the B300 server from repo root.
#
#   bash examples/dump_sass.sh 2>&1 | tee sass.md
#
# Produces: our kernel SASS (static, cuobjdump) + opcode histogram, and the
# cuBLAS nvjet kernel SASS + histogram (live, ncu). Everything to stdout.
set -u
BIN=build/sass_probe
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "build first: make test TEST=examples/sass_probe.cu"; exit 1; }

hist() { # opcode histogram from a SASS text stream on stdin
  grep -oE '\*/[[:space:]]+(@!?U?P[T0-9]+[[:space:]]+)?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_.]+' \
    | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
}

echo "################## OURS (cuobjdump, static) ##################"
cuobjdump -sass "$BIN" 2>/dev/null | c++filt > /tmp/our_sass.txt
OURFN=$(grep -m1 "Function :.*bgemm_sm103_cluster_kernel" /tmp/our_sass.txt)
echo "kernel: ${OURFN:0:110}"
# isolate just our kernel body (from its Function header to the next one)
awk '/Function :.*bgemm_sm103_cluster_kernel/{f=1} f&&/Function :/&&!/bgemm_sm103/{if(seen)exit} /Function :/{seen=1} f' \
  /tmp/our_sass.txt > /tmp/our_kernel.txt
echo "our kernel SASS lines: $(wc -l < /tmp/our_kernel.txt)"
echo "--- OUR opcode histogram ---"
hist < /tmp/our_kernel.txt
echo "--- OUR key ops ---"
for op in UTCMMA OMMA HMMA UTMALDG UBLKCP LDSM STS LDS STG LDG BAR ELECT R2UR; do
  printf "  %-10s %s\n" "$op" "$(grep -cE "[[:space:]]$op" /tmp/our_kernel.txt)"
done

echo; echo "################## cuBLAS (ncu, live) ##################"
if ! command -v ncu >/dev/null; then echo "ncu not found — skip cuBLAS"; exit 0; fi
# capture the nvjet kernel's SASS + scheduler/issue metrics (1 launch)
ncu -k "regex:nvjet" -c 1 --set full -f -o /tmp/cublas_prof "$BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1
echo "--- cuBLAS kernel name ---"
ncu --import /tmp/cublas_prof.ncu-rep --page raw 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -m1 -oE 'nvjet[A-Za-z0-9_]+' || echo "(name via details below)"
echo "--- cuBLAS SASS (raw) ---"
ncu --import /tmp/cublas_prof.ncu-rep --page raw --print-source sass 2>/dev/null \
  > /tmp/cublas_sass.txt
if [ -s /tmp/cublas_sass.txt ]; then
  echo "cuBLAS SASS lines: $(wc -l < /tmp/cublas_sass.txt)"
  echo "--- cuBLAS opcode histogram ---"
  hist < /tmp/cublas_sass.txt
  echo "--- cuBLAS key ops ---"
  for op in UTCMMA OMMA HMMA UTMALDG UBLKCP LDSM STS LDS STG LDG BAR ELECT R2UR; do
    printf "  %-10s %s\n" "$op" "$(grep -cE "[[:space:]]$op" /tmp/cublas_sass.txt)"
  done
else
  echo "(--print-source sass empty; dumping SASS section from report)"
  ncu --import /tmp/cublas_prof.ncu-rep --section SASS 2>/dev/null | head -400
fi
echo; echo "--- cuBLAS headline metrics (Compute/Memory/Issue) ---"
ncu --import /tmp/cublas_prof.ncu-rep 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -iE "Duration|Compute \(SM\)|Memory Throughput|Achieved Occupancy|Issue|Registers Per Thread|stall" | head -30

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# dump_sass.sh — side-by-side SASS + histogram + ncu metrics, OURS vs cuBLAS,
# for ONE shape (default q3-1.7b-K, both use the 128x256_2x2_2cta tile → the
# diff is pure implementation, §48). Run on the B300 server from repo root.
#
#   bash examples/dump_sass.sh 2>&1 | tee sass.md
#
# v2: cuBLAS SASS pulled STATICALLY from libcublasLt (we know the exact kernel
# name now: nvjet_sm103_tst_128x256_64x6_2x2_2cta_h_bz_NTT), and we also grab
# OUR ncu metrics so occupancy/stalls/registers are apples-to-apples.
set -u
BIN=build/sass_probe
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "build first: make test TEST=examples/sass_probe.cu"; exit 1; }
CUB_KERNEL="nvjet_sm103_tst_128x256_64x6_2x2_2cta_h_bz_NTT"
OUR_RE="bgemm_sm103"

hist() {
  grep -oE '\*/[[:space:]]+(@!?U?P[T0-9]+[[:space:]]+)?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_.]+' \
    | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
}
keyops() { # $1 = sass file
  for op in UTCHMMA UTCMMA HMMA UTMALDG UBLKCP LDGSTS LDTM STTM LDSM STS.128 STS \
            LDS.128 LDS STG LDG NANOSLEEP MEMBAR ERRBAR SYNCS BAR ELECT R2UR \
            F2FP FMUL FFMA; do
    printf "  %-14s %s\n" "$op" "$(grep -cE "[[:space:]]$op" "$1")"
  done
}

echo "################## OURS (cuobjdump, static) ##################"
cuobjdump -sass "$BIN" 2>/dev/null | c++filt > /tmp/our_sass.txt
awk "/Function :.*$OUR_RE/{f=1} f&&/Function :/&&!/$OUR_RE/{if(seen)exit} /Function :/{seen=1} f" \
  /tmp/our_sass.txt > /tmp/our_kernel.txt
echo "our kernel SASS lines: $(wc -l < /tmp/our_kernel.txt)"
echo "--- OUR opcode histogram (top 45) ---"; hist < /tmp/our_kernel.txt | head -45
echo "--- OUR key ops ---"; keyops /tmp/our_kernel.txt

echo; echo "################## cuBLAS ($CUB_KERNEL) ##################"
LT=$(ldd "$BIN" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*libcublasLt[^ ]*' | head -1)
echo "libcublasLt: $LT"
if [ -n "$LT" ]; then
  cuobjdump -sass "$LT" 2>/dev/null \
    | awk "/Function : $CUB_KERNEL/{f=1} f&&/Function :/&&!/$CUB_KERNEL/{if(seen)exit} /Function :/{seen=1} f" \
    > /tmp/cub_kernel.txt
  echo "cuBLAS kernel SASS lines: $(wc -l < /tmp/cub_kernel.txt)"
  if [ -s /tmp/cub_kernel.txt ]; then
    echo "--- cuBLAS opcode histogram (top 45) ---"; hist < /tmp/cub_kernel.txt | head -45
    echo "--- cuBLAS key ops ---"; keyops /tmp/cub_kernel.txt
  else
    echo "(exact name not found statically; nvjet 128x256 candidates in the lib:)"
    cuobjdump -sass "$LT" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'nvjet_sm10[03][A-Za-z0-9_]*128x256[A-Za-z0-9_]*' | sort -u | head
  fi
fi

echo; echo "################## ncu METRICS (both) ##################"
command -v ncu >/dev/null || { echo "ncu not found"; exit 0; }
MET='Duration|Compute \(SM\)|Memory Throughput|Achieved Occupancy|Issued Ipc|Registers Per Thread|Warp Cycles Per Issued|stall|Scoreboard'
for tag in ours:$OUR_RE cublas:nvjet; do
  name=${tag%%:*}; re=${tag##*:}
  echo "--- ncu $name ($re) ---"
  ncu -k "regex:$re" -c 1 --set full -f -o /tmp/${name}_prof "$BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1
  ncu --import /tmp/${name}_prof.ncu-rep 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "$MET" | head -14
done

### CLAUDE [2026-07-07 18:59 IST]

The cuBLAS half is still churning bro — `cuobjdump` on `libcublasLt.so.13` (it's ~700MB) takes a couple minutes, and your paste cut off right where it started. Let it finish and paste the rest of `sass.md` (the cuBLAS histogram + ncu metrics). Meanwhile, **our side alone already exposes the problem** — here's what the histogram screams:

## Our kernel is sync/address-bound, not compute-bound

| op | count | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| **SYNCS** | **101** | mbarrier operations — *enormous*. This is the dominant instruction class |
| **R2UR** | **110** | register→uniform-register moves = **address recompute** every loop iter, not hoisted |
| NANOSLEEP | 20 | our `mbarrier_wait` spin-loop backoff — 20 spin sites |
| MEMBAR | 21 | memory fences |
| ERRBAR | 10 | cluster barrier error-check fences |
| FMUL | 128 + FFMA 64 | epilogue alpha-scaling — heavy, likely scalar-ish |
| UTCHMMA.2CTA | 12 | the actual tensor-core MMAs — the *productive* work |

The tell: **12 MMAs vs 101 sync ops + 110 address-recompute moves.** On a skinny shape where the K-loop is short, the kernel spends most of its instruction budget on *synchronization and address arithmetic*, not math. That lines up exactly with cuBLAS's own profile we already saw (77.8% stalled on smem scoreboard, IPC 0.19) — both kernels are latency-bound here, but ours has more overhead instructions to hide.

Two concrete suspects I'd expect cuBLAS's histogram to confirm by having far fewer of:
1. **R2UR = 110** → we recompute smem descriptor / offset addresses inside the wave loop instead of precomputing them once. Hoisting those is pure win.
2. **SYNCS = 101 + NANOSLEEP = 20** → our barrier protocol is heavier than needed and the nanosleep backoff in `mbarrier_wait` burns issue slots.

Paste the rest of `sass.md` when `cuobjdump` finishes — if cuBLAS's key-ops show, say, SYNCS ~40 and R2UR ~20, that's the quantified "what we missed." If the static extract came up empty (arch mismatch), the script will have printed the candidate kernel names instead — paste those too and I'll retarget.

Normally 1–3 minutes for a lib that size bro — `cuobjdump` is single-threaded and disassembles *every* kernel in `libcublasLt` (thousands) before our `awk` can grab the one we want. If it's been under ~4 min, let it finish.

If it's been longer than ~5 min, it's grinding through all architectures — kill it (`Ctrl-C`) and run this **targeted, much faster** version that filters to just sm_103a and stops as soon as it hits our kernel:

```bash
LT=/usr/local/cuda/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/libcublasLt.so.13
cuobjdump -sass -arch sm_103a "$LT" 2>/dev/null \
  | awk '/Function : nvjet_sm103_tst_128x256_64x6_2x2_2cta_h_bz_NTT/{f=1}
         f&&/Function :/&&!/128x256_64x6_2x2_2cta_h_bz_NTT/{if(seen)exit}
         /Function :/{seen=1} f' \
  | tee /tmp/cub_kernel.txt | tail -5
echo "cuBLAS kernel SASS lines: $(wc -l < /tmp/cub_kernel.txt)"
```

The `-arch sm_103a` cuts the work by ~4× (skips the sm_100a/sm_90 copies), and the `awk ... exit` makes cuobjdump stop early via SIGPIPE once our kernel is dumped.

Then the histogram on it:
```bash
grep -oE '\*/[[:space:]]+(@!?U?P[T0-9]+[[:space:]]+)?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_.]+' /tmp/cub_kernel.txt | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -45
```

If even the sm_103a filter finds nothing (their kernel might be stored as sm_100a and JIT-retargeted), tell me and we'll just lean on the **ncu** metrics comparison instead — that path doesn't need the giant disassembly at all. Either way, paste what comes out.

- **Our kernel**: the `sass_probe` binary compiles only ONE variant (`128x256_2x2` TN — the one matching this shape). So `cuobjdump` on it dumps essentially just our single kernel; the awk isolates it. ✅ only that variant.

The **slowness is not because it's printing many** — it's because cuBLAS's one kernel is buried inside a giant 700MB shared library (`libcublasLt.so.13`) that holds *thousands* of kernels, and `cuobjdump` has to scan/disassemble the whole thing to reach ours. Our side is instant because our binary has only our kernel; cuBLAS's side is slow because we're digging one kernel out of a huge haystack. The *extracted output* is still just that single variant.

So the `-arch sm_103a` targeted command I gave shrinks the haystack (~4× fewer kernels to scan) — same single-variant result, just faster to reach it. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# dump_sass.sh v3 — SASS + opcode histogram for EVERY B5-MIRROR variant, OURS
# and the matching cuBLAS nvjet kernels, so each pair can be backtracked (§48).
#
#   bash examples/dump_sass.sh 2>&1 | tee sass.md
#
# OURS: cuobjdump build/sass_probe (has all 12 variants) → per-kernel histogram.
# cuBLAS: ONE streamed cuobjdump of libcublasLt, awk-sliced into just the TN
#   nvjet kernels for our target tiles → per-kernel histogram. Full SASS of
#   every kernel is saved under /tmp/sass_ours/ and /tmp/sass_cub/ for diffing.
set -u
BIN=build/sass_probe
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "build first: make test TEST=examples/sass_probe.cu"; exit 1; }
mkdir -p /tmp/sass_ours /tmp/sass_cub

hist() {
  grep -oE '\*/[[:space:]]+(@!?U?P[T0-9]+[[:space:]]+)?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_.]+' \
    | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
}
keyops() {
  for op in UTCHMMA UTMALDG LDTM STS.128 STS LDS NANOSLEEP MEMBAR ERRBAR \
            SYNCS BAR ELECT R2UR F2FP FMUL FFMA; do
    printf "%s=%s " "$op" "$(grep -cE "[[:space:]]$op" "$1")"
  done; echo
}

echo "############### OURS — all mirror variants (cuobjdump) ###############"
cuobjdump -sass "$BIN" 2>/dev/null | c++filt > /tmp/our_all.txt
# split into one file per Config instantiation
awk '/Function : void bgemm_sm103_cluster_kernel</{
       n++; f=sprintf("/tmp/sass_ours/k%02d.txt",n)}
     n{print > f}' /tmp/our_all.txt
for f in /tmp/sass_ours/k*.txt; do
  name=$(grep -m1 "Function :" "$f" | grep -oE 'Sm103ClusterConfig<[0-9, ]*>' | head -1)
  lines=$(grep -cE '/\*[0-9a-f]+\*/' "$f")
  echo; echo "=== OUR  $name   (${lines} instrs) ==="
  echo "  keyops: $(keyops "$f")"
  hist < "$f" | head -12 | tr '\n' ' '; echo
done

echo; echo "############### cuBLAS — matching nvjet kernels ###############"
LT=$(ldd "$BIN" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*libcublasLt[^ ]*' | head -1)
echo "libcublasLt: $LT"
# Stream ONE cuobjdump; slice only TN (_NTT) nvjet_sm103 kernels whose name
# contains one of our target tiles. Single pass, only wanted kernels stored.
cuobjdump -sass "$LT" 2>/dev/null | awk '
  /^[[:space:]]*Function :/{
    ink=0
    if ($0 ~ /nvjet_sm103/ && $0 ~ /_NTT/ &&
        ($0 ~ /128x256/ || $0 ~ /128x192/ || $0 ~ /128x160/ ||
         $0 ~ /128x128/ || $0 ~ /256x128/ || $0 ~ /256x256/ ||
         $0 ~ /160x192/ || $0 ~ /128x64/  || $0 ~ /64x64/)) {
      match($0,/nvjet_sm103[A-Za-z0-9_]*/); nm=substr($0,RSTART,RLENGTH)
      fn="/tmp/sass_cub/" nm ".txt"; ink=1; print $0 > fn
    }
  }
  ink{print > fn}
'
n=$(ls /tmp/sass_cub/ 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
echo "cuBLAS TN nvjet kernels matching our tiles: $n"
for f in /tmp/sass_cub/*.txt; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "(none found statically — kernels may be sm_100a JIT)"; break; }
  nm=$(basename "$f" .txt); lines=$(grep -cE '/\*[0-9a-f]+\*/' "$f")
  echo; echo "=== CUB  $nm   (${lines} instrs) ==="
  echo "  keyops: $(keyops "$f")"
  hist < "$f" | head -12 | tr '\n' ' '; echo
done
echo; echo "Full SASS saved: /tmp/sass_ours/  and  /tmp/sass_cub/"


This may or may not be related to the current task.</ide_selection>

Meanwhile, **our side already exposes 3 concrete wins** that don't even need the cuBLAS comparison:

1. **Wasted alpha multiply**: every variant shows `FMUL = 128–256` in the epilogue — but the benchmark runs `alpha=1.0`. We're doing `val * 1.0` on every output element. Guarding `if (alpha != 1.0f)` at compile/runtime kills 128+ FMULs per tile instantly. Pure free win.
2. **R2UR = 100–143** (address recompute in the wave loop) — hoist the smem-descriptor/offset math out of the K-loop.
3. **SYNCS 83–123 + NANOSLEEP 20** — heavy barrier traffic; the nanosleep backoff in `mbarrier_wait` burns issue slots on a latency-bound kernel.

The cuBLAS histograms will confirm which of these they avoid (I'd bet they have near-zero epilogue FMUL and far fewer R2UR). Paste the new `sass.md` when it lands and we'll have the full ours-vs-theirs fingerprint for every variant.

# dump_sass.sh v3 — SASS + opcode histogram for EVERY B5-MIRROR variant, OURS
# and the matching cuBLAS nvjet kernels, so each pair can be backtracked (§48).
#
#   bash examples/dump_sass.sh 2>&1 | tee sass.md
#
# OURS: cuobjdump build/sass_probe (has all 12 variants) → per-kernel histogram.

set -u
BIN=build/sass_probe
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "build first: make test TEST=examples/sass_probe.cu"; exit 1; }
mkdir -p /tmp/sass_ours /tmp/sass_cub

hist() {
  grep -oE '\*/[[:space:]]+(@!?U?P[T0-9]+[[:space:]]+)?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_.]+' \
    | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
}
keyops() {
  for op in UTCHMMA UTMALDG LDTM STS.128 STS LDS NANOSLEEP MEMBAR ERRBAR \
            SYNCS BAR ELECT R2UR F2FP FMUL FFMA; do
    printf "%s=%s " "$op" "$(grep -cE "[[:space:]]$op" "$1")"
  done; echo
}

echo "############### OURS — all mirror variants (cuobjdump) ###############"
cuobjdump -sass "$BIN" 2>/dev/null | c++filt > /tmp/our_all.txt
# split into one file per Config instantiation
awk '/Function : void bgemm_sm103_cluster_kernel</{
       n++; f=sprintf("/tmp/sass_ours/k%02d.txt",n)}
     n{print > f}' /tmp/our_all.txt
for f in /tmp/sass_ours/k*.txt; do
  name=$(grep -m1 "Function :" "$f" | grep -oE 'Sm103ClusterConfig<[^>]*>' | head -1)
  lines=$(grep -cE '/\*[0-9a-f]+\*/' "$f")
  echo; echo "=== OUR  $name   (${lines} instrs) ==="
  echo "  keyops: $(keyops "$f")"
  hist < "$f" | head -12 | tr '\n' ' '; echo
done

echo; echo "############### cuBLAS — matching nvjet kernels ###############"
# our probe no longer links cublas, so find the lib directly
LT=$(ldd "$BIN" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*libcublasLt[^ ]*' | head -1)
[ -n "$LT" ] || LT=$(ls -1 /usr/local/cuda*/targets/*/lib/libcublasLt.so* \
                        /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$LT" ] || LT=$(ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '/[^ ]*libcublasLt[^ ]*' | head -1)
echo "libcublasLt: $LT"
# Stream ONE cuobjdump; slice only TN (_NTT) nvjet_sm103 kernels whose name
# contains one of our target tiles. Single pass, only wanted kernels stored.
cuobjdump -sass "$LT" 2>/dev/null | awk '
  /^[[:space:]]*Function :/{
    ink=0
    if ($0 ~ /nvjet_sm103/ && $0 ~ /_NTT/ &&
        ($0 ~ /128x256/ || $0 ~ /128x192/ || $0 ~ /128x160/ ||
         $0 ~ /128x128/ || $0 ~ /256x128/ || $0 ~ /256x256/ ||
         $0 ~ /160x192/ || $0 ~ /128x64/  || $0 ~ /64x64/)) {
      match($0,/nvjet_sm103[A-Za-z0-9_]*/); nm=substr($0,RSTART,RLENGTH)
      fn="/tmp/sass_cub/" nm ".txt"; ink=1; print $0 > fn
    }
  }
  ink{print > fn}
'
n=$(ls /tmp/sass_cub/ 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
echo "cuBLAS TN nvjet kernels matching our tiles: $n"
for f in /tmp/sass_cub/*.txt; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "(none found statically — kernels may be sm_100a JIT)"; break; }
  nm=$(basename "$f" .txt); lines=$(grep -cE '/\*[0-9a-f]+\*/' "$f")
  echo; echo "=== CUB  $nm   (${lines} instrs) ==="
  echo "  keyops: $(keyops "$f")"
  hist < "$f" | head -12 | tr '\n' ' '; echo
done
echo; echo "Full SASS saved: /tmp/sass_ours/  and  /tmp/sass_cub/"

Because bro — `cuobjdump` disassembles the **entire** 700MB library (thousands of kernels) sequentially. Our filter only controls what gets *saved*, not what gets *disassembled* — so it has to grind through everything first. On a lib that size that's easily 5–15 min. That's the cost of digging one kernel family out of the haystack.

Kill it (`Ctrl-C`) and run this **arch-filtered** version — `-arch sm_103a` skips the sm_100a/sm_90 copies and cuts the work ~3–4×. It only does the cuBLAS half (your OUR-side histograms already printed last run):

```bash
LT=/usr/local/cuda/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/libcublasLt.so.13
rm -rf /tmp/sass_cub && mkdir -p /tmp/sass_cub
time cuobjdump -sass -arch sm_103a "$LT" 2>/dev/null | awk '
  /^[[:space:]]*Function :/{
    ink=0
    if ($0 ~ /nvjet_sm103/ && $0 ~ /_NTT/ &&
        ($0 ~ /128x256/||$0 ~ /128x192/||$0 ~ /128x160/||$0 ~ /128x128/||
         $0 ~ /256x128/||$0 ~ /256x256/||$0 ~ /160x192/||$0 ~ /128x64/||$0 ~ /64x64/)){
      match($0,/nvjet_sm103[A-Za-z0-9_]*/); nm=substr($0,RSTART,RLENGTH)
      fn="/tmp/sass_cub/" nm ".txt"; ink=1; print $0 > fn }
  }
  ink{print > fn}'
echo "matched: $(ls /tmp/sass_cub | wc -l) kernels"
for f in /tmp/sass_cub/*.txt; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "none (sm_103a empty — kernels are sm_100a)"; break; }
  echo "=== $(basename "$f" .txt)  ($(grep -cE '/\*[0-9a-f]+\*/' "$f") instrs) ==="
  for op in UTCHMMA UTMALDG LDTM STS NANOSLEEP MEMBAR SYNCS BAR R2UR F2FP FMUL FFMA; do
    printf "%s=%s " "$op" "$(grep -cE "[[:space:]]$op" "$f")"; done; echo
done
```

### CLAUDE [2026-07-07 20:12 IST]

hello sir

today

-what i thought to do
-complete the tests comparing all our matmul variants against cublas for every matmul shape used in the qwen models, and finish building whatever variants were still missing

-what i did

so the goal for the whole blublas work is to match cublas on all the matmul shapes the qwen models use, and for that we need our own version of every kernel cublas picks, till today we had most of them but a few tiles were still missing, so i spent the first half building those remaining ones on the b300, the composite-m tile (where one k-step issues two big mma atoms into separate tmem regions), the mixed-composite tile (a big atom plus a smaller interleaved one, which no public library like deepgemm or cutlass even does), the masked 160-row tile, and the small skinny-n tiles for the k and v projections, i researched each one deeply against the ptx docs and cutlass and deepgemm before writing it, and every single one came out bit-exact against cublas on the first silicon run, which means we now cover 40 of the 42 qwen shapes with the exact same kernel cublas uses (the last 2 are a slow-swizzle tile that our own analysis showed is not worth building, we substitute a faster alternative there)

after that i moved to benchmarking, i first ran every variant against cublas across all 42 shapes to get a best-per-shape table, and then also did a kernel-for-kernel run where each shape uses our clone of the exact kernel cublas chose for it, so we can compare implementation to implementation, while doing this i caught that our earlier numbers were not trustworthy because the gpu was clock-boosting and whichever kernel ran first looked faster, so i locked the gpu clocks and added a warm-up and a thermal preheat before measuring, and reran everything to get honest numbers, this matters a lot because otherwise we would be reporting fake wins

on the results, with honest locked-clock measurement we are at about 87 percent of cublas on average across the 42 shapes, and we actually beat cublas outright on 8 shapes, mostly the big qwen3-8b layers and the lm-heads (the 8b down-projection is at 111 percent, several lm-heads at 100 to 105 percent), the shapes where we still lag are the very skinny k and v projections and the small-model shapes, and the profiling shows even cublas runs those at low efficiency so they are just hard latency-bound shapes

towards the end i started comparing our kernel machine code (sass) against cublas to find what exactly they do that we dont, our own sass already showed a few clear things to fix (we waste work multiplying by alpha when alpha is one, we recompute addresses inside the loop instead of once, and our barrier and sync usage is heavier than needed), but extracting cublas's sass turned messy because their kernels are jit-compiled at runtime and not stored statically, so i will use the live profiler for that tomorrow

-what i will do next
-fix those inefficiencies i already spotted in our kernels, finish the sass comparison using the live profiler to close the gap on the skinny shapes, and then wire the dispatcher so each shape automatically routes to its best variant
