      // multicast_consumer_arrival_count = CM/atomM + CN/atomN - 1 = CLUSTER_N
      // for atom(2,1); == 1 for the 2×1 case, so no regression). §30.x.
      mbarrier_init(empty_mbar_addr + i * 8, cluster_n);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < EPI_PIPE_DEPTH; ++i) {
      mbarrier_init(tmem_full_addr + i * 8, 1);
      mbarrier_init(tmem_empty_addr + i * 8, NUM_EPI_WARPS * CLUSTER_SIZE);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < CLC_PIPE_DEPTH; ++i) {
      mbarrier_init(clc_full_mbar_addr + i * 8, 1);
      // NUM_WARPS × GRANTED cluster CTAs (runtime under DynamicCluster)
      mbarrier_init(clc_empty_mbar_addr + i * 8,
                    (CLC_EMPTY_ARRIVE / CLUSTER_CTAS) * cluster_ctas);
    }
    cluster_fence_mbarrier_init();
  } else if (warp_id == CONSUMER_WARP) {
    // Config::TMEM_COLS = per-stage accumulator column SUM over composite
    // pieces × EPI stages, rounded to the tcgen05.alloc power-of-2 rule
    // (§42 edit 5 — the old BN*EPI formula under-allocated composites).
    alloc_tmem<CLUSTER_SIZE>(tmem_smem_addr, Config::TMEM_COLS);
  }

  cluster_sync();

  const int tmem_addr = tmem[0];
  const int k_iters = K / BK;

  // i_desc: compile-time constant encoding MMA shape + transposition for this
  // layout
  constexpr uint32_t i_desc = sm103_make_i_desc<Config, Layout>();

  // Each PAIR's even (leader) CTA owns that pair's full_mbar; the odd partner
  // reaches across to its pair_leader (rank 0 for pair0, rank 2 for pair1).
  const int tma_mbar_base =
      (cta_m == 0) ? full_mbar_addr
                   : map_smem_addr_to_cta_rank(full_mbar_addr, pair_leader);

  const int cta0_clc_empty_addr =
      (cta_rank == 0) ? clc_empty_mbar_addr
                      : map_smem_addr_to_cta_rank(clc_empty_mbar_addr, 0);

  // One work item = one CLUSTER (CLUSTER_CTAS CTAs). total_mn_tiles counts
  // cluster-tiles, where each cluster covers CLUSTER_SIZE*BM rows × CLUSTER_N
  // N-blocks. grid_n is the number of N-CLUSTERS (= ceil(N/BN / CLUSTER_N)).
  const int init_tile_idx = (int)(blockIdx.x / CLUSTER_CTAS);
  int batch = init_tile_idx / total_mn_tiles;
  int mn_tile = init_tile_idx % total_mn_tiles;

  // grid_m (M-tiles per column) for the vertical-wave tile decode. grid_n is
  // passed in; total_mn_tiles = grid_m * grid_n, so grid_m = total/grid_n.
  const int grid_m = total_mn_tiles / grid_n;

  // ── producer warp ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Loads A and B tiles into the smem pipeline.
  // Layout-specific: how the global addresses map to TMA (x, y, z, w) coords.
  if (warp_id == PRODUCER_WARP && elect_sync()) {
    // decode_mn_tile gives the N-CLUSTER index; this CTA's actual N-block is
    // n_cluster*CLUSTER_N + cta_n (the CLUSTER_N adjacent N-blocks this cluster
    // owns). M-block is by the pair partner cta_m. For CLUSTER_N=1 this reduces
    // to the old 2×1 behaviour (cta_n=0, cta_m=cta_rank).
    int n_cluster, row_tile;
    decode_mn_tile<VerticalWave>(mn_tile, grid_n, grid_m, n_cluster, row_tile);
    int block_row = row_tile * CLUSTER_SIZE + (int)cta_m;
    int block_col = n_cluster * CLUSTER_N + (int)cta_n;
    int cur_batch = batch;
    // A-multicast group mask (MulticastA only): the CTAs sharing this M-half
    // across N = same cta_m, all cta_n. For 2×2: cta_m=0→{0,2}=0b0101,
    // cta_m=1→{1,3}=0b1010. cta_n==0 issues; parity routes completion to
    // leaders.
    uint16_t a_mask = 0; // CTAs sharing this A slice: same cta_m, every cta_n'
    for (int j = 0; j < cluster_n; ++j)
      a_mask |= (uint16_t)(1u << (j * CLUSTER_SIZE + (int)cta_m));

    int stage = 0, phase = 0, issued = 0;
    int clc_stage = 0, clc_full_phase = 0;

    while (true) {
      if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::TN) {
        // A[K,M]: select BM M-columns by column-group index
        // B[K,N]: select BN/2 N-columns by column-group index
        constexpr int A_CHUNK_W = A_SW64 ? 32 : SWIZZLE_W;
        const int A_col = block_row * BM / A_CHUNK_W;
        // Masked tiles (§45): tiles advance by OUT_ROWS (not a whole-chunk
        // multiple) — the element-granular A tmap is addressed per 64-elem
        // chunk below; smem bytes land identically to the chunked map.
        const int A_row_elem = block_row * Config::OUT_ROWS;
        const int B_col = (block_col * BN + (int)cta_m * (BN / CLUSTER_SIZE)) /
                          (Config::B_SW64 ? 32 : SWIZZLE_W);

        for (int k = 0; k < k_iters; ++k) {
          if (issued >= LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH)
            mbarrier_wait(empty_mbar_addr + stage * 8, phase ^ 1);
          ++issued;

          const int A_smem = smem_ptr + stage * copy_size;
          const int B_smem = A_smem + a_tile_bytes;
          const int mbar = tma_mbar_base + stage * 8;
          mbarrier_arrive_expect(mbar, copy_size);

          if constexpr (Config::MASK_M > 0) {
            // One TMA per 64-elem chunk (coords (m_elem, k_row, batch, 0));
            // expect_tx above already counts the full stage — mbar completes
            // per-copy additively (ptx 17115). DeepGEMM's multi-issue pattern.
#pragma unroll
            for (int ci = 0; ci < BM / SWIZZLE_W; ++ci)
              issue_A_load<CLUSTER_SIZE, MulticastA>(
                  A_smem + ci * (BK * SWIZZLE_W * 2), &A_tmap,
                  A_row_elem + ci * SWIZZLE_W, k * BK, cur_batch, 0, mbar,
                  a_mask, cta_n_grant);
          } else {
            // A TN: y = k*BK (K-row), z = A_col (M col-group)
            issue_A_load<CLUSTER_SIZE, MulticastA>(A_smem, &A_tmap, 0, k * BK,
                                                   A_col, cur_batch, mbar,
                                                   a_mask, cta_n_grant);
          }
          // B TN: y = k*BK (K-row), z = B_col (N col-group)
          tma_4d_gmem2smem<CLUSTER_SIZE>(B_smem, &B_tmap, 0, k * BK, B_col,
                                         cur_batch, mbar);

          stage = (stage + 1) % LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH;
          phase ^= (stage == 0);
        }
      } else if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
        // A[M,K]: select BM M-rows
        // B[N,K]: select BN/2 N-rows (B transposed — stored [N,K])
        const int A_row = block_row * Config::OUT_ROWS; // == *BM unmasked
        const int B_row = block_col * BN + (int)cta_m * (BN / CLUSTER_SIZE);

        for (int k = 0; k < k_iters; ++k) {
          if (issued >= LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH)
            mbarrier_wait(empty_mbar_addr + stage * 8, phase ^ 1);
          ++issued;

          const int A_smem = smem_ptr + stage * copy_size;
          const int B_smem = A_smem + a_tile_bytes;
          const int mbar = tma_mbar_base + stage * 8;
          mbarrier_arrive_expect(mbar, copy_size);

          // A NT: y = A_row (M-row), z = k (K-chunk index)
          issue_A_load<CLUSTER_SIZE, MulticastA>(A_smem, &A_tmap, 0, A_row, k,
                                                 cur_batch, mbar, a_mask,
                                                 cta_n_grant);
          // B NT: y = B_row (N-row), z = k (K-chunk index)
          tma_4d_gmem2smem<CLUSTER_SIZE>(B_smem, &B_tmap, 0, B_row, k,
                                         cur_batch, mbar);

          stage = (stage + 1) % LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH;
          phase ^= (stage == 0);
        }
      } else // NN
      {
        // A[M,K]: select BM M-rows
        // B[K,N]: select BN/2 N-columns by column-group index
        const int A_row = block_row * Config::OUT_ROWS; // == *BM unmasked
        const int B_col = (block_col * BN + (int)cta_m * (BN / CLUSTER_SIZE)) /
                          (Config::B_SW64 ? 32 : SWIZZLE_W);

        for (int k = 0; k < k_iters; ++k) {
          if (issued >= LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH)
            mbarrier_wait(empty_mbar_addr + stage * 8, phase ^ 1);
          ++issued;

          const int A_smem = smem_ptr + stage * copy_size;
          const int B_smem = A_smem + a_tile_bytes;
          const int mbar = tma_mbar_base + stage * 8;
          mbarrier_arrive_expect(mbar, copy_size);

          // A NN: y = A_row (M-row), z = k (K-chunk index)
          issue_A_load<CLUSTER_SIZE, MulticastA>(A_smem, &A_tmap, 0, A_row, k,
                                                 cur_batch, mbar, a_mask,
                                                 cta_n_grant);
          // B NN: y = k*BK (K-row), z = B_col (N col-group)
          tma_4d_gmem2smem<CLUSTER_SIZE>(B_smem, &B_tmap, 0, k * BK, B_col,
                                         cur_batch, mbar);

          stage = (stage + 1) % LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH;
          phase ^= (stage == 0);
        }
      }

      mbarrier_wait(clc_full_mbar_addr + clc_stage * 8, clc_full_phase);
      uint32_t is_valid, new_ctaid;
      clc_query_response(clc_response_addr + clc_stage * 16, is_valid,
                         new_ctaid);
      mbarrier_arrive_cluster(cta0_clc_empty_addr + clc_stage * 8);
      clc_stage = (clc_stage + 1) % CLC_PIPE_DEPTH;
      if (clc_stage == 0)
        clc_full_phase ^= 1;

      if (!is_valid)
        break;

      const int new_tile_idx = (int)(new_ctaid / CLUSTER_CTAS);
      cur_batch = new_tile_idx / total_mn_tiles;
      const int new_mn = new_tile_idx % total_mn_tiles;
      int row_tile, n_cluster;
      decode_mn_tile<VerticalWave>(new_mn, grid_n, grid_m, n_cluster, row_tile);
      block_row = row_tile * CLUSTER_SIZE + (int)cta_m;
      // n_sub per STOLEN tile: cancellation units are REQUESTER-SIZED (B300
      // probe, §31.3) — a fallback-2 piece's position within its preferred
      // unit is encoded in the response ctaid. Degenerates to cta_n for all
      // rigid launches (response always cluster-aligned there).
      block_col =
          n_cluster * CLUSTER_N + (int)(((new_ctaid % (uint32_t)CLUSTER_CTAS) /
                                         (uint32_t)CLUSTER_SIZE) +
                                        cta_n_grant);
      // DO NOT reset `issued` here — it must grow monotonically across
      // CLC tiles so the `if (issued >= LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH) wait()` check
      // fires on the next tile's first issue. Resetting caused a
      // producer/consumer race (stage reuse while in-flight) that shows
      // up as "unspecified launch failure" at scale (many tiles, e.g.
      // 4096³). Ported from the fixed _cluster.cu files (2026-07-02).
    }
  }
  // ── consumer warp ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Drives tcgen05.mma from CTA0.  Layout-specific: a_off / b_off reflect
  // how the K dimension strides through smem for each storage order.
  else if (warp_id == CONSUMER_WARP && elect_sync()) {
    int stage = 0, phase = 0;
    int wave_iter = 0;
    int clc_stage = 0, clc_full_phase = 0;
    // Two DISTINCT commit masks for two DISTINCT smem lifetimes (CUTLASS
    // sm100_pipeline.hpp): the accumulator/tmem barrier is PAIR-LOCAL; the
    // operand-smem barrier is CLUSTER-WIDE because A is shared across pairs.
    //
    // pair_mask (accumulator/tmem, calculate_umma_peer_mask): each pair leader
    // signals only ITS 2 CTAs. pair0 (cta_n=0)→0b0011; pair1 (cta_n=1)→0b1100.
    const uint16_t pair_mask =
        (uint16_t)(CTA_MASK << (CLUSTER_SIZE * cta_n_grant));
    // operand_empty_mask (operand smem, calculate_multicast_mask<kRowCol>): for
    // atom(2,1) every CTA participates → full cluster (0b11 for 2×1, 0xF for
    // 2×2). Each pair leader releases with this; each empty_mbar collects
    // CLUSTER_N arrives (matches the CLUSTER_N init count). Using pair_mask
    // here was the deadlock: pair1's producer never saw pair0's release. §30.x.
    const uint16_t operand_empty_mask = (uint16_t)((1u << cluster_ctas) - 1u);

    while (true) {
      // Each pair's even (leader) CTA drives that pair's MMA (ranks 0 and 2);
      // was cta_rank==0 (single leader) in the 2×1 kernel.
      if (cta_m == 0) {
        const int wave_stage = wave_iter % EPI_PIPE_DEPTH;
        const int wave_phase = (wave_iter / EPI_PIPE_DEPTH) & 1;

        if (wave_iter >= EPI_PIPE_DEPTH)
          mbarrier_wait(tmem_empty_addr + wave_stage * 8, wave_phase ^ 1);

        tcgen05_fence_after();

        for (int k = 0; k < k_iters; ++k) {
          mbarrier_wait(full_mbar_addr + stage * 8, phase);
          tcgen05_fence_after();

          const int A_smem = smem_ptr + stage * copy_size;
          const int B_smem = A_smem + a_tile_bytes;

          for (int k1 = 0; k1 < BK / SWIZZLE_W; ++k1) {
            for (int k2 = 0; k2 < SWIZZLE_W / MMA_K_STEP; ++k2) {
              const int use_accum = (k == 0 && k1 == 0 && k2 == 0) ? 0 : 1;

              // a_off: byte offset into A smem for K-step (k1, k2)
              // NN/NT: A smem is [BM × BK], K advances along columns
              //        → k2 * MMA_K_STEP columns = k2 * MMA_K_STEP * 2 bytes
              // TN:    A smem is [BK × BM], K advances along rows
              //        → k2 * MMA_K_STEP rows = k2 * MMA_K_STEP * BM * 2 bytes
              int a_off, b_off;
              if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::TN) {
                // TN A smem is CHUNK-MAJOR after TMA+128B swizzle:
                // per +K step = +SWIZZLE_W (NOT BM). Ported from
                // fixed TN _cluster.cu (2026-07-02).
                a_off = k1 * SWIZZLE_W * SWIZZLE_W * 2 +
                        k2 * MMA_K_STEP * SWIZZLE_W * 2;
              } else {
                a_off = k1 * SWIZZLE_W * BM * 2 + k2 * MMA_K_STEP * 2;
              }

              // b_off depends on B's STORAGE layout, not the GEMM name:
              //   NN & TN both store B as [K,N] → identical chunk-major smem →
              //     identical b_off (SWIZZLE_W × SWIZZLE_W form).
              //   NT stores B as [N,K] → different (k2 term is bare).
              // Validated 2026-07-02: TN 128×256 passes with the SW×SW form;
              // NN must match (same B layout). The legacy SW*(BN/CLUSTER) form
              // only equalled SW×SW at BN=128 by coincidence, giving garbage at
              // BN=256 — that was a bad over-split; corrected here.
              if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
                b_off = k1 * SWIZZLE_W * (BN / CLUSTER_SIZE) * 2 +
                        k2 * MMA_K_STEP * 2;
              } else if constexpr (Config::B_SW64) {
                // 32-elem B slice in sw64 chunks (§42 B3): one K-row advances
                // 64 bytes (the sw64 chunk pitch — same form as the validated
                // swap-AB sw64 A operand).
                b_off = (k1 * SWIZZLE_W + k2 * MMA_K_STEP) * 64;
              } else { // NN and TN — B stored [K,N]
                b_off = k1 * SWIZZLE_W * SWIZZLE_W * 2 +
                        k2 * MMA_K_STEP * SWIZZLE_W * 2;
              }

              // Descriptor LBO/SBO is chosen PER-OPERAND by that operand's
              // storage layout, not by the whole GEMM layout:
              //   A is stored [K,M] (chunk-major, needs LBO) only when trans_a
              //     -> TN. NN/NT keep A as [M,K] (1-arg, LBO=0).
              //   B is stored [K,N] (chunk-major, needs LBO) when trans_b
              //     -> NN and TN. NT keeps B as [N,K] (1-arg, LBO=0).
              // The LBO (=BK*SWIZZLE_W*2) only matters once the operand spans
              // more than one 64-col swizzle chunk (BM=128 or BN/2=128 at
              // BN=256). At BN=128, B is a single chunk so LBO is unused and
              // the 1-arg form coincidentally worked -- which is exactly why
              // NN 128x128 passed but NN 128x256 produced garbage.
              if constexpr (SWAP_AB) {
                // C' = C^T (1x2_plan.md R7d): MMA-A' = the B smem slot
                // (192-wide, M' side, composite 128+64 atoms; 2nd atom = rows
                // 128-191 = swizzle chunk 2 -> +2*LBO = +16384), MMA-B' = the
                // A smem slot (BM-wide, N' side). Both K-major TN descriptors.
                // d-tmem: M128 atom at col wave_stage*BM (2 stages, cols
                // [0,2*BM)); M64 atom in the SHARED col region [2*BM,3*BM)
                // with lane alignment 16*wave_stage (Layout F interleave,
                // plan Q5). One commit tracks both MMAs.
                const uint64_t ap_desc = make_smem_desc(
                    B_smem + b_off, BK * SWIZZLE_W * 2, 8 * SWIZZLE_W * 2);
                const uint64_t ap_desc2 =
                    make_smem_desc(B_smem + b_off + 16384, BK * SWIZZLE_W * 2,
                                   8 * SWIZZLE_W * 2);
                // B' (the BM-wide operand): 64B-swizzled when BM%64!=0 —
                // per-K-row pitch 64B, LBO=4096, SBO=512 (R7d); else the
                // validated 128B form (pitch 128B == a_off).
                const int bp_off =
                    A_SW64 ? ((k1 * SWIZZLE_W + k2 * MMA_K_STEP) * 64) : a_off;
                const uint64_t bp_desc =
                    A_SW64 ? make_smem_desc_sw64(A_smem + bp_off, BK * 32 * 2,
                                                 8 * 32 * 2)
                           : make_smem_desc(A_smem + bp_off, BK * SWIZZLE_W * 2,
                                            8 * SWIZZLE_W * 2);
                constexpr uint32_t idesc_m128 =
                    sm103_make_i_desc_swap<Config, 128>();
                constexpr uint32_t idesc_m64 =
                    sm103_make_i_desc_swap<Config, 64>();
                tcgen05_mma_bf16<CLUSTER_SIZE>(tmem_addr + wave_stage * BM,
                                               ap_desc, bp_desc, idesc_m128,
                                               use_accum);
                tcgen05_mma_bf16<CLUSTER_SIZE>(
                    tmem_addr + 2 * BM + ((16 * wave_stage) << 16), ap_desc2,
                    bp_desc, idesc_m64, use_accum);
              } else {
                uint64_t b_desc;
                if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
                  b_desc = make_smem_desc(B_smem + b_off);
                } else if constexpr (Config::B_SW64) {
                  // sw64 B descriptor (§41 R8): LBO=BK*64=4096, SBO=8*64=512.
                  b_desc = make_smem_desc_sw64(B_smem + b_off, BK * 32 * 2,
                                               8 * 32 * 2);
                } else {
                  // NN and TN: B stored [K,N], needs LBO=BK*SWIZZLE_W*2.
                  b_desc = make_smem_desc(B_smem + b_off, BK * SWIZZLE_W * 2,
                                          8 * SWIZZLE_W * 2);
                }
                // Composite-M (B1, §42): one M256 atom per piece per K-step.
                // Piece p = this CTA's rows [p*128, p*128+128): its A operand
                // sits +p*16384 B into the SAME smem stage (TN: chunk 2p ->
                // 2p*LBO(8192); NN/NT: 16 8-row atoms -> 16*SBO(1024) — same
                // constant, different derivation, both additive with a_off;
                // §41 R3.7). d-tmem: disjoint BN-col region per piece. Shared
                // b_desc; the ONE commit below tracks all pieces (ptx 35698).
                // N_M256==1 for all pre-B1 configs -> loop degenerates.
#pragma unroll
                for (int p = 0; p < Config::N_M256; ++p) {
                  uint64_t a_desc;
                  if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::TN) {
                    a_desc =
                        make_smem_desc(A_smem + a_off + p * 16384,
                                       BK * SWIZZLE_W * 2, 8 * SWIZZLE_W * 2);
                  } else {
                    a_desc = make_smem_desc(A_smem + a_off + p * 16384);
                  }
                  tcgen05_mma_bf16<CLUSTER_SIZE>(
                      tmem_addr + wave_stage * Config::ACC_COLS_PER_STAGE +
                          p * BN,
                      a_desc, b_desc, i_desc, use_accum);
                }
                // Tail M=128 atom (B2, §42): covers this CTA's last 64 rows
                // (per-CTA M/2 of the 128-instruction). A operand = the next
                // chunk after the M256 pieces (+N_M256*16384, same constant
                // progression: TN chunk 2p; NN/NT 8-row atoms — §41 R3.7);
                // b_desc SHARED; accumulator = Layout B (per-CTA BN/2 cols at
                // lane alignment 0, §41 R10) in its own col region; idesc
                // M-field = 128 (per-atom, R12). Same commit tracks it.
                if constexpr (Config::HAS_M128) {
                  constexpr uint32_t i_desc_m128 =
                      sm103_make_i_desc<Config, Layout, 128>();
                  uint64_t a_desc_t;
                  if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::TN) {
                    a_desc_t =
                        make_smem_desc(A_smem + a_off + Config::N_M256 * 16384,
                                       BK * SWIZZLE_W * 2, 8 * SWIZZLE_W * 2);
                  } else {
                    a_desc_t =
                        make_smem_desc(A_smem + a_off + Config::N_M256 * 16384);
                  }
                  tcgen05_mma_bf16<CLUSTER_SIZE>(
                      tmem_addr + wave_stage * Config::ACC_COLS_PER_STAGE +
                          Config::N_M256 * BN,
                      a_desc_t, b_desc, i_desc_m128, use_accum);
                }
              }
            }
          }

          tcgen05_commit_multicast<CLUSTER_SIZE>(empty_mbar_addr + stage * 8,
                                                 operand_empty_mask);

          stage = (stage + 1) % LOAD_PIPE_DEPTH;
          phase ^= (stage == 0);
        }

        tcgen05_commit_multicast<CLUSTER_SIZE>(tmem_full_addr + wave_stage * 8,
                                               pair_mask);
        wave_iter++;
      }

      mbarrier_wait(clc_full_mbar_addr + clc_stage * 8, clc_full_phase);
      uint32_t is_valid, new_ctaid;
      clc_query_response(clc_response_addr + clc_stage * 16, is_valid,
                         new_ctaid);
      mbarrier_arrive_cluster(cta0_clc_empty_addr + clc_stage * 8);
      clc_stage = (clc_stage + 1) % CLC_PIPE_DEPTH;
      if (clc_stage == 0)
        clc_full_phase ^= 1;

      if (!is_valid)
        break;
    }
  }
  // ── scheduler warp (identical for all layouts and configs) ───────────────
  // PROTOCOL: exactly ONE clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel outstanding at any
  // time (CUTLASS sm100 scheduler, sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:689-721
  // — issue→consume strictly 1:1). We previously armed CLC_PIPE_DEPTH (2)
  // up-front and kept 2 in flight; the two in-flight cancels can execute out
  // of order at END-OF-GRID: the LATER one steals the last cluster (valid)
  // while the EARLIER returns invalid. Consuming stages in order hits the
  // invalid first → every warp breaks → the stolen cluster's response is
  // orphaned and its tile NEVER computed → zero-filled C tiles. Seen as flaky
  // LM-head failures (19k-tile grids: thousands of steals still landing right
  // at exhaustion; small grids orphan only invalid responses = harmless).
  // With one outstanding, an invalid response ⇒ nothing else in flight ⇒ the
  // plain `break` in every warp role stays safe. §30.12.
  else if (warp_id == SCHEDULER_WARP && elect_sync()) {
    if (cta_rank == 0) {
      // Arm ONLY stage 0. try_cancel uses multicast::cluster::all → the
      // response broadcasts to EVERY CTA of the cluster, each completing its
      // own clc_full, so expect_tx=16 is armed on all CLUSTER_CTAS CTAs.
      mbarrier_arrive_expect_cluster(clc_full_mbar_addr, 16);
      for (int r = 1; r < cluster_ctas; ++r) { // GRANTED size (mapa outside
        int remote_full = map_smem_addr_to_cta_rank(clc_full_mbar_addr, r);
        mbarrier_arrive_expect_cluster(remote_full, 16); // granted cluster=UB)
      }
      clc_try_cancel(clc_response_addr, clc_full_mbar_addr);
    }

    int clc_stage = 0, clc_full_phase = 0, clc_empty_phase = 0;
    // Next arm slot index; slot = arm_idx % CLC_PIPE_DEPTH (equals clc_stage
    // after the consume below — kept separate for clarity). Slots
    // 1..CLC_PIPE_DEPTH-1 get armed for the FIRST time inside the loop, so
    // their clc_empty has never completed — skip the empty wait for those.
    int arm_idx = 1;

    while (true) {
      mbarrier_wait(clc_full_mbar_addr + clc_stage * 8, clc_full_phase);
      uint32_t is_valid, new_ctaid;
      clc_query_response(clc_response_addr + clc_stage * 16, is_valid,
                         new_ctaid);
      mbarrier_arrive_cluster(cta0_clc_empty_addr + clc_stage * 8);

      clc_stage = (clc_stage + 1) % CLC_PIPE_DEPTH;
      if (clc_stage == 0)
        clc_full_phase ^= 1;

      if (!is_valid)
        break; // one-outstanding ⇒ no orphaned steal possible

      if (cta_rank == 0) {
        const int s2 = arm_idx % CLC_PIPE_DEPTH;
        if (arm_idx >= CLC_PIPE_DEPTH) {
          // Slot reuse: wait until ALL warps of ALL CTAs have consumed the
          // response this slot held CLC_PIPE_DEPTH responses ago.
          mbarrier_wait(clc_empty_mbar_addr + s2 * 8, clc_empty_phase);
          if (s2 == CLC_PIPE_DEPTH - 1)
            clc_empty_phase ^= 1;
        }
        mbarrier_arrive_expect_cluster(clc_full_mbar_addr + s2 * 8, 16);
        for (int r = 1; r < cluster_ctas; ++r) { // GRANTED size
          int remote_full =
              map_smem_addr_to_cta_rank(clc_full_mbar_addr + s2 * 8, r);
          mbarrier_arrive_expect_cluster(remote_full, 16);
        }
        clc_try_cancel(clc_response_addr + s2 * 16,
                       clc_full_mbar_addr + s2 * 8);
        ++arm_idx;
      }
    }
  }
  // ── epilogue warps: SWAP_AB transposed path ──────────────────────────────
  // TMEM holds C' = C^T: M128 atom lanes = C-cols n_local 0..127 (cols = C-row
  // m, [wave*BM,+BM)); M64 atom = C-cols 128..191 in Layout-F strips (shared
  // col region [2*BM,3*BM), lane alignment 16*wave_stage). Warp w owns
  // n_local 32w..32w+31 (M128) + strip 128+16w..128+16w+15 (M64). Writes are
  // TRANSPOSED into the store buffer [BM m-rows x STORE_COLS n-cols]; the C
  // TMA store is unchanged. Scalar smem writes (bring-up; optimize later).
  else if (SWAP_AB && warp_id < NUM_EPI_WARPS) {
    constexpr int EPI_BAR = 7;
    constexpr int EPI_THREADS = NUM_EPI_WARPS * WARP_THREADS;
    constexpr int num_chunks = BN / STORE_COLS; // 3 chunks of 64 C-cols

    int n_cluster, row_tile;
    decode_mn_tile<VerticalWave>(mn_tile, grid_n, grid_m, n_cluster, row_tile);
    int block_row = row_tile * CLUSTER_SIZE + (int)cta_m;
    int block_col = n_cluster * CLUSTER_N + (int)cta_n;
    int cur_batch = batch;

    int wave_iter = 0;
    int clc_stage = 0, clc_full_phase = 0;

    while (true) {
      const int wave_stage = wave_iter % EPI_PIPE_DEPTH;
      const int wave_phase = (wave_iter / EPI_PIPE_DEPTH) & 1;

      mbarrier_wait(tmem_full_addr + wave_stage * 8, wave_phase);
      tcgen05_fence_after();

      const int t_m128 =
          tmem_addr + wave_stage * BM + ((warp_id * WARP_THREADS) << 16);
      const int t_m64 = tmem_addr + 2 * BM +
                        ((warp_id * WARP_THREADS + 16 * wave_stage) << 16);
      const int n128 = warp_id * WARP_THREADS + lane_id; // my M128 C-col
      int store_stage = 0;

      for (int chunk = 0; chunk < num_chunks; ++chunk) {
        if (warp_id == 0)
          tma_store_wait<STORE_PIPE_DEPTH - 1>();
        barrier_sync(EPI_BAR, EPI_THREADS); // buffer free for all writers

        const int n_base = chunk * STORE_COLS;
        __nv_bfloat16 *buf = store_base + store_stage * BM * STORE_COLS;

        if (n_base < 128) {
          // M128-atom chunks (C-cols 0..127): VECTORIZED transposed store via
          // 16dp256b loads + stmatrix.x4.trans (swap-epilogue vectorization;
          // DeepGEMM sm100_store_cd_swap_ab.cuh). Our 64-col chunk ==
          // DeepGEMM's 64-col swizzle atom (2 warps/chunk). Each active warp:
          // two 16x256b loads (DP-lanes 32w..+15 and +16..+31) -> 8 fp32/thread
          // -> pack -> one stmatrix.x4.trans per 8 m-rows lands buf[m][n]
          // transposed with the 128B swizzle folded into the dst address.
          // Bit-exact vs the old scalar path (P6/RUN_1X2C worst-element dump
          // gates it). BM % 8 == 0.
          if (n128 >= n_base && n128 < n_base + STORE_COLS) {
            const int pm = 2 * (lane_id & 3);                 // 0,2,4,6
            const int qn = lane_id >> 2;                      // 0..7
            const int base_n = block_col * BN + 32 * warp_id; // warp C-col base
            const int col_g = (warp_id & 1) * 4 + (lane_id >> 3);
            for (int m0 = 0; m0 < BM; m0 += 8) {
              float v[8];
              tcgen05_ld_16x256b(v, t_m128 + m0); // DP 0..15
              tcgen05_ld_16x256b(v + 4,
                                 (t_m128 + m0) | 0x00100000); // DP 16..31
              tcgen05_wait_ld();
              const long long row0 =
                  (long long)(cur_batch * M + block_row * BM + m0);
#pragma unroll
              for (int k = 0; k < 8; ++k) {
                const int dm = pm + (k & 1);
                const int dn = qn + 8 * (k >> 1);
                float x = v[k] * alpha;
                if (beta != 0.0f)
                  x += beta *
                       __bfloat162float(C_in[(row0 + dm) * N + (base_n + dn)]);
                v[k] = x;
              }
              const int row_m = m0 + (lane_id & 7);
              uint8_t *dst = reinterpret_cast<uint8_t *>(buf) + row_m * 128 +
                             ((col_g ^ (row_m & 7)) * 16);
              stmatrix_x4_trans((uint32_t)__cvta_generic_to_shared(dst),
                                pack2bf16(v[0], v[1]), pack2bf16(v[2], v[3]),
                                pack2bf16(v[4], v[5]), pack2bf16(v[6], v[7]));
            }
          }
        } else {
          // M64-atom chunk (C-cols 128..191): every warp reads its strip via
          // 16x256b.x1 (4 regs: (t/4, 2c),(t/4,2c+1),(t/4+8,2c),(t/4+8,2c+1)).
          const int n0 = 128 + 16 * warp_id + (lane_id / 4); // strip row A
          const int n1 = n0 + 8;                             // strip row B
          const int mc = 2 * (lane_id % 4);                  // col pair
          for (int m0 = 0; m0 < BM; m0 += 8) {
            float tmp[4];
            tcgen05_ld_16x256b(tmp, t_m64 + m0);
            tcgen05_wait_ld();
#pragma unroll
            for (int j = 0; j < 4; ++j) {
              const int n_loc = (j < 2) ? n0 : n1;
              const int m = m0 + mc + (j & 1);
              float v = tmp[j] * alpha;
              if (beta != 0.0f) {
                const long long cr =
                    (long long)(cur_batch * M + block_row * BM + m) * N +
                    (block_col * BN + n_loc);
                v += beta * __bfloat162float(C_in[cr]);
              }
              {
                const int off = n_loc - n_base; // swizzled write (see above)
                const int soff = ((((off >> 3) ^ (m & 7)) << 3) | (off & 7));
                buf[m * STORE_COLS + soff] = __float2bfloat16(v);
              }
            }
          }
        }

        // Signal tmem free after the LAST chunk's reads are done.
        if (chunk == num_chunks - 1) {
          tcgen05_fence_before();
          if (elect_sync())
            mbarrier_arrive_cluster(tmem_empty_addr + wave_stage * 8);
        }

        __syncwarp();
        tma_store_fence();
        barrier_sync(EPI_BAR, EPI_THREADS);

        if (warp_id == 0 && elect_sync()) {
          const int src = store_smem + store_stage * store_buf_sz;
          const int c_col = block_col * BN + chunk * STORE_COLS;
          const int c_row = cur_batch * M + block_row * BM;
          tma_2d_smem2gmem(src, &C_tmap, c_col, c_row);
          tma_store_commit();
        }
        store_stage ^= 1;
      }

      wave_iter++;

      mbarrier_wait(clc_full_mbar_addr + clc_stage * 8, clc_full_phase);
      uint32_t is_valid, new_ctaid;
      clc_query_response(clc_response_addr + clc_stage * 16, is_valid,
                         new_ctaid);
      if (elect_sync())
        mbarrier_arrive_cluster(cta0_clc_empty_addr + clc_stage * 8);
      clc_stage = (clc_stage + 1) % CLC_PIPE_DEPTH;
      if (clc_stage == 0)
        clc_full_phase ^= 1;

      if (!is_valid)
        break;

      const int new_tile_idx = (int)(new_ctaid / CLUSTER_CTAS);
      cur_batch = new_tile_idx / total_mn_tiles;
      const int new_mn = new_tile_idx % total_mn_tiles;
      int row_tile2, n_cluster2;
      decode_mn_tile<VerticalWave>(new_mn, grid_n, grid_m, n_cluster2,
                                   row_tile2);
      block_row = row_tile2 * CLUSTER_SIZE + (int)cta_m;
      block_col =
          n_cluster2 * CLUSTER_N + (int)(((new_ctaid % (uint32_t)CLUSTER_CTAS) /
                                          (uint32_t)CLUSTER_SIZE) +
                                         cta_n_grant);
    }

    if (warp_id == 0)
      tma_store_wait<0>();
    barrier_sync(EPI_BAR, EPI_THREADS);
  }
  // ── epilogue warps (identical for all layouts and configs) ───────────────
  // Reads TMEM → scales by alpha/beta → writes to smem → TMA stores to C.
  else if (warp_id < NUM_EPI_WARPS) {
    constexpr int EPI_BAR = 7;
    constexpr int EPI_THREADS = NUM_EPI_WARPS * WARP_THREADS;
    constexpr int num_chunks = BN / STORE_COLS;
    constexpr int LOADS_PER =
        STORE_COLS / 8; // 8 = tcgen05_ld loads 8 floats per call

    int n_cluster, row_tile;
    decode_mn_tile<VerticalWave>(mn_tile, grid_n, grid_m, n_cluster, row_tile);
    int block_row = row_tile * CLUSTER_SIZE + (int)cta_m;
    int block_col = n_cluster * CLUSTER_N + (int)cta_n;
    int cur_batch = batch;

    int wave_iter = 0;
    int clc_stage = 0, clc_full_phase = 0;

    while (true) {
      const int wave_stage = wave_iter % EPI_PIPE_DEPTH;
      const int wave_phase = (wave_iter / EPI_PIPE_DEPTH) & 1;

      mbarrier_wait(tmem_full_addr + wave_stage * 8, wave_phase);
      tcgen05_fence_after();

      // TMEM is 128 DP (datapaths/lanes) × 512 col, PER CTA and LOCAL. A
      // cta_group::2 MMA splits total M=2*BM cleanly: CTA0 → rows [0,BM) in
      // CTA0's TMEM DP [0,BM); CTA1 → rows [BM,2*BM) in CTA1's OWN TMEM DP
      // [0,BM). So each CTA reads its own accumulator at DP base 0 — there is
      // NO cross-CTA lane offset (a CTA cannot address the peer's TMEM via a DP
      // index; only 128 DP exist). Verified vs CUTLASS tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp
      // /mma_traits_sm100.hpp + DeepGEMM sm100_store_cd.cuh (2026-07-03,
      // §28.7). NOTE: a prior `cta_rank*BM<<16` term was spurious — at BM=128
      // it lands on DP 128 (out of the 7-bit DP range) and is silently ignored,
      // so it only *accidentally* worked; at BM<128 it corrupts the read.
      // Removed. (The tcgen05.ld auto-distributes 32 DP per warp; the warp term
      // is a no-op the hardware ignores but is kept to match the validated
      // form.)
      const int row = warp_id * WARP_THREADS + lane_id;
      int store_stage = 0;

      // Composite-M (B1/B2, §42): piece p = per-CTA C rows [p*128, ..): M256
      // pieces are 128 rows (validated Layout-D read); the optional LAST
      // piece is the M=128 Layout-B tail (64 rows, quadrant warp map).
      // Accumulator col base = wave_stage*ACC_COLS + p*BN (matches the
      // consumer). N_M256==1/!HAS_M128 pre-B1 -> identical codegen to before.
      for (int p = 0; p < Config::NUM_PIECES; ++p) {
        if (Config::HAS_M128 && p == Config::N_M256) {
          // ── Layout-B tail piece (M=128 atom ::2 -> per-CTA 64 rows) ──────
          // Map (§41 R10): C(row m, col n) sits at TMEM (lane m, col n) for
          // n < BN/2, (lane m+64, col n-BN/2) for n >= BN/2. Quadrant warps:
          // warp w -> rows 32*(w&1)..+32 of C-cols (w>>1)*64..+64, so every
          // warp reads the SAME BN/2 tmem cols at its own 32-lane strip, and
          // each 64-col store chunk is produced by warp pair (w>>1)==chunk.
          const int t_tail =
              (tmem_addr + wave_stage * Config::ACC_COLS_PER_STAGE +
               Config::N_M256 * BN) +
              ((warp_id * WARP_THREADS) << 16);
          const int piece_row = Config::N_M256 * 128;
          const int r_in = 32 * (warp_id & 1) + lane_id; // piece-local C row
          // Quadrant col split (§42 B2/B3): warp pair (w>>1) owns TAIL_COLS
          // = BN/2 C-cols. BN=128: pairs == the two 64-col store chunks.
          // BN=64: pairs == the two 32-col HALVES of the single store chunk.
          constexpr int TAIL_COLS = BN / 2;
          constexpr int TAIL_LOADS = TAIL_COLS / 8;
          const int col_base = (warp_id >> 1) * TAIL_COLS; // in-piece C col
          const int my_chunk = col_base / STORE_COLS;
          const int col_in = col_base % STORE_COLS; // offset inside the chunk

          for (int chunk = 0; chunk < num_chunks; ++chunk) {
            if (warp_id == 0)
              tma_store_wait<STORE_PIPE_DEPTH - 1>();

            float tmp[TAIL_LOADS][8];
            if (my_chunk == chunk) {
#pragma unroll
              for (int n = 0; n < TAIL_LOADS; ++n)
                tcgen05_ld(tmp[n], t_tail + n * 8);
              tcgen05_wait_ld();
            }

            // Tail is always the LAST piece: signal tmem free on its last
            // chunk (warps whose chunk came earlier finished their reads
            // then; the fence orders all of this warp's reads).
            if (chunk == num_chunks - 1) {
              tcgen05_fence_before();
              const int tmem_empty_leader =
                  (cta_m == 0)
                      ? (tmem_empty_addr + wave_stage * 8)
                      : map_smem_addr_to_cta_rank(
                            tmem_empty_addr + wave_stage * 8, pair_leader);
              if (elect_sync())
                mbarrier_arrive_cluster(tmem_empty_leader);
            }

            barrier_sync(EPI_BAR, EPI_THREADS);

            // Masked tiles (§45): rows >= TAIL_ROWS of the tail piece are
            // dead (computed but never stored); the store box is TAIL_ROWS
            // tall so the buffer's dead rows are never read either.
            // TAIL_ROWS==64 unmasked -> predicate is compile-time true.
            if (my_chunk == chunk && r_in < Config::TAIL_ROWS) {
#pragma unroll
              for (int n = 0; n < TAIL_LOADS; ++n) {
                __nv_bfloat162 packed[4];
                if (beta != 0.0f) {
                  const int c_col = block_col * BN + col_base + n * 8;
                  const int c_row = cur_batch * M +
                                    block_row * Config::OUT_ROWS + piece_row +
                                    r_in;
                  const __nv_bfloat16 *cp = C_in + (long long)c_row * N + c_col;
#pragma unroll
                  for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
                    __nv_bfloat162 old =
                        *reinterpret_cast<const __nv_bfloat162 *>(cp + i * 2);
                    float2 old_f = __bfloat1622float2(old);
                    float v0 = tmp[n][i * 2] * alpha + old_f.x * beta;
                    float v1 = tmp[n][i * 2 + 1] * alpha + old_f.y * beta;
                    packed[i] = __float22bfloat162_rn({v0, v1});
                  }
                } else if (alpha == 1.0f) {
#pragma unroll
                  for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i)
                    packed[i] = __float22bfloat162_rn(
                        {tmp[n][i * 2], tmp[n][i * 2 + 1]});
                } else {
#pragma unroll
                  for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
                    packed[i] = __float22bfloat162_rn(
                        {tmp[n][i * 2] * alpha, tmp[n][i * 2 + 1] * alpha});
                  }
                }
                // 16B-group index within the store-buffer row includes the
                // warp pair's in-chunk column base (0 for BN=128; 0/4 for
                // BN=64's two 32-col halves).
                const int g = col_in / 8 + n;
                const int swizzled_g = g ^ (r_in & 7);
                __nv_bfloat16 *wp =
                    store_base + store_stage * Config::EPI_ROWS * STORE_COLS +
                    r_in * STORE_COLS + swizzled_g * 8;
                *reinterpret_cast<int4 *>(wp) =
                    *reinterpret_cast<int4 *>(packed);
              }
            }

            __syncwarp();
            tma_store_fence();
            barrier_sync(EPI_BAR, EPI_THREADS);

            if (warp_id == 0 && elect_sync()) {
              const int src = store_smem + store_stage * store_buf_sz;
              const int c_col = block_col * BN + chunk * STORE_COLS;
              const int c_row =
                  cur_batch * M + block_row * Config::OUT_ROWS + piece_row;
              // 64-row box (C_tmap_tail) — a 128-row box would overwrite the
              // NEXT tile's rows (TMA clips only at the tensor edge).
              tma_2d_smem2gmem(src, &C_tmap_tail, c_col, c_row);
              tma_store_commit();
            }
            store_stage ^= 1;
          }
          continue; // next piece (tail is last — loop ends)
        }
        const int tmem_row =
            (tmem_addr + wave_stage * Config::ACC_COLS_PER_STAGE + p * BN) +
            ((warp_id * WARP_THREADS) << 16);
        const int piece_row = p * 128; // C-row base of this piece in the tile

        for (int chunk = 0; chunk < num_chunks; ++chunk) {
          if (warp_id == 0)
            tma_store_wait<STORE_PIPE_DEPTH - 1>();

          float tmp[LOADS_PER][8];
#pragma unroll
          for (int n = 0; n < LOADS_PER; ++n)
            tcgen05_ld(tmp[n], tmem_row + chunk * STORE_COLS + n * 8);
          tcgen05_wait_ld();

          // The LAST piece signals tmem free — the Layout-B tail when present
          // (its branch above), else the last M256 piece here.
          if (!Config::HAS_M128 && p == Config::N_M256 - 1 &&
              chunk == num_chunks - 1) {
            tcgen05_fence_before();
            // Signal THIS pair's leader tmem_empty (rank0 for pair0, rank2 for
            // pair1). Odd partner reaches the leader via mapa; even leader uses
            // its local addr. (Was a bit-24 clear that always hit rank0 — wrong
            // for pair1 in a 2×2 cluster.)
            const int tmem_empty_leader =
                (cta_m == 0)
                    ? (tmem_empty_addr + wave_stage * 8)
                    : map_smem_addr_to_cta_rank(
                          tmem_empty_addr + wave_stage * 8, pair_leader);
            if (elect_sync())
              mbarrier_arrive_cluster(tmem_empty_leader);
          }

          barrier_sync(EPI_BAR, EPI_THREADS);

#pragma unroll
          for (int n = 0; n < LOADS_PER; ++n) {
            __nv_bfloat162 packed[4];

            if (beta != 0.0f) {
              const int c_col = block_col * BN + chunk * STORE_COLS + n * 8;
              const int c_row = cur_batch * M + block_row * Config::OUT_ROWS +
                                piece_row + row;
              const __nv_bfloat16 *cp = C_in + (long long)c_row * N + c_col;
#pragma unroll
              for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
                __nv_bfloat162 old =
                    *reinterpret_cast<const __nv_bfloat162 *>(cp + i * 2);
                float2 old_f = __bfloat1622float2(old);
                float v0 = tmp[n][i * 2] * alpha + old_f.x * beta;
                float v1 = tmp[n][i * 2 + 1] * alpha + old_f.y * beta;
                packed[i] = __float22bfloat162_rn({v0, v1});
              }
            } else if (alpha == 1.0f) {
              // alpha==1 (every inference GEMM): skip the wasted *1.0 FMULs
              // (SASS showed 128-256 of them per tile), convert directly.
#pragma unroll
              for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i)
                packed[i] =
                    __float22bfloat162_rn({tmp[n][i * 2], tmp[n][i * 2 + 1]});
            } else {
#pragma unroll
              for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
                packed[i] = __float22bfloat162_rn(
                    {tmp[n][i * 2] * alpha, tmp[n][i * 2 + 1] * alpha});
              }
            }

            // Swizzle n within the store-smem row to avoid bank conflicts
            const int swizzled_n = n ^ (row & 7);
            __nv_bfloat16 *wp = store_base +
                                store_stage * Config::EPI_ROWS * STORE_COLS +
                                row * STORE_COLS + swizzled_n * 8;
            *reinterpret_cast<int4 *>(wp) = *reinterpret_cast<int4 *>(packed);
          }

          __syncwarp();
          tma_store_fence();
          barrier_sync(EPI_BAR, EPI_THREADS);

          if (warp_id == 0 && elect_sync()) {
            const int src = store_smem + store_stage * store_buf_sz;
            const int c_col = block_col * BN + chunk * STORE_COLS;
            const int c_row =
                cur_batch * M + block_row * Config::OUT_ROWS + piece_row;
            tma_2d_smem2gmem(src, &C_tmap, c_col, c_row);
            tma_store_commit();
          }

          store_stage ^= 1;
        }
      } // piece loop (B1)

      wave_iter++;

      mbarrier_wait(clc_full_mbar_addr + clc_stage * 8, clc_full_phase);
      uint32_t is_valid, new_ctaid;
      clc_query_response(clc_response_addr + clc_stage * 16, is_valid,
                         new_ctaid);
      if (elect_sync())
        mbarrier_arrive_cluster(cta0_clc_empty_addr + clc_stage * 8);
      clc_stage = (clc_stage + 1) % CLC_PIPE_DEPTH;
      if (clc_stage == 0)
        clc_full_phase ^= 1;

      if (!is_valid)
        break;

      const int new_tile_idx = (int)(new_ctaid / CLUSTER_CTAS);
      cur_batch = new_tile_idx / total_mn_tiles;
      const int new_mn = new_tile_idx % total_mn_tiles;
      int row_tile, n_cluster;
      decode_mn_tile<VerticalWave>(new_mn, grid_n, grid_m, n_cluster, row_tile);
      block_row = row_tile * CLUSTER_SIZE + (int)cta_m;
      // n_sub per STOLEN tile (requester-sized pieces, §31.3) — see producer.
      block_col =
          n_cluster * CLUSTER_N + (int)(((new_ctaid % (uint32_t)CLUSTER_CTAS) /
                                         (uint32_t)CLUSTER_SIZE) +
                                        cta_n_grant);
    }

    if (warp_id == 0)
      tma_store_wait<0>();
    barrier_sync(EPI_BAR, EPI_THREADS);
  }

  cluster_sync();
  if (warp_id == 0)
    dealloc_tmem<CLUSTER_SIZE>(tmem_addr, Config::TMEM_COLS);
}

// ─── unified launcher
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Template args:
//   Config  — an Sm103ClusterConfig<BM, BN, BK, ...> instantiation
//   Layout  — Sm103Layout::NN / NT / TN
//
// Replaces the three separate launch_bgemm_{nn,nt,tn}_cluster functions.

template <typename Config, Sm103Layout Layout, bool VerticalWave = false,
          bool MulticastA = false, bool DynamicCluster = false>
static void launch_bgemm_sm103_cluster(const __nv_bfloat16 *A,
                                       const __nv_bfloat16 *B, __nv_bfloat16 *C,
                                       int M, int N, int K, int batchCount,
                                       float alpha, float beta,
                                       cudaStream_t stream) {
  // This cta_group::2 kernel only supports BM=128 (total MMA M=256), the clean
  // non-interleaved 128-DP accumulator layout the epilogue reads. BM=64
  // (total M=128) is a LEGAL cta_group::2 shape but uses a 2x2 INTERLEAVED TMEM
  // layout (half-N in DP[0,64), half in DP[64,128)) that this epilogue does not
  // de-interleave — it silently miscomputes. Smaller row-tiles must use a
  // cta_group::1 (M=64) variant. See analyzations.md §28.7.
  static_assert(Config::BM == 128 || (Config::SWAP_AB && Config::BM == 160) ||
                    (Config::CLUSTER_SIZE == 2 && !Config::SWAP_AB &&
                     ((Config::BM == 256 && Config::EPI_PIPE_DEPTH == 1) ||
                      Config::BM == 192 || Config::BM == 64)),
                "BM=128 (cta_group::2 epilogue, §28.7), swap-AB 160x192 "
                "(1x2_plan.md R7), composite BM=256 with EPI_PIPE_DEPTH=1 "
                "(§41 R11 / §42 B1), composite BM=192 = M256+M128 Layout-B "
                "tail (§42 B2), or pure-Layout-B BM=64 (§42 B3).");
  static int s_arch_ok = -1;
  if (s_arch_ok < 0) {
    int dev;
    cudaGetDevice(&dev);
    cudaDeviceProp prop;
    cudaGetDeviceProperties(&prop, dev);
    s_arch_ok = (prop.major == 10 && prop.minor >= 3) ? 1 : 0;
    if (!s_arch_ok)
      fprintf(stderr,
              "[BluBridge SM103] WARNING: device '%s' SM %d.%d, requires SM "
              "10.3+\n",
              prop.name, prop.major, prop.minor);
  }
  if (!s_arch_ok)
    return;

  constexpr int BM = Config::BM;
  constexpr int BN = Config::BN;
  constexpr int BK = Config::BK;
  constexpr int CLUSTER_SIZE = Config::CLUSTER_SIZE;
  constexpr int CLUSTER_N = Config::CLUSTER_N;
  constexpr int CLUSTER_CTAS = Config::CLUSTER_CTAS;
  constexpr int STORE_COLS = Config::STORE_COLS;

  // ── alignment preconditions (LOUD, never silent) ─────────────────────────
  // Our chunk-factorized 4D tmaps encode the sliced dim as {chunk, ., X/chunk}
  // — integer division TRUNCATES a non-multiple tail, and TMA then zero-fills
  // reads past it: the kernel would return silently-wrong zeros in the tail
  // rows/cols (found via the M=200 B2 test, §33.2). Reject loudly instead.
  // All 42 Qwen shapes satisfy these. Proper arbitrary-M support = true-extent
  // tmaps (DeepGEMM runtime_utils.hpp:199 style) or a fallback kernel route
  // (cuBLAS ships cutlass_75_wmma align1 for exactly this) — documented TODO.
  {
    constexpr int A_CHUNK = (Config::SWAP_AB && (Config::BM % 64 != 0)) ? 32
                            : (Config::MASK_M > 0)                      ? 8
                                                                        : 64;
    // MASK_M>0 TN uses the ELEMENT-granular A tmap (§45) with true M extent —
    // no chunk truncation; only 16B-aligned rows required (M%8).
    constexpr int B_CHUNK = Config::B_SW64 ? 32 : 64;
    bool aligned = true;
    if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::TN)
      aligned = (M % A_CHUNK == 0) && (N % B_CHUNK == 0);
    else if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT)
      aligned = (K % 64 == 0);
    else // NN
      aligned = (K % 64 == 0) && (N % B_CHUNK == 0);
    if (!aligned) {
      fprintf(stderr,
              "[BluBridge SM103 Cluster] UNSUPPORTED alignment for this "
              "kernel (chunked-tmap sliced dims must be chunk multiples; "
              "TN: M%%%d && N%%64, NN: K%%64 && N%%64, NT: K%%64). "
              "M=%d N=%d K=%d — refusing to compute silently-wrong output.\n",
              A_CHUNK, M, N, K);
      return;
    }
  }

  // Build TMA descriptors — layout-specific A and B initialisation
  CUtensorMap A_tmap, B_tmap, C_tmap;

  if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::TN) {
    // A[batch, K, M]  batch stride = K * M. The swap-AB 160-wide slice needs
    // the 64B-swizzle tmap (R7a); masked tiles need the ELEMENT-granular map
    // (§45 — tile stride OUT_ROWS is not a whole-chunk multiple); everything
    // else keeps the validated chunk-factorized 128B map.
    if constexpr (Config::MASK_M > 0)
      init_4d_tma_A_KM_elem(&A_tmap, A, M, K, BK, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                            (uint64_t)K * M);
    else if constexpr (Config::SWAP_AB && (Config::BM % 64 != 0))
      init_4d_tma_A_KM_sw64(&A_tmap, A, M, K, BM, BK, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                            (uint64_t)K * M);
    else
      init_4d_tma_A_KM(&A_tmap, A, M, K, BM, BK, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                       (uint64_t)K * M, CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B);
    // B[batch, K, N]  batch stride = K * N. 32-elem per-CTA slices (BN=64)
    // take the sw64 B map (§42 B3).
    if constexpr (Config::B_SW64)
      init_4d_tma_B_KN_sw64(&B_tmap, B, K, N, BK, BN, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                            (uint64_t)K * N, CLUSTER_SIZE);
    else
      init_4d_tma_B_KN(&B_tmap, B, K, N, BK, BN, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                       (uint64_t)K * N, CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B,
                       CLUSTER_SIZE);
  } else if constexpr (Layout == Sm103Layout::NT) {
    // A[batch, M, K]  batch stride = M * K
    init_4d_tma_A_MK(&A_tmap, A, M, K, BM, BK, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                     (uint64_t)M * K, CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B);
    // B[batch, N, K]  batch stride = N * K  (stored transposed)
    init_4d_tma_B_NK(&B_tmap, B, N, K, BN, BK, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                     (uint64_t)N * K, CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B, CLUSTER_SIZE);
  } else { // NN
    // A[batch, M, K]  batch stride = M * K
    init_4d_tma_A_MK(&A_tmap, A, M, K, BM, BK, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                     (uint64_t)M * K, CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B);
    // B[batch, K, N]  batch stride = K * N (sw64 for 32-elem slices, §42 B3)
    if constexpr (Config::B_SW64)
      init_4d_tma_B_KN_sw64(&B_tmap, B, K, N, BK, BN, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                            (uint64_t)K * N, CLUSTER_SIZE);
    else
      init_4d_tma_B_KN(&B_tmap, B, K, N, BK, BN, (uint64_t)batchCount,
                       (uint64_t)K * N, CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B,
                       CLUSTER_SIZE);
  }

  // C store box is one composite piece tall (EPI_ROWS == BM for all pre-B1
  // configs; 128 for BM=256 — the epilogue stores per piece, §42 edit 4).
  init_2d_tma_C(&C_tmap, C, (uint64_t)batchCount * M, (uint64_t)N,
                (uint32_t)Config::EPI_ROWS, (uint32_t)STORE_COLS,
                CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B);
  // Tail store box (B2): the Layout-B piece is 64 rows — storing it with the
  // 128-row box would overwrite the next tile's rows (TMA clips only at the
  // tensor edge). Plain copy when unused.
  CUtensorMap C_tmap_tail = C_tmap;
  if constexpr (Config::HAS_M128)
    init_2d_tma_C(&C_tmap_tail, C, (uint64_t)batchCount * M, (uint64_t)N,
                  (uint32_t)Config::TAIL_ROWS, (uint32_t)STORE_COLS,
                  CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B);

  // Ceil-div so shapes smaller than one cluster tile still launch (grid>=1).
  // TMA OOB-fill + clipped 2D store handle partial tiles. Floor-div gave
  // grid=0 → "invalid argument" for shapes < one tile. Ported from fixed
  // _cluster.cu (2026-07-02).
  // Tiles advance by OUT_ROWS (== BM unmasked; 160 for the masked tile whose
  // MMA computes 192 rows but stores only 160 — §45).
  const int grid_m = (M + CLUSTER_SIZE * Config::OUT_ROWS - 1) /
                     (CLUSTER_SIZE * Config::OUT_ROWS);
  const int grid_n_blocks = (N + BN - 1) / BN; // total BN-blocks along N
  // Each cluster owns CLUSTER_N adjacent N-blocks → count N-CLUSTERS. grid_n
  // (passed to the kernel) is the N-cluster count; decode_mn_tile enumerates
  // clusters and cta_n picks the block within. For CLUSTER_N=1 this ==
  // N-blocks.
  const int grid_n = (grid_n_blocks + CLUSTER_N - 1) / CLUSTER_N;
  const int total_mn_tiles = grid_m * grid_n;

  auto kernel = bgemm_sm103_cluster_kernel<Config, Layout, VerticalWave,
                                           MulticastA, DynamicCluster>;
  cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize,
                       Config::SMEM_BYTES);

  // Cluster dims via LAUNCH ATTRIBUTES (one kernel serves rigid AND dynamic
  // launches; CUTLASS cluster_launch.hpp pattern, §31.1). Grid is sized in
  // PREFERRED-cluster units (CLUSTER_CTAS) — required divisibility for the
  // preferred-cluster launch, and the unit of the CTA-level tile decode.
  dim3 grid(total_mn_tiles * batchCount * CLUSTER_CTAS);

  cudaLaunchConfig_t cfg = {};
  cfg.gridDim = grid;
  cfg.blockDim = dim3(Config::NUM_THREADS);
  cfg.dynamicSmemBytes = Config::SMEM_BYTES;
  cfg.stream = stream;
  cudaLaunchAttribute attrs[2] = {};
  attrs[0].id = cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension;
  cfg.attrs = attrs;
  cfg.numAttrs = 1;
  if constexpr (DynamicCluster) {
#if CUDART_VERSION >= 12080
    // "2x2f": fallback = one MMA pair; preferred = the full CLUSTER_CTAS
    // cluster. HW grants per cluster; kernel adapts via %cluster_nctaid.
    attrs[0].val.clusterDim.x = (unsigned)Config::CLUSTER_SIZE; // fallback
    attrs[0].val.clusterDim.y = 1;
    attrs[0].val.clusterDim.z = 1;
    attrs[1].id = cudaLaunchAttributePreferredClusterDimension;
    attrs[1].val.preferredClusterDim.x = (unsigned)Config::CLUSTER_CTAS;
    attrs[1].val.preferredClusterDim.y = 1;
    attrs[1].val.preferredClusterDim.z = 1;
    cfg.numAttrs = 2;
#else
    fprintf(stderr, "[BluBridge SM103 Cluster] DynamicCluster requires "
                    "CUDA >= 12.8 (preferred-cluster launch)\n");
    return;
#endif
  } else {
    attrs[0].val.clusterDim.x = (unsigned)Config::CLUSTER_CTAS;
    attrs[0].val.clusterDim.y = 1;
    attrs[0].val.clusterDim.z = 1;
  }

  cudaError_t lerr =
      cudaLaunchKernelEx(&cfg, kernel, A, C, C, M, N, K, total_mn_tiles, alpha,
                         beta, A_tmap, B_tmap, C_tmap, C_tmap_tail, grid_n);
  if (lerr != cudaSuccess)
    fprintf(stderr, "[BluBridge SM103 Cluster] LaunchEx error: %s\n",
            cudaGetErrorString(lerr));

  cudaError_t err = cudaGetLastError();
  if (err != cudaSuccess)
    fprintf(stderr, "[BluBridge SM103 Cluster] Launch error: %s\n",
            cudaGetErrorString(err));
}

### CLAUDE [2026-07-08 12:52 IST]

Good question bro — important to get this right since it's a shared GPU. Let me be precise:

## What `-lgc 1400` does
`nvidia-smi -lgc 1400` **locks the graphics clock to 1400 MHz** — it's:
- **GPU-wide, not per-process.** It affects the *whole GPU*, so **yes — your colleagues' kernels running on this same GPU will also be locked to 1400 MHz** while it's set.
- **Persistent until you reset it** (or reboot / driver reload) — NOT just for this one run. It stays locked across all runs, yours and theirs.
- It's **not temperature** — it's the clock *frequency*. We lock it so our benchmark numbers are reproducible (constant clock = apple-to-apple; otherwise boost clocks drift and inflate whoever measures first, the bias we fought last time).

## So to be a good shared-server citizen
- For a **correctness run** (`RUN_1X2C`), you **don't even need the clock lock** — correctness doesn't care about clock speed. You could skip `-lgc` entirely for the bit-exact gate.
- The lock only matters for the **perf measurement** step (later, after correctness passes).
- **When you're done, reset it** so your colleagues get normal boost clocks back:

```bash
nvidia-smi -rgc      # reset graphics clock to default (undoes the -lgc lock)
```

If you want to be extra considerate, only lock right before the ncu/perf run and reset right after.

---

So "just add one cvt instruction on load" isn't quite available to us — the convert would need warps to read fp32 smem → cvt → write bf16 smem, an extra manual stage that breaks the pure-async TMA→MMA pipeline. Plus fp32 operands double smem per stage → halve our pipeline depth. That's the real cost, beyond the double DRAM bytes you already spotted.

**Three alternatives being verified:**
1. **Fuse the cast into the PREVIOUS op** (the prior layernorm/gelu writes bf16 directly) — kills 2 trips without touching the GEMM at all; suspect this is what torch.compile/Transformer Engine actually do

## Findings: Transformer Engine precision-cast handling around GEMMs

**1. Claim A — Dedicated fused cast+transpose kernels: CONFIRMED.**
URL: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/tree/main/transformer_engine/common/transpose
The directory contains `cast_transpose.cu`, `cast_transpose.h`, `cast_transpose_fusion.cu`, `multi_cast_transpose.cu`, plus newer block-scaled variants `quantize_transpose_square_blockwise.cu`, `quantize_transpose_vector_blockwise.cu`, and `quantize_transpose_vector_blockwise_fp4.cu` — standalone CUDA kernels that produce quantized data and its transpose in one pass. The C API exposes `nvte_cast_transpose()` (listed in the Common API docs at https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/transformer-engine/user-guide/api/common.html).

**2. Claim B — Casts fused into normalization and activation kernels: CONFIRMED.**
Normalization: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/transformer_engine/common/normalization/common.h — the forward kernel parameter struct contains `bool fp8_out` plus `void* scale`, `void* scale_inv`, and `void* amax` fields, i.e., the LayerNorm/RMSNorm forward kernels (under `normalization/layernorm/` and `normalization/rmsnorm/`) write quantized FP8 output directly with scaling metadata.
Activation: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/transformer_engine/common/activation/activation_template.h — the activation templates (`gelu.cu`, `swiglu.cu`, `relu.cu`, etc.) dispatch through `dispatch::quantize_fwd_helper&lt;...&gt;(input, output, ...)` / `quantize_bwd_helper&lt;...&gt;`, so activation output quantization is fused into the same kernel launch.

**3. Claim C — FP8 casts are managed operations driven by amax history + scaling factors (delayed scaling): CONFIRMED.**
URL: https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/transformer-engine-releases/release-1.7/user-guide/examples/fp8_primer.html (FP8 primer). Verbatim: "The FP8 operator uses scaling factor obtained using the history of amaxes (maximums of absolute values) seen in some number of previous iterations and produces both the FP8 output and the current amax, which gets stored in the history," and the motivation: the FP8 dynamic range "is not sufficient for all of them at the same time" — hence per-tensor scaling. The recipe machinery is in the C API (`nvte_compute_amax()`, `nvte_compute_scale_from_amax()`, `nvte_delayed_scaling_recipe_amax_and_scale_update()`, https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/transformer-engine/user-guide/api/common.html). This is exactly why the cast is a distinct, stateful, managed operation rather than an ad-hoc load-time convert: each cast must read a scale computed from cross-iteration amax state and write back a new amax.

**4. Claim D — TE never fuses the input cast into the GEMM kernel itself: CONFIRMED (no exceptions found).**
- C++ wrapper: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/transformer_engine/common/gemm/cublaslt_gemm.cu — `CanonicalizeGemmInput` only validates and forwards pre-quantized pointers; asserts include "FP8 input to GEMM requires inverse of scale!" and "FP4 input to GEMM requires inverse of scale!". There is no casting/quantization logic in the GEMM path; it passes `A.data.dptr` + `A.scale_inv.dptr` (or MXFP8 rowwise/columnwise data) straight to cuBLASLt.
- Python wrapper: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/transformer_engine/pytorch/cpp_extensions/gemm.py — `general_gemm` ("GEMM supporting fp8 inputs") unwraps already-quantized tensor objects via `A.get_tensor(...)`/`B.get_tensor(...)` and delegates to `tex.generic_gemm`; the `quantization_params: Optional[Quantizer]` argument governs the *output*, not input casting.
- Blackwell exception check: per the MXFP8 feature docs (https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/transformer-engine/user-guide/features/low_precision_training/mxfp8/mxfp8.html), Blackwell Tensor Cores require MXFP8 data "consecutive over the reduction dimension," so TE quantizes both a regular and a transposed copy from the original high-precision input before the GEMM (to avoid double-quantization error) — i.e., even for MXFP8/NVFP4 block scaling, the cast still happens in producer kernels (the `quantize_transpose_*` files in finding 1), never inside the GEMM. Caveat: whatever cuBLASLt does internally (e.g., converting FP8 inputs up to the tensor-core compute type, or epilogue output conversion) is inside NVIDIA's closed kernels, but from TE's side the operands handed to cuBLASLt are always already quantized. VERDICT on "expected answer NO": Confirmed — casts always occur in producer/dedicated kernels.

**5. Claim E — Higher-precision master params + per-minibatch FP8 weight caching via `is_first_microbatch`: CONFIRMED.**
URL: https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/transformer-engine-releases/release-1.7/user-guide/examples/advanced_optimizations.html ("FP8 weight caching" section). Verbatim: "If our training iteration is split into multiple gradient accumulation steps, each micro-batch will encounter the same weight tensors. **TE never fuses the input cast into the GEMM.** Verified from their source: their GEMM wrapper (`cublaslt_gemm.cu`) only accepts *already-converted* operands — no cast logic in the GEMM path at all. Instead, TE solves your 3-trip problem exactly the way I suspected — **they fuse the cast into the PRODUCER op**:

- LayerNorm/RMSNorm kernels write the low-precision output **directly** (cast fused into the norm kernel)
- Activation kernels (gelu, swiglu…) same — quantize fused into the activation launch
- Plus dedicated fused `cast_transpose` kernels when both are needed in one pass
- And for weights: cast **once per iteration** and cached (`is_first_microbatch` flag), not per-GEMM — master weights stay fp32/bf16

So the tensor arrives in VRAM *already bf16* — the prior op writes 2 bytes instead of 4, the GEMM reads 2 bytes. That's **fewer total bytes than the fused-fp32-input-GEMM idea** (which still writes 4 + reads 4), which is why NVIDIA structures it this way even though they control the GEMM kernels.

## A. Autocast inserts casts as separate ops (eager) — CONFIRMED

- **URL:** https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/autocast_mode.cpp (verified against raw file at `main`)
- Autocast's C++ dispatch wrapper routes every eligible arg through `cached_cast`, whose actual cast is a plain dispatch of `aten::to`: on cache miss it executes `auto casted_arg = arg.to(to_type);` and on the non-cacheable path `return arg.to(to_type);`. In eager mode `Tensor.to(dtype)` dispatches `_to_copy` → an elementwise copy/conversion kernel, i.e. its own CUDA kernel launch, not something fused into the matmul (eager launches one kernel per aten op; autocast adds these `to` ops in front of the matmul).
- Docs framing: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/amp.html — "ops run in an op-specific dtype chosen by autocast to improve performance while maintaining accuracy" (the dtype change is realized by casting inputs). The "separate kernel + extra DRAM round trip for activations" reading is correct for eager: activations are fp32-written by the producer, then re-read/re-written by the cast kernel.

## B. Autocast cast cache — CONFIRMED

- **URLs:** https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/autocast_mode.cpp ; https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/amp.html
- Cache declaration comment (autocast_mode.cpp): "Imitate Apex and cache some of the casts to streamline parameter reuse. Our heuristic is to cache lower_precision_fp casts of fp32 model weights (see cached_cast below)." Map: `ska::flat_hash_map&lt;TensorImpl*, val_type&gt;&amp; get_cached_casts()` with `val_type = std::tuple&lt;weakref_type, Tensor&gt;`.
- **Exact caching condition** (verbatim from `cached_cast`):
```cpp
bool can_try_cache = (to_type == get_lower_precision_fp_from_device_type(device_type) &amp;&amp;
                     arg.scalar_type() == at::kFloat &amp;&amp; arg.requires_grad() &amp;&amp;
                     arg.is_leaf() &amp;&amp; !arg.is_view() &amp;&amp; cache_enabled &amp;&amp;
                     !at::caching::is_cached_tensor(arg) &amp;&amp;
                     !c10::InferenceMode::is_enabled());
```
So: only fp32 → lower-precision-fp casts of **leaf tensors with requires_grad=True that are not views** (i.e., model weights) are cached; plain activations are re-cast every time.
- **When cleared:** source comment — "When the autocast context manager exits to a nesting level that's outside any instance of autocast (which should occur at the end of each forward pass) it calls clear_cache() to ensure cached Tensors don't leak outside the autocasting region." (So per-iteration: cache lives only within one outermost autocast region.)
- **`cache_enabled` docs** (torch.autocast arg): "Whether the weight cache inside autocast should be enabled. Default: `True`." Docs also state: "autocast should wrap only the forward pass(es) of your network... Backward passes under autocast are not recommended" (backward runs in the dtypes forward used; the cache is a forward-region construct).
- Related caveat: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/86136 — "torch.clear_autocast_cache() doesn't actually clear every cache" (per-device caches nuance).

## C. torch.compile/Inductor fuses casts into producer pointwise ops — CONFIRMED

- **URL (source):** https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/_inductor/lowering.py — `to_dtype` (line ~959 at main) is implemented as `return make_pointwise(_to_dtype, override_return_dtype=dtype)(x)`, i.e. a dtype conversion is just another pointwise node in Inductor IR, so it participates in ordinary pointwise fusion — the producer op writes bf16 directly and the standalone cast kernel disappears from the schedule.
- **URL (design doc):** https://dev-discuss.pytorch.org/t/torchinductor-a-pytorch-native-compiler-with-define-by-run-ir-and-symbolic-shapes/747 — jansel: "Pointwise ops can be fused with: other pointwise ops; reduction ops; and matmul/conv templates." (dtype cast = pointwise per lowering.py, so it's covered by this rule.)

## D. "Prologue fusion" is a real, named Inductor feature — CONFIRMED

- **Main PR:** https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/134532 ("Prologue Fusion", eellison, merged Dec 12, 2024 after a Dec 11 revert). Description: "fusing pointwise nodes into triton templates - prologue fusion" — extends epilogue fusion to fuse pointwise ops (dtype casts/dequant, gathers — "gather into matmul is particularly useful in MOE") into the **load side of Triton matmul templates**, so the GEMM template converts on load. Author notes it is "generally much less profitable than epilogue fusion" (applies per loop iteration) and is conservative: only fuses if it doesn't increase bytes read beyond a small factor.
- **Follow-up PRs (eellison):** #142401 (zero-mask preservation analysis for prologue loads before `tl.dot`), #142402 (infer prologues computable without fp32 upcast — i.e., do the cast in low precision when numerics allow), #142435 (don't fuse unaligned accesses into mm), #145103, #145104.
- **Config (verified in `torch/_inductor/config.py` at main, fetched today):**
```python
# fuse pointwise into template prologues
prologue_fusion = prologue_fusion_enabled()
```
where `prologue_fusion_enabled()` returns `True` in OSS (env override `TORCHINDUCTOR_PROLOGUE_FUSION`, fbcode killswitch via justknobs). So the *flag* is on by default — but it only has effect when a **Triton template** is chosen, which requires max-autotune-style GEMM autotuning (`max_autotune = os.environ.get("TORCHINDUCTOR_MAX_AUTOTUNE") == "1"` — default False; `max_autotune_gemm_backends = "ATEN,TRITON,CPP"`).
- **Release-note confirmation:** https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/releases/tag/v2.8.0 — "Inductor config variables `use_mixed_mm` and `mixed_mm_choice` are deprecated (#152071). Inductor now supports prologue fusion, so there is no need for special cases now." (mixed_mm was exactly the old special-case "fuse the weight dtype-cast into mm" path; prologue fusion generalizes it.)

## E. cuBLAS/aten.mm fallback cannot absorb the cast — CONFIRMED (by composition of primary sources)

- Prologue fusion fuses "pointwise nodes into **triton templates**" only (PR #134532); with default compile options Inductor emits matmul as an extern ATen/cuBLAS call, not a Triton template — jansel (dev-discuss #747): "The two exceptions are matmul/conv where it has a template... In the current numbers these are disabled by config, and we are just using aten." Triton GEMM templates are selected via autotuning (`max_autotune`/`max_autotune_gemm_backends`, config.py). An extern cuBLAS kernel is opaque to the scheduler, so the fp32→bf16 cast cannot be fused into the GEMM itself; it either remains a standalone Triton kernel or gets fused into the producing pointwise/reduction op per C. Corroborating: even when ATEN wins autotuning under max-autotune, fusion is lost — see https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/142315 ("Better fusion on triton templates") and the mixed_mm deprecation note above (a special case existed precisely because default mm couldn't fuse the cast).

**Net for the GEMM engineer's claim:** correct for eager autocast on activations (separate cast kernel per use, extra DRAM round trip), softened for weights (cast cache, one cast per weight per autocast region/iteration — condition: fp32 + requires_grad + leaf + non-view + cache_enabled), and largely eliminated under torch.compile: producer-fusion always, in-GEMM conversion only with max-autotune Triton templates via prologue fusion (default-on flag since ~2.5-dev/merged Dec 2024, generalized by 2.8), never with the cuBLAS extern path.

## Your 3-trip analysis: CONFIRMED for eager autocast

Inductor's **"prologue fusion"** (PR #134532, merged Dec 2024, default-on since ~2.8) fuses the dtype cast **into the load side of the matmul template** — exactly your "convert inside the GEMM on load" idea. BUT:

- The author's own note: prologue fusion is **"generally much less profitable than epilogue fusion"** — because the conversion cost applies *per loop iteration* (the GEMM re-reads operand tiles many times, each read is now double-width)

And the default torch.compile behavior is the **producer fusion** (same as Transformer Engine): the cast becomes a pointwise node fused into the *previous* op, which just writes bf16 directly — cast kernel disappears, GEMM stays pure bf16.

> "Allows the library to use Tensor Cores with automatic down-conversion and **bfloat16 compute for 32-bit input and output matrices**."

That's literally it: **fp32 A/B/C in VRAM, bf16 tensor-core compute, ONE call, no separate cast kernel.** Invoked via `cublasGemmEx`/`cublasLtMatmul` with Atype/Btype/Ctype = `CUDA_R_32F` + that compute type. It's **opt-in only** — default cuBLAS never silently downconverts fp32.

PyTorch even exposes it: `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("medium")` = fp32 matmuls internally computed in bf16.

## Even better for our B300 specifically: BF16x9 emulation
`CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_EMULATED_16BFX9` — supported on **cc 10.0 and 10.3 ONLY** (10.3 = our B300, CUDA 12.9+):
- Splits each fp32 into **3 exact bf16 pieces** (a = a0 + 2⁻⁸a1 + 2⁻¹⁶a2), does 9 bf16 tensor-core products
- NVIDIA blog: **3–4× faster than native fp32** matmul on Blackwell, with accuracy **"equivalent or superior to native FP32"**
- So on our exact GPU there's a mode that keeps *fp32-level accuracy* while running on the same bf16 tensor cores we're optimizing

## One honest gap
Whether cuBLAS fuses the downconvert **inside** the GEMM kernel vs a hidden pre-pass is **undocumented** — circumstantial evidence says fused (no workspace documented for FAST_* modes), but nobody's proven it. We could actually *answer this ourselves* with ncu on B300 later (count kernels launched under FAST_16BF — one kernel = fused). That'd be a genuine reverse-engineering finding.

### CLAUDE [2026-07-09 10:07 IST]

Fourth report in bro — **master weights pattern**, verified from Megatron-LM + DeepSpeed source:

## Weights are NOT the problem — only activations are
- **Megatron-LM**: optimizer keeps **fp32 master params**, steps on those, then copies fp32→bf16 back into the model weights **once per optimizer step** — not per GEMM
- **DeepSpeed BF16_Optimizer**: same — fp32 flat master partition, `update_lp_params()` refreshes the bf16 working copy once per step
- **PyTorch autocast**: even in eager mode, weight casts are **cached** within the autocast region (`cache_enabled=True` default)
- This design goes back to the original mixed-precision paper (Micikevicius et al., NVIDIA/Baidu 2017): keep an fp32 master copy, work in half precision

**What this means for your idea:** the fp32→bf16 conversion overhead you're targeting is **per-GEMM only for the ACTIVATION operand** (the X in X·W). The weight matrix arrives already-bf16 in every serious training stack. So a fused fp32-input GEMM would only want **mixed inputs**: A = fp32 activations (convert in-kernel), B = bf16 weights (load as-is) — not both fp32. That halves the extra-bandwidth cost of the idea, but also halves its benefit (only one operand's trips saved).

## Updated picture
- weights: cast amortized per-step → **zero recurring cost** (solved everywhere)
- activations: the real recurring cast → industry answer = **fuse into producer op** (TE, torch.compile); your answer = fuse into GEMM load (shipped as inductor prologue fusion + cuBLAS FAST_16BF, both with caveats)

### CLAUDE [2026-07-09 10:07 IST]

Fifth report bro — **TF32**, and it settles the hardware question for our kernel:

## TF32 = the hardware's "accept fp32 directly" path, but at HALF rate
- TF32 rounding happens **inside the tensor-core datapath** — fp32 in memory, no cast kernel, fp32 accumulate. Cleanest version of "no conversion trips."
- **BUT: 2:1 penalty everywhere** — verified on Ampere (312 vs 156 TFLOPS) through Blackwell (BF16 36 / TF32 18 PFLOPS on both HGX B200 *and* HGX B300). TF32 runs at **half of bf16 throughput** on every published NVIDIA spec.
- Precision bonus though: TF32 keeps **10 mantissa bits vs bf16's 7** — *more* accurate than bf16, same fp32 range.

## The key constraint for OUR kernel (verified from PTX ISA 9.3)
`tcgen05.mma` kinds are exhaustive: **f16 (fp16/bf16 inputs), tf32, f8f6f4, i8, mx-formats. There is NO fp32-operand kind at bf16 rate.** So the hardware gives you exactly two choices:
1. bf16-rate compute → operands **must already be bf16 in smem** (someone must convert before the MMA reads)
2. fp32 operands directly → `kind::tf32` → **half rate**

No free lunch instruction exists. A fused fp32-input bf16-rate kernel means *we* do the cvt with regular warps between TMA and MMA.

## Small corrections to what we said earlier (honesty log)
- bf16 = **7 stored mantissa bits** (8 only counting the implicit bit)
- TF32 is **NOT default in cuBLAS** — opt-in (`CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32`); it's only default inside NGC containers, and PyTorch's `allow_tf32` defaults **False** since 1.12

**VERDICT: Cast fused into GEMM mainloop — fp32 operands in gmem, in-kernel fp32→bf16 conversion by dedicated transform warps. This is the exact architecture in question, shipping in CUTLASS for SM100.**

## 3. CUTLASS tf32: the "accept fp32 directly" answer — zero conversion stage

**VERDICT: tf32 direct-fp32. ElementA/B = float is accepted by the standard mainloops with NO cast kernel and NO transform warps; the type is merely relabeled tf32 for the TMA descriptor and the MMA runs kind::tf32.**

## 5. DeepGEMM: no fp32→bf16 downconvert; but has in-kernel UPcast + tf32-direct kernel

**VERDICT: bf16/fp8/fp4 kernels take same-type inputs only. One notable kernel does in-mainloop conversion the other direction.**

- No fp32-input variant of the bf16 kernels exists (`impls/` listing: `sm100_bf16_gemm.cuh`, `sm90_bf16_gemm.cuh`, fp8/fp4 kernels).

**VERDICT: Separate cast kernel (`aten::to`), NOT fused; the 3-DRAM-trip cost is paid, but fp32 *leaf weights* are cast once per step and cached.**
